ARC01.blurb:
Archery opens with ranking rounds for women's compound and men's recurve. This session is listed as not ticketed, so it is one for the schedule rather than the shopping cart.

Each archer shoots a full set of arrows for a score that decides seeding in the head-to-head brackets. Compound's qualification round is new to the Games program, feeding the debut compound mixed team event.

Top seeding matters because it brings softer early matchups. Carson Stadium hosts archery July 19-28, and organizers note the schedule is subject to change.

potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 individual bronze medalist who traded the lead with Kim in Shanghai 2025 qualifying. A likely threat for the top seed if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Andres Temino
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion in men's individual recurve, so a projected contender for a high seed if he qualifies.

ARC02.blurb:
Day two of ranking rounds covers men's compound and women's recurve. Like the opening session, it is listed as not ticketed.

The men's compound round seeds the debut compound mixed team event. The women's recurve scores set the seeding for the individual brackets that start at the 1/32 round.

The qualifying scores will be early signals of who arrives in form. Carson Stadium is the archery venue, and the schedule is subject to change.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Barbelin

ARC03.blurb:
Archery's first medal event at the 2028 Games is also a first for the sport: compound mixed team. It runs from the 1/8 round to the gold medal match in one evening.

Compound bows use pulleys, cables, magnifying sights and release aids, and they are more accurate than recurve bows. Expect tight scoring where one arrow outside the 10-ring can swing a match.

India has never won an archery medal at the Games, and Ojas Deotale has said he hopes the first comes from compound. Carson Stadium should be loud for what will be a historic first medal ceremony.

ARC04.blurb:
The recurve individual brackets begin with the 1/32 elimination round for men and women. Seeds from the ranking rounds decide the matchups, with top seeds facing the lowest.

It is a morning of many short matches across the field. Early rounds are a good chance to see a wide mix of nations before the field narrows.

Top seeds can still fall: Kim Woojin exited early in the individual event at Antalya 2025. Carson Stadium's soccer-style bowl keeps spectators close to the shooting line.

ARC05.blurb:
This evening session carries the individual recurve brackets through the 1/32 and 1/16 rounds. It is a good chance to see the first elimination rounds at Carson Stadium after dark.

Paths to medals narrow with each round, and a single bad end can end a campaign. Match play creates quick momentum swings.

The stadium previously hosted the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final. Fans will be seated near the field of play with clear sight lines.

A Sunday morning of men's and women's recurve 1/32 and 1/16 matches. By the end, the field will start to look like a medal bracket.

Korea won all five recurve golds in Paris, and each of its archers in 2028 will carry that expectation. Qualifying from the roster is itself a difficult task.

Kim Woojin has said he wants to leave an unforgettable mark on archery history. Carson Stadium's open-air setting should make for a pleasant day.

Home fans may have an American star to follow in Brady Ellison, who lost the Paris 2024 final to Kim Wu-Jin in a shoot-off. He would compete in a home Games if selected.

French bronze medalist Lisa Barbelin could also appear. The stadium's sight lines keep the action close.

Im Si-hyeon won three golds in Paris, including individual gold over Nam Su-hyeon. Her return to competition in 2025 included some mental rust, a reminder of how fine the margins are.

The women's team medal matches follow the next day. Carson Stadium offers close views of the shooting line.

ARC09.blurb:

Korea has won men's team gold at every Games since Tokyo 2020, and Kim Woojin has won three consecutive team golds. Its core of Kim Je Deok, Kim Woojin and Lee Wooseok won the 2025 world title.

Silver and bronze are also up for grabs, with the USA second at the 2025 Worlds. Expect a lively crowd for these team matches at Carson Stadium.

He has also said he still considers himself young in his career. Carson Stadium sets up an intimate stage for early-round upsets.

That suggests the 2028 field may be wide open. Carson Stadium will be loud for a crowd-pleasing evening.

Mixed team is one of two mixed events at the 2028 Games, alongside debuting compound. Spain's Elia Canales and Andres Temino won the 2025 world title, Spain's first-ever World Championships gold.

It is a quick, fast-paced morning of matches. Carson Stadium keeps fans close to the action.

Expect a loud crowd at Carson Stadium for the final session.

Eight archers per bracket half become four on the last morning of the archery program. The 1/8 elimination round is where the women's individual bracket gets thin, and one cold end can send a top seed home.

Matches are head-to-head, with archers trading arrows over set scoring. Paris 2024 went to Korea's Im Si-Hyeon, with Nam Su-Hyeon silver and France's Lisa Barbelin bronze, so every seeded name here carries weight.

This is a morning session at Carson Stadium, a soccer-specific bowl where the seats sit close to the field. Expect a quieter, focused crowd before the evening medal matches, and a good value look at elite recurve.

ARC17.blurb:
The final archery medal session of the 2028 Games crowns the women's individual recurve champion on Friday night, July 28, two days before the Games close. It runs from quarterfinals through the bronze and gold matches.

The field has been dominated by Korea, which won every archery gold in Paris 2024. Im Si-Hyeon beat teammate Nam Su-Hyeon in an all-Korean final, with France's Lisa Barbelin taking bronze.

Challengers are rising, though. China's Zhu Jingyi took 2025 world silver, and Chinese Taipei and Japan finished ahead of Korea in the 2025 world women's team event. A Korean sweep is far from guaranteed.

Carson Stadium, home of the LA Galaxy and host of the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final, will be set up for a night finale. Expect a big-stadium atmosphere with every seat close to the shooting line.

ATH01.blurb:
Track and field opens at the Coliseum with a packed morning of qualifying. The women's 100m starts here, with the preliminary round and Round 1 both on the card.

The women's 100m will run all four rounds on opening day, a first for the Games. Qualifying also covers the women's shot put and hammer throw, men's pole vault, and first rounds of the women's 5000m and 800m.

The 2025 world 100m champion, Melissa Jefferson-Wooden (USA), ran a championship-record 10.61 in Tokyo. If she is in the field, she will enter at a later round than the prelims, so expect big names in Round 1.

The open-air bowl is still warming up at 9 AM, but a fresh crowd and a dozen events at once make it easy to roam between sightlines.

ATH02.blurb:
Opening night is stacked: the women's 100m semifinals and final share an evening with the women's shot put final and the men's 10,000m final. A medal event is decided here, and the 100m caps the night.

For the first time, the women's 100m final lands on day one. Sprinters will have already raced that morning, so recovery and nerve could shape the outcome.

The 2025 world 100m podium went to Jefferson-Wooden (USA), Tina Clayton (JAM) and Julien Alfred (LCA), but Paris 2024 silver medalist Sha'Carri Richardson was fifth in Tokyo. The shot put is also unsettled after the 2025 world title went to Jessica Schilder (NED).

Expect the Coliseum floodlit and loud as the stadium fills for the first big evening of the Games.

ATH03.blurb:
Day two opens with the first half of the men's decathlon, plus qualifying rounds that will thin the fields before the medal sessions begin. It is an easy-entry morning for fans who like to see a bit of everything.

The decathlon begins with the 100m, long jump and shot put. Men's shot put and long jump qualifying, the women's 800m repechage, and the mixed 4x400m first round fill out the session.

The repechage gives 800m runners who missed automatic advancement a second chance. Mixed 4x400m has history: the US set a world record in the Paris 2024 heats, and the Netherlands took gold in the final.

With the men's 100m final scheduled later on this day, the Coliseum will be filling up early for a long day of track and field.

ATH04.blurb:
Sunday afternoon at the Coliseum packs a men's 100m final, a hammer final, a shot put final and the mixed 4x400m relay final into under four hours. Decathletes also work through the high jump and 400m.

The 100m is the main draw, with semifinals and the final in one session. Noah Lyles won Paris 2024 gold ahead of Kishane Thompson, but Oblique Seville won the 2025 world title with Thompson second and Lyles third.

In the hammer, Camryn Rogers of Canada is the Paris 2024 champion and threw 80.51m to win the 2025 world title. If she competes, she could be chasing records.

The Coliseum hosted the 1932 and 1984 Games, including Carl Lewis's four golds. Its peristyle arch and 77,500-seat bowl should give this card a big-night feel.

ATH05.blurb:
Morning action centers on the women's triple jump final, with decathlon day two and hurdle repechages in the same session. It is a good mix of field drama and track rounds.

The triple jump is wide open. Cuba's Leyanis Pérez Hernández won the 2025 world title with a world-leading 14.94m, ahead of Paris 2024 champion Thea LaFond (DMA) and four-time world champion Yulimar Rojas (VEN).

The 400m hurdles repechages give a second route to the semifinals. Men's 400m Round 1 also includes world champion Busang Collen Kebinatshipi (BOT), if he competes.

Morning Coliseum sun is easier to handle than the afternoon, and the triple jump pit is a good place to watch the crowd clap athletes into their runs.

ATH06.blurb:
The men's pole vault final headlines this late-afternoon session, with Mondo Duplantis bidding to defend his Paris 2024 title. The mixed 4x100m relay also makes its Games debut, with both its first round and final held here.

Duplantis has raised the outdoor world record to 6.30m, and a world-record attempt is plausible whenever he is in form. He is not confirmed for 2028, but he is the projected favorite.

The depth behind him is real. Seven men cleared 5.90m at the 2025 world final, and Emmanouil Karalis (GRE) took silver after a first clearance above 6.00m.

The session also holds women's 800m semifinals, the decathlon javelin and 1500m, and men's 1500m repechage. Late-day sun and a dense schedule give the stadium a loud, busy feel.

ATH07.blurb:
This is a qualifying morning with an accessible feel: women's pole vault qualification, men's triple jump qualification, and first rounds of the women's 400m, men's 110m hurdles and men's 3000m steeplechase.

The pole vault field is tightly clustered. Katie Moon (USA) won the 2025 world title at 4.90m, with Sandi Morris (USA) second and Tina Šutej (SLO) third. Paris 2024 gold went to Nina Kennedy (AUS).

The women's 400m could be an event to watch. Paris 2024 champion Marileidy Paulino (DOM) is a likely contender, and Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone, who skipped the hurdles in 2025 to focus on the flat 400m, would be a possible entry.

Get there early for the vault runway: qualifying is when you can sit close to the action without the final-night crowds.

ATH08.blurb:
A busy evening with real medals on the line: the women's 5000m final, women's 800m final, men's high jump final and men's discus final. The men's 200m opens, and 400m hurdles and 1500m semifinals add intensity.

The women's 5000m could be a Kenyan showdown. Beatrice Chebet, the Paris 2024 champion and 2025 world champion, holds the world record of 13:58.06 and has Faith Kipyegon in her sights.

The 800m is just as tight. Lilian Odira won the 2025 world title, with Georgia Hunter Bell and Paris 2024 champion Keely Hodgkinson only hundredths behind.

The Coliseum bowl should be near full, and field events like the high jump give the infield its own rhythm of clapping and quiet.

ATH09.blurb:
Wednesday's morning card is mostly about second chances, with repechage rounds in the men's 200m and both 400m events. One medal event, the women's 3000m steeplechase final, is the headline.

The steeplechase mixes hurdles and a water jump, so the field often spreads out and tangles at barriers. It is a classic crowd-pleaser for fans who like chaos.

The session also features women's long jump qualifying, where Paris 2024 champion Tara Davis-Woodhall (USA) won the 2025 world title at 7.13m. Men's hammer qualifying rounds out the field events.

Repechage is new to many fans: runners who miss direct advancement get a second shot, so the stakes are high even in an early heat.

Three finals and one hurdles showdown make this a headline evening: women's discus, men's long jump, men's 1500m, and the men's 400m hurdles final.

The 400m hurdles rematch is the main draw. Rai Benjamin (USA) won Paris 2024 and the 2025 world title in 46.52, while Karsten Warholm (NOR) holds the world record of 45.94.

The men's 1500m also has history: Cole Hocker (USA) beat Josh Kerr and Jakob Ingebrigtsen at Paris 2024, then won the 2025 world 5000m. Women's 200m first round and men's 110m hurdles repechage fill out the rest.

The Coliseum evening crowd should be at full volume, and a loud finish on the home straight is hard to beat for atmosphere.

The men's 3000m steeplechase final is the headline here, with qualifying rounds in women's javelin and high jump, first-round men's 800m, and the women's 200m repechage.

Soufiane El Bakkali (MAR), the Paris 2024 steeplechase champion, is the projected leader if he competes. His pace over the barriers and water jump has made him hard to beat.

The men's 800m opens with Paris 2024 champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi (KEN) and Marco Arop (CAN), both likely to appear if selected. Women's high jump qualification could feature Paris 2024 champion Yaroslava Mahuchikh (UKR).

A morning session at the Coliseum is quieter than night finals, but the steeplechase makes for a lively close.

ATH12.blurb:
A deep evening packs three medal finals: women's pole vault, men's hammer throw and women's 400m hurdles. Men's 200m, 400m and 110m hurdles semifinals and women's 400m semifinals fill the track.

Katie Moon (USA) won the 2025 world pole vault title at 4.90m, with Sandi Morris (USA) at 4.85m and Tina Šutej (SLO) at 4.80m. Paris 2024 gold went to Nina Kennedy (AUS).

In the hammer, Ethan Katzberg (CAN) is the Paris 2024 and 2025 world champion, and Merlin Hummel (GER) won the 2026 Ultimate Championship. The 400m hurdles is open: Femke Bol is not expected to return to it.

The semis bring heat-by-heat tension, and Ja'Kobe Tharp, the 12.75 world record holder in the 110m hurdles, could be one to watch.

Friday's morning session opens the women's heptathlon and settles the men's triple jump final. First rounds in the men's 5000m and women's 100m hurdles share the card, with a men's 800m repechage.

The triple jump final could be a tight one. Pedro Pichardo (POR) won the 2025 world title, while Jordan Díaz (ESP) took Paris 2024 gold and Andy Díaz (ITA) bronze.

The 5000m opening round might feature Jakob Ingebrigtsen (NOR) and Cole Hocker (USA), who finished one-two at the 2026 Ultimate Championship. Anna Hall (USA), the 2025 world heptathlon champion, could begin her campaign in the hurdles and high jump.

Heptathlon morning sessions are a slow-burn: you can watch the multi-event athletes pushing through high jump while a medal final plays out.

The men's 200m features Noah Lyles (USA), the 2025 world champion in 19.52, and Kenny Bednarek (USA), the 2026 Ultimate Championship winner. Paris 2024 gold went to Letsile Tebogo (BOT).

The hurdles might be the quickest sprint event on the card. Ja'Kobe Tharp (USA) set a 12.75 world record in June 2026, and Cordell Tinch (USA) won the 2025 world title.

In the 10,000m, Beatrice Chebet (KEN) is the Paris 2024 and 2025 champion. Expect a loud finale in the home straight.

Saturday afternoon is a finals marathon: women's 200m, women's 400m, men's 400m and women's long jump, plus the end of the heptathlon with the 800m. Men's 800m semifinals also run.

Melissa Jefferson-Wooden (USA) swept the 100m and 200m at the 2025 World Championships and won the 2026 Ultimate Championship 200m in 21.47. Gabby Thomas (USA) is the Paris 2024 200m champion.

The 400m finals are filled with headline names. Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone ran 47.78 in the 2025 final, and Marileidy Paulino (DOM) was also under 48 seconds. In the men's final, Busang Collen Kebinatshipi (BOT) ran 43.53.

A full Coliseum and four medal finals back to back make this a high-energy session worth planning around.

Sunday brings five finals: women's high jump, women's javelin, men's 800m, women's 1500m and men's 4x100m. Relay first rounds and the women's 100m hurdles semifinal are also on the card.

The men's 800m looks tight. Emmanuel Wanyonyi (KEN) won Paris 2024 and the 2025 world title in 1:41.86, with Djamel Sedjati (ALG) and Marco Arop (CAN) a few hundredths behind.

Faith Kipyegon (KEN) won her fourth world 1500m title in 2025 in 3:52.15. The men's 4x100m is just as open: Canada won Paris 2024, while Noah Lyles was part of the 2025 world relay gold.

A Sunday evening crowd and a relay finale make for a loud send-off, and relay exchanges are always worth watching up close.

ATH17.blurb:
The last stadium session at the Coliseum packs six finals into under two hours: men's javelin, women's 4x100m, men's 5000m, women's 100m hurdles, and both 4x400m relays. It is a closing-night feel, with only the road events still to come.

The relays are the draw. The US women won the 2025 world 4x400m in a championship record 3:16.61, while Botswana beat the US to the 2025 world men's 4x400m title. Both sprint and quarter-mile relays could swing on a single anchor leg.

The men's 5000m is projected to be a tactical chess match. Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Cole Hocker traded blows at the 2026 Ultimate Championship, where Ingebrigtsen edged Hocker by under a second.

The Coliseum is an open-air bowl with no roof, so expect late-afternoon Southern California sun. It will be the first stadium to host track and field at three Summer Games, and the 1932 and 1984 history is part of the atmosphere.

ATH18.blurb:
Two medal races, one morning. The men's and women's half-marathon race walks both reach their finals on Thursday, July 27, with no heats, so every walker on the road is racing for a podium spot.

The 21.1 km distance is new, replacing the 20 km walks as World Athletics shifts to half-marathon and marathon walk distances. The order of the two races within the 7:30 to 11:35 a.m. window had not been announced when the schedule was released.

This is also a farewell to the mixed marathon walk relay, which was held only at Paris 2024 and dropped to make room for a mixed 4x100m relay. Canada's Evan Dunfee called that part of the 'ongoing TikTokification' of the Games.

The course and venue are still listed as TBD, but expect an early-morning road race after the track program at the Coliseum wraps up. Walks reward watching in person: judges, tight packs and late surges all play out in the open.

ATH19.blurb:
The women's marathon opens the final weekend of athletics with a single winner-take-all race. There are no heats and no second chances, just 26.2 miles starting on the sand-side edge of Los Angeles.

Paris 2024 was won by Sifan Hassan in a Games record 2:22:55, after a sprint duel with Tigst Assefa. Assefa has since set women-only world records in London and has said she is targeting gold in 2028.

The start is on the Venice Beach Boardwalk, with palm trees, the Pacific and the boardwalk scene behind the runners. Fans watch from the roadside rather than from stadium seats, and the finish venue is still to be confirmed.

The 7:15 AM start is early, which suits distance runners and Saturday-morning spectators alike.

ATH20.blurb:
The men's marathon is the last athletics event of the 2028 Games. It is a single-race final, so the track and field program ends on the roads rather than in the stadium.

The form book is moving fast. Kenya's Sabastian Sawe ran 1:59:30 in London in 2026, the first sub-two-hour marathon in a record-eligible race. Paris 2024 champion Tamirat Tola ran 2:03:10 in Beijing that October.

Racing begins at the Venice Beach Boardwalk, with the Pacific and the beach scene as the backdrop. Spectators line the roadside rather than sit in a stadium, and the finish venue is still to be confirmed.

A 7:15 AM Sunday start means a morning crowd on closing weekend. Whether the course favors fast times or tactics will depend on routes organizers have yet to publish.

Badminton opens at the Galen Center with a morning session that touches all five medal events. Group play begins for men's, women's and mixed doubles and for both singles draws.

The field is 172 players, with 16 pairs in each doubles event. The men's singles title will go to a new champion, since two-time winner Viktor Axelsen has retired with chronic back problems.

The arena seats roughly 10,000 in a tight two-deck bowl, so even upper rows sit close to the court. It is the first Games competition ever held at this USC venue, and the Jefferson/USC Metro stop is next door.

Doubles pairs trade fast, flat exchanges while the crowd sits close to the floor. The Galen Center's red-brick exterior, just off Figueroa Street, makes for an easy first-day outing.

Matchups depend on the group phase, which hasn't been played yet. The USA is the reigning champion and the world's top-ranked side, with France and Australia ranked 2nd and 3rd at the start of the 2026 World Cup.

The Dome's 'Wall' section, 51 rows of seats at one end, tends to get loud for primetime games. This 8 PM start should give you that atmosphere.
BKB31.potentialContendersIntro: The field comes out of the group phase, so these are projected contenders based on Paris 2024 results and recent rankings.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and host nation, going for a ninth straight title. Won 5-0 at the March 2026 qualifying tournament.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, who lost the final 67-66. Ranked 2nd in the world at the start of the 2026 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. Went 5-0 at the March 2026 qualifying tournament in Istanbul.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: EuroBasket Women 2025 champions, ranked 5th in the world. A likely quarterfinal side if they qualify.

BKB32.blurb:
The men's quarterfinals start with an early-afternoon game in Inglewood. Win and you're in the final four. Lose and the tournament is over.

The US men are going for a sixth straight gold medal. Erik Spoelstra is the head coach through 2028, but no roster has been announced.

LeBron James has said he will watch rather than play, and Stephen Curry has said he highly doubts he will play. Which teams meet in this game depends on group-phase results.

The 1 PM tip-off puts the game in daylight outside the arena. Inside the Dome you get a modern, bowl-shaped arena built just for basketball.
BKB32.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings aren't set, so these are teams likely to reach the quarterfinals based on Paris 2024 results and recent form.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and Paris 2024 gold medalists, with a roster still to be named. Coached by Erik Spoelstra.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, who lost 98-87 in the final. Victor Wembanyama is projected to lead them.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Went 8-0 in Americas Group F of 2027 World Cup qualifying as of September 2026.

BKB33.blurb:
The quarterfinal has a primetime slot and a chance for a star-driven game. With France projected to be in the field, Victor Wembanyama could be the main draw.

Wembanyama said after the Paris 2024 final that the loss would drive France to go for gold. He scored 26 points in that game, and in 2026 he became France's captain.

At 22, he is the team's youngest captain since Tony Parker in 2003. He plays center and power forward for the San Antonio Spurs.

An 8 PM Monday game at Intuit Dome should be one of the loudest sessions of the week.
BKB33.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings depend on the group phase. These teams are projected contenders, assuming they qualify and advance.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists. Wembanyama is captain, and the team has said it is aiming for gold.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host and Paris 2024 gold medalists. The roster hasn't been announced.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: A likely European contender if they qualify. The team won the 2023 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. Projected to be in the mix if they qualify.

BKB34.blurb:
This afternoon quarterfinal could draw from teams that are still qualifying. Seven places will go through the 2027 World Cup in Qatar, and the rest are decided in mid-2028.

As of September 2026, Canada and Australia were both 8-0 in their 2027 World Cup qualifying groups. The USA was 7-1, and Serbia took bronze at Paris 2024.

Afternoon games here have a different feel from the primetime sessions. It's a good way to see the knockout round without late-night tickets.
BKB34.potentialContendersIntro: The field isn't set. These teams are projected based on qualifying results and Paris 2024 performance.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Automatic host qualifier and Paris 2024 gold medalists. Led Americas Group E at 7-1 as of September 2026.

BKB35.blurb:
The last men's quarterfinal of the round should be a big game for US fans. The host nation is chasing a sixth straight men's gold medal.

Spoelstra will coach the team, but no roster has been named. In 2026, a USA team of non-NBA players won qualifying games over the Dominican Republic (82-81) and Mexico (94-93).

A Tuesday primetime game can set up a semifinal run. Expect a crowd that has come to see knockout basketball on home soil.
BKB35.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings come out of the group phase, which begins July 13. These are projected contenders.

potentialContenders.note: Host and Paris 2024 gold medalists, the defending champions, coached by Erik Spoelstra.

BKB36.blurb:
A place in the women's gold medal game is at stake. This is the first of two women's semifinals at Intuit Dome, three days before the final on July 29.

The US women beat France 67-66 in Paris for an eighth straight title. A Gabby Williams shot from just inside the arc would have tied it, but it counted for two.

The USA and France were ranked 1st and 2nd in the world at the start of the 2026 World Cup. A rematch is possible but not guaranteed.

The 4 PM start should give you a fast, tense game with a lot on the line.
BKB36.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal pairings depend on the bracket. These are projected players, and no 2028 rosters have been announced.

potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 tournament MVP. She missed the 2026 World Cup, but could be a core player if she's selected for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Paige Bueckers

potentialContenders.name: Caitlin Clark

potentialContenders.name: Gabby Williams
potentialContenders.note: Took the last shot in the Paris 2024 final. Could return if France qualifies.

BKB37.blurb:
The second women's semifinal is a late-night game with a gold medal game at stake. Winners go through to July 29 and losers go to the bronze game.

Australia took bronze at Paris 2024, and Belgium won EuroBasket Women 2025. The two were drawn in the same group at the 2026 World Cup, so they have a recent history.

A 9:30 PM tip-off in Inglewood means a long night. The arena's big halo video board should make for a strong atmosphere.

BKB38.blurb:
The first men's semifinal brings the tournament down to four teams. The winner goes on to the July 30 gold medal game.

The US men are chasing a sixth straight gold medal, though the roster looks different from Paris. LeBron James has ruled out playing, and Stephen Curry has said he is unlikely to play.

France captain Victor Wembanyama has said France is aiming for gold after losing the Paris 2024 final.

A 4 PM semifinal in Inglewood is a good option if you want to see top-level basketball in the daytime.

BKB39.blurb:
The second men's semifinal is a primetime game with a gold medal game on the line. Teams that lose play for bronze.

Canada and Australia were both 8-0 in their 2027 World Cup qualifying groups as of September 2026. France and Serbia took silver and bronze in Paris.

The US men are going for a sixth straight title. The matchup depends on how the bracket falls.

A 9:30 PM start under the halo board will probably feel like a big night in Inglewood.

BKB40.blurb:
This is the women's bronze medal game, played between the two semifinal losers. The medal is still worth fighting for, and the day before the final it's an easy game to enjoy.

Australia won bronze at Paris 2024, and France took silver. Belgium, Nigeria, Spain, Italy and host Germany at the 2026 World Cup are possible contenders if they qualify.

A 4 PM game on Friday has a lower-key feel than the final. Expect players who lost in the semifinals to go all out for a medal.
BKB40.potentialContendersIntro: Nobody knows who will play in the bronze game, since it depends on the semifinal losers. These are projected players.

potentialContenders.name: A'ja Wilson

BKB41.blurb:
The men's bronze medal game is played between the two semifinal losers, with a podium finish at stake. It is the day before the gold medal game.

Serbia won bronze at Paris 2024, and France lost to the USA in the final. France could end up here if it loses in the semifinals.

USA Basketball chairperson Gen. Martin Dempsey named Victor Wembanyama as the biggest international threat to the US.

A Saturday noon game at Intuit Dome has a more relaxed feel than the final. Players on both sides will want to leave with a medal.
BKB41.potentialContendersIntro: The field isn't set. Seven places come from the 2027 World Cup and the rest from mid-2028 qualifying, so these are projected players.

BKB42.blurb:
The women's gold medal game is the final of the women's tournament. The USA has won eight straight titles, and a ninth on home soil would extend the record.

The US won Paris 2024 by beating France 67-66. The US also won the 2026 World Cup in Germany, and the winner qualifies directly.

A'ja Wilson was Paris 2024 tournament MVP, but she didn't play at the 2026 World Cup. Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers were on that team.

Head coach Kara Lawson expects 2028 roster selection to be the most competitive yet. The 4 PM game on Saturday at Intuit Dome is the biggest session of the women's tournament.

BKB43.blurb:
The men's gold medal game is the last day of the 2028 Games, hours before the Closing Ceremony. It is the final of the men's tournament.

The US beat France 98-87 at Paris 2024 for a fifth straight title and 17th overall. The US is chasing a sixth straight men's title on home soil.

LeBron James has ruled out playing, and Stephen Curry has said it's highly unlikely he will. Media projections point to younger players like Cooper Flagg and Chet Holmgren, but no roster has been announced.

USA Basketball chairperson Gen. Martin Dempsey named Victor Wembanyama as the top threat. The Sunday afternoon game at Intuit Dome is the biggest basketball ticket of the Games.

BMF01.blurb:
Before anyone chases a medal, 24 riders (12 men, 12 women) have to survive this morning qualification session. It's the first look at BMX Freestyle park in the San Fernando Valley, and a bad run can end a medal bid early.

Paris 2024 showed how quickly that can happen: Tokyo 2020 champion Charlotte Worthington of Great Britain didn't make it out of qualification. Format details for 2028 are expected to match Paris, with judges scoring difficulty, execution and creativity.

The venue is a temporary park at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin, near the 405 and 101 interchange. A 10:30 AM start means an open-air, daytime crowd watching the sport return to its Southern California roots.
BMF01.potentialContendersIntro: The 2028 field isn't set; qualification runs through UCI events and a Q-Series in May and June 2028. Based on 2025 form, these riders are projected contenders if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Anthony Jeanjean
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist, 2025 world champion and 2025 World Cup men's overall winner. A projected men's favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Marcus Christopher

potentialContenders.name: Sun Sibei
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 women's world title with 95.86. Could lead another strong Chinese group in 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Miharu Ozawa

potentialContenders.name: Hannah Roberts
potentialContenders.note: Six-time world champion, but 10th at the 2025 worlds. Her 2028 participation is unconfirmed.

BMF02.blurb:
Two park finals, men's and women's, share one Saturday morning session, and each rider gets two 60-second runs with the better score counting. One clean run can decide a medal, as Paris 2024 showed.

That Paris podium was razor-thin: José Torres Gil took men's gold with 94.82, just ahead of Kieran Reilly and Anthony Jeanjean. On the women's side, Deng Yawen won with 92.60, ahead of Perris Benegas and Natalya Diehm.

Expect a loud, open-air atmosphere at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin, with riders linking huge tricks on a temporary course. Seeing BMX in the Los Angeles area, where the sport has deep roots, adds to the occasion.
BMF02.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected contenders for the men's and women's park finals, based on 2025 results. None of the Paris 2024 medalists had publicly confirmed or ruled out 2028, and qualification is still ahead.

potentialContenders.name: Anthony Jeanjean
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion (94.4 in Riyadh in 2025), 2025 World Cup overall winner and Paris 2024 bronze medalist.

potentialContenders.name: Kieran Reilly
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who landed two world-first triple tailwhip tricks in April 2025. A likely podium threat if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Perris Benegas
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and X Games Salt Lake City 2025 bronze medalist. A potential home-crowd medal hope if she qualifies.

BMX01.blurb:
Saturday morning is where the BMX field gets cut down. Quarterfinals and last chance runs for both men and women decide who earns a place in Sunday's semifinals and finals, and it's a good entry point for fans who like racing at full speed.

Riders go through short, fast heats over jumps and banked turns, so crashes and photo-finish scrambles for the top spots are part of the appeal. The last chance runs give a second shot to those who missed out.

The course is a temporary build in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, set into the natural terrain of the park. Expect full summer sun at the 10:30 AM start. Fans can reach it on the Metro G Line via Woodley Station.
BMX01.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 rosters exist yet, and quota places go to national committees based on rankings as of 30 May 2028. These names are projections from 2025 form and Paris 2024 results.

potentialContenders.name: Sylvain André
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and second in the 2025 World Cup men's overall. France's depth means he is not guaranteed a spot.

potentialContenders.name: Saya Sakakibara

BMX02.blurb:
Two medal events, one morning. Sunday's semifinals lead straight into the men's and women's finals, with Games medals decided at the Sepulveda Basin course in the San Fernando Valley.

France swept the men's podium at Paris 2024 with Joris Daudet, Sylvain André and Romain Mahieu. Saya Sakakibara won women's gold for Australia, ahead of Manon Veenstra of the Netherlands and Zoé Claessens of Switzerland.

What happens in 2028 is open. Arthur Pilard won the 2025 world title, and France put four riders in the top five of that final, so even making the French team looks tough. Daudet and Sakakibara have not confirmed plans for 2028.

This is the first time the San Fernando Valley hosts Games competition, and BMX has Southern California roots going back to the first organized race in West Los Angeles in 1969. Expect sun, noise and finals decided in seconds.
BMX02.potentialContendersIntro: Finalists are not known and no 2028 rosters have been named. These are projected contenders based on 2025 results and Paris 2024 medalists, if they qualify and compete.

potentialContenders.name: Manon Veenstra

BOX01.blurb:
Boxing returns to the Games program with its first bell of 2028 at Peacock Theater. This opening-day session mixes round-of-32 bouts in three women's and two men's classes with men's +90kg round-of-16 fights.

It is a chance to see fields that have just come through a long qualification cycle. Each nation can send only one boxer per weight class, so every bout carries a lot of weight.

Peacock Theater is better known for award shows. Here every seat looks straight at one raised ring on a huge stage, in a climate-controlled room right in the L.A. Live complex.

potentialContenders.name: Khalimjon Mamasoliev

BOX02.blurb:
Opening day gets a second act under the evening lights. The night card continues the women's 54kg, 60kg and 65kg and men's 55kg and 65kg round-of-32 bouts, plus men's +90kg round-of-16 fights.

The heavyweights are the main draw. Men's +90kg was a Uzbek stronghold in Paris, and whether Bakhodir Jalolov returns to chase a third gold is one of the biggest open questions in the sport.

The evening crowd in the theater should feel like a fight night more than a sports hall. Ring-focused sightlines mean the bigger punches land in front of everyone.

BOX03.blurb:
Sunday afternoon brings a broad sweep of weights. Women's 51kg and men's 60kg and 70kg are in round-of-32 action, while women's 70kg and men's 90kg start at the round-of-16.

It is a good first session for fans who like variety. Several lighter weights in the same card mean fast pacing and plenty of stylistic contrast.

The first world championships to award medals and 2028 quotas together will be held in 2027, so early-round fights here may feature boxers whose paths were set by a long qualifying run. Inside Peacock Theater, the ring dominates the room.

Sunday night keeps the same bracket in motion with a later start and a longer slate. The card includes women's 51kg round-of-32 bouts, women's 70kg and men's 90kg round-of-16 fights and men's 60kg and 70kg round-of-32 bouts.

A round-of-16 loss ends a tournament in a single-elimination bracket, so these late bouts matter. Winners start to move toward the quarterfinals, one win from a guaranteed bronze.

Evening sessions at Peacock Theater tend to feel like a main event. The ring sits on a big raised stage, so everyone gets the same view.

Monday afternoon is a round-of-16 session, so every winner is a step closer to the medal rounds. Women's 60kg and men's 55kg and 65kg are on the card.

Women's 60kg carries a storyline worth watching: Ireland's Kellie Harrington, a two-time champion at this weight, has said she will attempt to qualify. A medal in 2028 would make her only the second Irish athlete to medal at three Games.

The theater's tiered seats put the whole crowd on one side of the ring, which makes the noise for a favorite or a home boxer hard to miss.

Monday evening finishes the round of 16 in women's 60kg, men's 55kg and men's 65kg. By the end of the night, the quarterfinal brackets in those classes will be set.

The women's 60kg draw is especially intriguing. Lin Yu-ting, the Paris 2024 featherweight champion, returned to international competition at the 2026 Asian Boxing Championships after World Boxing cleared her in March 2026.

Reports noted that the World Boxing statement left some uncertainty over her 2028 status. In the room, the evening crowd should add real energy around the one big ring.

The heavyweights often draw the loudest reactions. In this theater setting, that sound should carry well.

The big question mark is Bakhodir Jalolov. He fought Solomon Dacres in London on October 17, 2026 while unbeaten as a pro, and reports have pointed both toward a professional focus and toward an Asian Games selection.

The theater's single-ring layout means every seat gets a clear view of the action, and a heavyweight quarterfinal here would make for a great night.

It is a mix of nerves and celebration, and the theater setup puts everyone on the same side of the ring to feel it.

Expect a crowd that follows the bracket. Peacock Theater's tiered seating puts everyone facing a single ring, so each knockdown draws a collective reaction.

The women's 70kg and men's +90kg semifinals matter most. Every division awards two bronzes, so both losing semifinalists in those weights still leave with a medal, and the winners move on to gold-medal bouts.

The +90kg semifinal is the big draw. Uzbekistan's Bakhodir Jalolov won super-heavyweight gold at two straight Games, and if he qualifies and reaches this stage, heavyweight power will fill the room.

The Peacock Theater is an awards-show venue with about 7,100 tiered seats facing a single raised ring, so everyone looks straight at the action. It's indoors and air-conditioned, in the L.A. Live complex downtown.

The women's 57kg bracket could be especially tight. India's Jaismine Lamboria is the reigning world champion, and Poland's Julia Szeremeta, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, is a likely rival if both qualify.

The 57kg semifinals matter too, because Chinese Taipei's Lin Yu-Ting won Paris 2024 gold at that weight. Her participation in 2028 is not confirmed.

The men's 80kg division is close to Paris light-heavyweight, where Ukraine's Oleksandr Khyzhniak won gold. Uzbekistan's Javokhir Ummataliev is the reigning world champion.

The final session of the boxing tournament hands out four gold medals: women's 57kg and 75kg, and men's 65kg and 70kg. It is the last chance to see boxing at DTLA Arena.

This is the first Games boxing tournament run by World Boxing, and the first with full gender parity. That makes this closing card a milestone as well as a medal session.

The men's 65kg class is deep, with Paris 2024 champions already mixing in 2025 worlds. In the women's 57kg final, Lin Yu-Ting's Paris 2024 gold remains part of the backdrop, and sex testing is now required.

This is a good Sunday-lunchtime ticket for fans who want the full finale.

BSB01.blurb:
Baseball's return to the Games starts at Dodger Stadium on July 13, a day before the Opening Ceremony. Midday first pitch opens the six-team men's tournament.

The host United States, the Dominican Republic and Venezuela are the confirmed teams so far. The other three spots are still to be decided in the 2027 Premier12 and a final qualifier.

Expect sun on the hillside of Chavez Ravine, pastel 1962 seat colors and skyline views from the upper decks. Whether active MLB players take part is still unsettled.

Venezuela will be the story to watch. It won the 2026 World Baseball Classic over the United States, 3-2, and is making its Games debut in baseball.

Evening games at Chavez Ravine mean glowing city views and a big crowd. Whether major leaguers like Bryce Harper are in uniform depends on talks that were unresolved as of mid-2026.

CER01A.blurb:
For the first time in modern Games history, the Opening Ceremony will play out across two stadiums at once. The 2028 Stadium in Inglewood and the LA Memorial Coliseum will share the same Friday evening kickoff.

Film producer Kathleen Kennedy, former Lucasfilm president, is Head of Ceremonies and Content, working alongside Ben Winston and Scott Givens. Openings traditionally feature an athlete parade, an artistic program and the cauldron lighting, though show details remain under wraps.

The Inglewood venue is sunk into the ground beneath a translucent canopy, with open sides that let in the coastal breeze and a ring-shaped video board overhead. Top seats have reportedly sold for more than $5,000, so this is a premium ticket.

The schedule puts the first medals of the Games, in women's triathlon, right after the ceremony.

CER02.blurb:
The Games close on Sunday evening, July 30, with a farewell staged entirely at the LA Memorial Coliseum. Plans originally split the show with Inglewood, but the Los Angeles City Council voted unanimously in November 2025 to keep it at the Coliseum.

Closing ceremonies typically bring a mix of athletes, music and spectacle, capped by the flag handover to the next host city. Kathleen Kennedy, as Head of Ceremonies and Content, is shaping the farewell, though specific programming hasn't been announced.

Paris 2024 set a high bar for the handover, with Tom Cruise arriving from the stadium roof and a pre-recorded Los Angeles segment featuring Billie Eilish, Snoop Dogg and the Red Hot Chili Peppers.

The Coliseum is an open-air bowl dating to 1923, entered through the arched Peristyle plaza beneath the cauldron tower. It is expected to become the first venue to host events at three Summer Games, so this send-off carries real historical weight.

The format is T20, a fast, roughly three-hour contest, and six women's teams are chasing gold, silver and bronze. Most matchdays are morning and evening double-headers, so this 9:00 AM start opens a full day of cricket.

The Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium sits inside the Pomona fairgrounds, about 30 miles east of downtown LA, with roughly 10,000 seats close to the boundary. Expect an early sun-soaked, first-day buzz.

CKT26.blurb:
Thursday evening is the last scheduled men's group-stage play before the medal matches. Expect real stakes under the lights, because results here set the finals line-up.

With six teams in the field, the table can swing on a single over. A team that cruised through earlier rounds could suddenly face a bronze match instead of gold.

It's a good night to be at the ground. The 6:00 PM session in Pomona should be loud, and the next two days bring the bronze and gold medal matches.

CKT27.blurb:
Friday morning is the men's bronze medal match, the first cricket medal contest at a Summer Games since 1900. It's a 9:00 AM start in Pomona, with a podium place on the line.

Bronze matches can be fiercely played, since neither side wants to leave empty-handed. Finalists and bronze contenders are not yet known, and the teams depend on the group stage.

The temporary ground at Fairplex, about 50 km from downtown LA, is a close-in venue where you can watch the sport's first medal moment up close.

CKT28.blurb:
The men's gold medal match closes the cricket program on Saturday, July 29. It will be the first cricket medal match at a Summer Games since Great Britain beat France in Paris in 1900.

The benchmark is high. India scored 255/5 against New Zealand in the 2026 T20 World Cup final, the highest total in a T20 World Cup final. India are the projected favorites, though nothing is settled.

Expect a long, sun-soaked session at the Pomona ground, with a 9:00 AM start. The Fairplex oval will be the setting for the sport's return and its first Games champion of the modern era.

CLB01.blurb:
Opening morning at the Long Beach Climbing Theater brings the first standalone men's Boulder medal event into view. This semifinal decides who reaches the final.

Boulder is short, explosive problem-solving on compact routes, where a single missed move can change the standings. Paris 2024 folded Boulder and Lead into one event, so this format is new for the Games.

The open-air stands face the wall with the Pacific behind it, and a big video screen follows each attempt. Expect a loud, early-morning crowd.

CLB02.blurb:
Speed opens with a qualification round for both men and women. Climbers race alone against the clock on the standardized 15-meter wall, and only the fastest move on to the head-to-head knockouts.

This session is a quick, accessible way to see Speed at its most precise. A slipped foot costs hundredths of a second and can end a run before the knockouts begin.

Qualification gives a close look at the whole field, from record-chasers to climbers just trying to make the bracket. The sea air and ocean backdrop make for a bright, fast-paced afternoon.

CLB03.blurb:
The women's Boulder semifinal is where the field narrows before the first standalone medal in the discipline. Every top finish counts, and every fall matters.

Slovenia's Janja Garnbret, who won the Boulder and Lead combined at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, is the name to watch if she qualifies. She also won Boulder at the 2025 Worlds, her 10th world title.

The temporary stadium sits on the Long Beach waterfront, and the crowd should react to every top and every fall. Bring a hat for a morning session in the sun.

CLB04.blurb:
Lead is the discipline of height and endurance, and this is the first time men's Lead has its own medal event. The semifinal sets the field for the final.

Each climber gets one attempt on a tall, overhanging route, and the winner is whoever climbs highest. A single fall ends the run, so the pressure is on from the first hold.

The Long Beach wall puts the climbers against the open sky, and the audience can follow each climber's progress up the route. The evening slot should feel different from the morning Boulder sessions.

CLB05.blurb:
This is the Speed medal session: quarterfinals, semifinals and finals for men and women in one morning. Races last only a handful of seconds, but the knockout format is tense.

Two climbers race side by side up identical walls, and a false start or a slip can end a run. The women's world record is 6.03 seconds, and the men's record belongs to Sam Watson.

The crowd at Long Beach is close to the action, with the ocean behind the wall. Expect loud cheers for every race, with gold medals decided before lunch.

CLB06.blurb:
The women's Lead semifinal is the last step before the first standalone Lead medal for women. Climbers try to get as high as possible on a single route.

Slovenia's Janja Garnbret won Lead at the 2025 Worlds, then won Boulder the next night. If she qualifies for 2028, she would be the climber to beat.

The evening session puts the climbers on a lit wall beside the Pacific. It should be a quieter, more focused crowd than a Speed final, with big cheers for every high point.

CLB07.blurb:
The men's Boulder final is the first time this discipline awards its own medals. Finalists face a set of compact, powerful problems.

Japan's Sorato Anraku comes in as the reigning world champion if he qualifies, after winning the previous three World Cup Boulder season titles. He also took Paris 2024 combined silver.

Boulder finals are tactical and loud, with fans reacting to every attempt. At Long Beach, the wall faces the stands and the Pacific beyond it, which makes a lively morning scene.

CLB08.blurb:
The women's Boulder final awards the first standalone Boulder medals for women. Climbers go problem by problem in a tight final.

At the 2025 Worlds, Oriane Bertone of France was in position to win until she missed the last boulder, and Janja Garnbret passed her for gold. Finals like that show how quickly it can turn.

Garnbret has won the Boulder and Lead combined at both Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. If she competes in 2028, the Long Beach crowd could see her chase another medal.

CLB09.blurb:
The men's Lead final decides the first standalone Lead medals for men. Finalists each climb one route, and the highest point reached wins.

South Korea's Lee Dohyun is the reigning world champion after winning in Seoul in front of a home crowd. Britain's Toby Roberts is the Paris 2024 combined champion.

Afternoon light on the wall should make for a dramatic setting. Sorato Anraku could appear in both Boulder and Lead if the qualification system allows it.

The climbing program closes with the women's Lead final, the first standalone Lead medals for women. Each finalist climbs one route as high as she can.

Janja Garnbret won Lead at the 2025 Worlds, then took Boulder the next night for her 10th world title. She won the combined at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, so a third Games title is a storyline if she qualifies.

It is a morning session with the ocean behind the wall, and every fall draws a gasp. It is a fitting finale to six days at Long Beach.

CRD01.blurb:
Two medal events, one morning: the men's and women's individual time trials run back to back on July 19, with riders leaving alone and racing only the clock. There are no heats, so the fastest time on the day takes gold.

The course is about 35 km, starting at the LA Zoo in Griffith Park and finishing at Griffith Observatory. Organizers call it challenging, and the finish suggests a climb into the hills, though gradients and the full route are still to be published.

The women's race will crown a new champion, since Paris 2024 winner Grace Brown has retired. On the men's side, Remco Evenepoel won in Paris and at the 2025 World Championships, but his 2028 entry is not confirmed.

This is roadside viewing, not a stadium: no fixed seats, and each rider flashes past briefly. Pick a spot on the climb, watch the start-house rituals near the zoo, and follow the times on the big screens.

CRD02.blurb:
The women's road race opens the Games' road cycling weekend with a 150 km run from the Pacific shoreline to a finish at Griffith Observatory. It ends on a climb, so the day could be decided by who has legs left at the top.

The final ascent is reported at about 3.9 km, with roughly 190 m of elevation gain and an average gradient of 4.9 percent. The steepest pitches average about 6.7 percent. The full turn-by-turn route has not been published yet.

The defending champion is American Kristen Faulkner, who won Paris 2024 with a late attack. Her 2028 participation is not confirmed, but a home-roads defense would be a major storyline.

The start is on the Venice Beach Boardwalk, with fans lining the roadside rather than sitting in stadium seats. Expect palm trees, the Pacific behind you and a very Southern California send-off.

CRD03.blurb:
The men's road race is the longest single day of cycling at the 2028 Games: 250 km from the Venice Beach Boardwalk to Griffith Observatory. The day starts at the Pacific and ends with a climb above the city.

That last ascent is reported at about 3.9 km, with 190 m of climbing and an average gradient of 4.9 percent. The steepest sections average about 6.7 percent, which could suit the sport's strongest climbers. Organizers have not yet released the full route.

Belgium's Remco Evenepoel enters as reigning champion in both the road race and the time trial, if he competes. Tadej Pogacar, who has no gold from the Games, is widely tipped as a possible rival.

Fans can gather along the boardwalk for the start, with the beach and the Venice scene behind them. Expect an early-morning crowd and a long day for anyone following the race.

CSL01.blurb:
The first morning of slalom is where the K1 field gets sorted. Every kayaker gets two runs down the course, and the results decide who advances to the semifinal and final.

Heats are an easy way into the sport. Paddlers must clear the gates in order, and a missed gate or a touch of a pole adds time penalties, so tiny mistakes decide a lot.

The course is a 304.8 m concrete channel with the downtown Oklahoma City skyline behind it. It is open-air, so expect summer heat, and spectators watch from the banks and from the decks of the McClendon Whitewater Center.

CSL02.blurb:
The women's K1 semifinal and final fall on July 15, so this is one of the first medal events of the Games. Fox, the Paris 2024 champion, is the name everyone will be watching.

Both rounds run in one morning. Paddlers race the semifinal first, and the best then go straight into a final that comes down to one run.

The riverside setting makes it a good morning to be there. Fans line the concrete channel and the decks above the rapids, and the rest of the Games are only beginning.

Watch from the banks and you will see the line choices up close. Paddlers attack the gates in the pumped channel, with the Oklahoma City skyline behind them.

CSL04.blurb:
C1 heats begin the canoe events. Paddlers kneel in a single-blade canoe, and each gets two runs to reach the semifinals. Women's and men's fields share this morning session.

Heats are a good way to see the sport at close range. The canoe is harder to control than a kayak, and small slips cost time on every gate.

The session is shorter than the K1 heats, so it is an easy morning to fit in. Watch from the channel banks or the covered patio, with the downtown skyline in view.

The Paris podium also included Germany's Elena Lilik and the USA's Evy Leibfarth. A home-nation medal chance adds extra interest for American fans.

Both rounds are packed into a single morning. The 2026 worlds showed Slovakia and the Czech Republic are deep in this event too, so the final could be a wide-open race.

Men's C1 is one of the sport's most technical events, with a semifinal and final in a single morning on July 19. Gestin, the Paris champion, faces a field full of recent winners.

Britain's Adam Burgess has won silver at both Paris 2024 and the 2026 worlds. Spain's Miquel Trave beat him in Oklahoma City, so a good rivalry is in place.

The event drew 70 paddlers from 32 nations at the 2026 worlds on this course. Watching from the banks, you can see the gate-to-gate moves that decide the final.

CSL07.blurb:
Kayak cross is a different kind of slalom. Several paddlers start together and race head to head, with the top finishers moving on and the others getting a second chance in the repechage.

The format debuted at Paris 2024 and is built for contact and chaos. Expect fast starts, crowded gates and plenty of changes in position.

It is a lively session for newcomers to the sport. The first rounds of racing take place on the Oklahoma City channel, and the large field makes for a quick pace.
CSL07.potentialContendersIntro: Finn Butcher (NZL) and Noemie Fox (AUS) won the first kayak cross titles at Paris 2024. The men's event at the 2026 worlds on this course drew 77 paddlers from 40 nations. The 2028 field is not yet confirmed.

CSL08.blurb:
The heats are the next stage of kayak cross. Paddlers who came through round 1 and the repechage line up in head-to-head races that decide who reaches the quarterfinals.

The session is short, at about two hours, and moves quickly. Each race is over in moments, so every start and every gate matters.

It is a good way to see how kayak cross works before the final day. The pumped channel and nearby decks give a close view of the contact.

CSL09.blurb:
The last day of slalom puts both kayak cross finals on the same morning, with quarterfinals, semifinals and medal races back to back. It closes out the canoe slalom program in Oklahoma City.

Each round is head-to-head racing, so a bad start can end a run for a medal. Favorites have little room for error, and surprise winners are possible.

It is a fast morning on the banks. The final races will feel close, with paddlers jostling at each gate in front of the downtown skyline.

CSP01.blurb:
The sprint program opens with heats and quarterfinals across four events: men's and women's K2 500m, men's C1 1000m and women's C1 200m. It's a long, varied morning for anyone who likes to see the field before the medal races.

The women's C1 200m is a short sprint with tiny margins. Katie Vincent won Paris 2024 in a world-record 44.12, just 0.01 ahead of Nevin Harrison.

The men's C1 1000m brings Paris champion Martin Fuksa and Brazil's Isaquias Queiroz, if both qualify. Lisa Carrington says the 2028 Games remain her goal, so a New Zealand K2 crew is possible.

Marine Stadium is a narrow saltwater channel where fans stand along the shoreline beside the lanes. Belmont Shore and the Long Beach skyline sit in the background, and the same water hosted rowing in 1932.

CSP02.blurb:
Medals are on the line in this session, with semifinals and A finals in the men's and women's K2 500m and the men's C1 1000m. Expect a fast morning of heat-to-final racing.

The C1 1000m is the main draw. Czechia's Martin Fuksa took Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 world title, while Brazil's Isaquias Queiroz has won gold and silver at the past two Games.

In the women's K2 500m, New Zealand's Lisa Carrington and Alicia Hoskin won in Paris. Carrington says she still aims to race in 2028 after announcing a pregnancy in 2026, but a 2028 pairing is not confirmed.

Germany won the men's K2 500m in Paris. At Marine Stadium you watch from the shoreline, close to the lanes, with the finish line a natural gathering point for flag-waving fans.

CSP03.blurb:
Day three is the busiest morning of the heats, with six events in the program: men's and women's K4 500m and C2 500m, plus the men's K1 1000m and women's K1 500m. It's a good way to see crews from many nations.

The men's K1 1000m field was 45 nations strong at the 2025 worlds. That depth means plenty of early drama as paddlers fight for a place in the semifinals.

Paul-style names aside, the storylines are clear. Czechia's Josef Dostal won Paris gold, Hungary's Balint Kopasz owns the 2025 world title, and Lisa Carrington is aiming for a return to the women's K1 500m.

Heats are an easy, low-pressure introduction to the venue. Fans can walk the shoreline and watch crews warm up and race in the narrow channel off Alamitos Bay.

CSP04.blurb:
Two kayak medals are decided here: the women's K1 500m and the men's K1 1000m, plus the women's C2 500m. Semifinals and A finals run back to back in one morning.

The women's K1 500m is where Lisa Carrington's story could land. She won in Paris to reach eight career golds, a tie for the canoeing record, and says she is still targeting 2028 after announcing a pregnancy.

The men's K1 1000m features Paris champion Josef Dostal and 2025 world champion Balint Kopasz. Adam Varga took Paris silver, so Hungarian depth makes this a tough race to call.

Expect a loud, flag-heavy crowd along the shoreline. China won the women's C2 500m in Paris, so its crews are worth watching in that final.

CSP05.blurb:
The canoe sprint program closes with a four-final morning: the women's C1 200m, men's C2 500m and the women's and men's K4 500m. Big boats and a short sprint make a lively finish.

The women's C1 200m is a thriller waiting to happen. Katie Vincent set a world record of 44.12 in Paris, beating Nevin Harrison by 0.01, with Cuba's Yarisleidis Cirilo third.

Germany won the men's K4 in Paris, New Zealand won the women's K4 with Lisa Carrington aboard, and China won the men's C2. Whether those crews return in 2028 is still an open question.

For spectators, the K4 races are a visual treat, with four paddles in sync down the Marine Stadium channel. It's a fitting last session at the same venue that hosted rowing in 1932.

CTR01.blurb:
Track cycling opens at 9 AM with team sprint qualifying, three riders per team and three laps of flying-start speed. It is a short, fast session that sets the bracket for the first-round and final session later in the day.

Each team is timed on its own, and only the fastest advance. The Netherlands set the pace in men's qualifying at the 2025 World Championships, and Great Britain led the women's qualifying.

Carson Velodrome seats roughly 2,400 around a 250-meter Siberian pine track with 45-degree banking. Every seat is close to the boards, so you hear the riders and feel the speed.

CTR02.blurb:
Team sprint gets its medal moment here, with first-round heats leading straight into the finals. Three riders per team, a standing start and a few seconds of raw power decide who wins.

The Paris 2024 winners set world records, 40.949 for the Netherlands men and 45.186 for the Great Britain women. The Netherlands won both world titles in 2025, so a Dutch sweep is a real possibility.

Men's team pursuit qualifying fills out the afternoon. Denmark won the 2025 world title, so expect a different pace from the sprinters' bursts.

Wednesday morning is a prelim session with plenty going on. Men's sprint qualifying uses the flying 200m, and the women's keirin begins with its first round and repechage.

The qualifying time sets the seeding for the men's sprint. Matt Richardson lowered the flying 200m world record to 8.857 in 2025, and Harrie Lavreysen is the six-time-plus world champion looking to defend his Paris 2024 title.

Team pursuit riders are also on track, with women's qualifying and the men's first round. The 250-meter bowl keeps everything close, so you can follow the fast heats up close.

The men's team pursuit final is the medal race here, four riders chasing for 4,000 meters as the stands grow loud. It shares the session with the men's sprint opening rounds and women's keirin quarterfinals.

Australia won Paris 2024 gold over Great Britain after a heat world record, and Italy took bronze. Denmark won the 2025 world title in 3:43.915, so the field is wide open heading into 2028.

The velodrome is compact and the 53 mph turns are right in front of you. It is a fun session if you like to see sprinters and endurance riders on the same afternoon.

This is one of the busiest days of the meet. The women's team pursuit final, the women's keirin final and the full men's omnium all run between 11 AM and about 4 PM.

The United States won women's team pursuit gold in Paris 2024, beating New Zealand. Italy won the 2025 world title, so the home team is not alone at the top.

The keirin brings motor-paced chaos at the finish, with Mina Sato the reigning world champion. Fans can see several medal events in one session at a venue where no seat is far from the track.

CTR06.blurb:
The men's sprint semifinals are the main draw in this early session. Two-lap tactical duels, best of three, will decide who reaches the final.

Harrie Lavreysen won the 2025 world sprint title, his seventh, and the Paris 2024 gold. Matt Richardson was Paris silver for Australia and the 2025 world silver for Great Britain.

Women's sprint qualifying and the 1/32 round with repechages fill out the session. It is a good one to watch the rhythm of sprint racing up close in a very small arena.

Two medals are decided in this session. The men's sprint final and the women's madison final run on the same afternoon, with the women's sprint 1/16 round alongside.

The sprint final is best of three. Harrie Lavreysen beat Matt Richardson for the 2025 world title, and Lavreysen won Paris 2024 with Richardson in silver.

The women's madison is a long, tactical point-scoring race. Great Britain's Katie Archibald and Maddie Leech won the 2025 world title, and Italy won at Paris 2024.

Saturday brings the women's sprint 1/8 and quarterfinals, the men's madison final and the men's keirin opening rounds. The madison is the most chaotic event on the track program.

Portugal won the Paris 2024 men's madison ahead of Italy and Denmark. Iuri Leitao, a member of that Portuguese gold medal pair, was third in the 2025 world scratch race.

In the women's sprint, Paris 2024 champion Ellesse Andrews and Emma Finucane are the names to watch. The venue is small enough that you see every hand sling and lunge.

CTR09.blurb:
The final track session packs a lot into the morning: the women's omnium, women's sprint semifinals and final, and the men's keirin from quarterfinals to final.

The keirin is the chaotic one, with riders behind a pacing motorbike before a flat-out sprint. Harrie Lavreysen won Paris 2024 and the 2025 world title, with Richardson second at Paris.

Jennifer Valente won the women's omnium at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, but she is not confirmed for 2028. Lorena Wiebes was the 2025 world champion.

DIV01.blurb:
Women's 3m springboard starts with the preliminary round, where the field is sorted before the semifinal. It's the easiest way into the diving program and a chance to see the whole field at close range.

Chen Yiwen won this event at Paris 2024 ahead of Australia's Maddison Keeney, part of China's first sweep of all eight diving golds. Whether either returns in 2028 is not yet known.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is an open-air pool in the Arroyo Seco canyon, with Brookside Park's hills behind the well. Diving moved here in September 2025, and a morning session means Southern California sunshine.

The semifinal is the middle round of the individual springboard event and cuts the field down to the finalists. Every dive counts, and a single mistake can end a medal hope here.

China swept all eight diving golds at Paris 2024, so this round is a test of whether other nations can close the gap. Chen Yiwen won gold and Australia's Maddison Keeney took silver in Paris.

Expect a focused crowd at the open-air Rose Bowl Aquatics Center, with the springboard set against the Arroyo Seco hills. The mid-morning session makes for a relaxed, sun-soaked setting.

This is the first individual diving medal on the schedule. Women's 3m springboard goes to a final session that is over quickly, with every dive deciding the standings.

Chen Yiwen won gold at Paris 2024 ahead of Australia's Maddison Keeney. China won every diving gold there, and Great Britain's five medals were the most of any other nation, though none were gold.

The final starts at 3:30 PM at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center, an open-air pool in Brookside Park. Expect a loud crowd, which helps in a home Games.

DIV04.blurb:
Men's 3m springboard opens with a preliminary round that sets the field for the semifinal. Divers need clean, consistent lists to advance, and the morning session is an easy entry point.

China took the top two spots at Paris 2024, with Xie Siyi first and Wang Zongyuan second. Mexico's Osmar Olvera was the only non-Chinese medalist, taking bronze.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center sits in the Arroyo Seco canyon, near the stadium. It's an open-air pool, so a morning session is bright and warm, with the board and the hills in the same view.

China's Xie Siyi and Wang Zongyuan went one-two in Paris, and Mexico's Osmar Olvera took bronze. Olvera also won a synchronized silver with Juan Celaya, so Mexico will try to turn that into a gold.

The late-afternoon session at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center should be cooler than the morning. Watch for the first splashes, and the crowd's reaction to a good dive.

Xie Siyi won in Paris, with Wang Zongyuan second in a Chinese one-two. Osmar Olvera of Mexico was the only non-Chinese medalist, with bronze, so the question is whether he or anyone else can reach the top step.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is an open-air pool in Arroyo Seco. The 3:30 PM start gives a final under lowering afternoon light.

China has been dominant here. Quan Hongchan took gold at Paris 2024 ahead of teammate Chen Yuxi, and North Korea also made the synchronized podium, which suggests the field may be deeper than the results suggest.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center makes for a sunny morning setting, with the tower in front of the Brookside Park hills. A prelim is a relaxed way to see the platform up close.

China took gold and silver in Paris with Quan Hongchan and Chen Yuxi. China won all eight diving golds there, and the semifinal is where challengers must show they can keep pace.

The afternoon light at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is good for this event, which is full of twisting entries. The crowd should be a part of it.

Cao Yuan won gold in Paris, with Japan's Rikuto Tamai second and Great Britain's Noah Williams third. Reigning world champion Yang Hao finished only 12th, a reminder that the event is open.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is open-air, with the tower set against Brookside Park. A morning session is a good chance to watch the platform up close.

Quan Hongchan won Paris 2024 gold ahead of teammate Chen Yuxi. China won every diving gold in Paris, while Great Britain's five medals were the most of any other nation but none were gold.

The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is an open-air pool, and the 3:30 PM start puts the final under afternoon sun. Expect a loud crowd and a lot of flags.

At Paris 2024 the event went from a preliminary round to an 18-diver semifinal. Yang Hao, the reigning world champion, finished 12th in the final, which shows that top contenders can falter.

Tom Daley retired after Paris 2024, so Great Britain looks to divers like Noah Williams. Canada's Rylan Wiens and Nathan Zsombor-Murray also compete on platform. The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center is open-air, so a mid-morning session is bright and warm.

The men's 10m platform final decides one of the most dramatic medals in the sport. Twelve divers qualify from the semifinal, and the window is short, so mistakes cost the most here.

Cao Yuan won gold at both Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, and the second completed China's sweep. China has not always won it, as Australia's Matthew Mitcham won in 2008 and the USA's David Boudia in 2012.

Rikuto Tamai took silver and Noah Williams bronze in Paris, with Tom Daley retired. Whether Cao Yuan competes in 2028 is unconfirmed. The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center puts the tower in front of the Arroyo Seco hills.

The women's synchronized 3m springboard final is a one-hour session with no preliminary round. Two divers must match their timing, height and entry, so the margin for error is small.

Chen Yiwen and Chang Yani won Paris 2024 gold for China. The United States' Sarah Bacon and Kassidy Cook took silver, and Great Britain's Yasmin Harper and Scarlett Mew Jensen won bronze.

The United States will be at home in this event, where it took silver in Paris, though 2028 pairings are not confirmed. The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center puts a late-morning crowd outdoors in Brookside Park.

China's Lian Junjie and Yang Hao won this event at Paris 2024, ahead of Tom Daley and Noah Williams of Great Britain and Canada's Rylan Wiens and Nathan Zsombor-Murray. Daley has retired, so Britain's lineup is an open question.

The session is outdoors at the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center, in the Arroyo Seco canyon with Brookside Park's hills behind the diving well. Expect a late-afternoon Pasadena crowd and plenty of attention on how closely each pair moves together.

The equestrian program opens here, with the first riders in the eventing dressage arena on a Saturday morning. It is a quiet, precise start to a three-phase test that will not be settled until Tuesday.

Germany's Michael Jung set a Games record dressage score on the way to his third individual title at Paris 2024. He and FischerChipmunk FRH scored a CCI5*-L record 18.6 at Kentucky in 2025, though the horse is aging and a 2028 appearance is uncertain.

Santa Anita Park hosted equestrian at the 1984 Games, and the grandstand looks out toward the San Gabriel Mountains. Expect hushed, polite crowds, applause that swells only at the final salute, and morning light on the arena.

Cross-country is the sport's big-risk day, with horse and rider tackling a long course of solid obstacles at speed. It is the phase most likely to reshuffle the standings.

The FEI has floated a hybrid format for 2028 that could decide team medals right after this phase. The published schedule instead lists cross-country as a preliminary round followed by a combined jumping finals session on Tuesday.

Santa Anita is a racetrack with about 26,000 grandstand seats and room for roughly 50,000 more in the infield. Expect a large, mobile crowd moving around the course to catch the big fences.

Both team and individual eventing medals are decided in one long evening of showjumping. After days of dressage and cross-country, a single rail can change the podium.

Pressure builds as the leaders jump in reverse order of standing. At Paris 2024 Jung won ahead of Burton and Collett, with Britain taking team gold over France and Japan.

The finale is a late-day session, so expect floodlights and a more charged crowd than in the dressage sessions. The FEI's hybrid proposal would have moved team medals earlier, but the published schedule awards both sets here.

Dressage begins with the Grand Prix, a qualifier for both team and individual competition. Riders perform a set test, and these scores determine who advances to the Special and the Freestyle.

Germany took Paris 2024 team gold over Denmark and Great Britain, and won the 2025 European team title again. Jessica von Bredow-Werndl's champion mare Dalera BB retired in 2024, so her path to 2028 depends on a new partner.

The morning session is a good entry point. Santa Anita also hosted dressage in 1984, when West Germany's Reiner Klimke won team and individual gold on Ahlerich.

The afternoon Grand Prix session continues the qualification day. This is where riders from across the world, not just the top nations, come into the arena.

Britain's Charlotte Fry took Paris 2024 individual bronze, and she and Glamourdale won a World Cup qualifier in London in December 2025. Belgium's Justin Verboomen, the reigning double European champion, is another rider to watch.

An afternoon dressage session is unhurried. Spectators watch the freestyle-length test move through music and patterns, and applause is saved for the end of each ride.

The morning session offers a relaxed look at the sport's best. At Santa Anita, the arena sits in a wide-open racetrack setting, with the mountains as a backdrop.

The last Grand Prix session closes out the qualifying stage. By the end of the day, the fields for the team final and the individual Freestyle will be set.

The Grand Prix Special decides the team medals. Each country counts its best scores, so a team has to be consistent across all three riders.

Germany won Paris 2024 team gold, with Denmark second and Great Britain third. Germany also won the 2025 European team title, with Britain second and Denmark third, so the same three nations look like the contenders again.

The morning session gives you a medal-stakes event without a late night. At Santa Anita, the crowd tends to stay quiet during rides and then applaud generously at the final salute.

The afternoon Special session offers a second chance to see the team medals decided. It is a fitting time to appreciate the place itself, since Santa Anita staged dressage in 1984 too.

That year, West Germany's Reiner Klimke won team and individual gold on Ahlerich. Germany has a long record of team dressage titles, and it took Paris 2024 gold ahead of Denmark and Great Britain.

EQU12.blurb:
The Freestyle is dressage at its most expressive, with each rider performing a choreographed routine to music. It decides the individual medals, and the scoring rewards both technical precision and artistry.

Jessica von Bredow-Werndl won Paris 2024 gold ahead of Isabell Werth and Charlotte Fry. Her partner for both of her titles, Dalera BB, retired in 2024, so a defense would require a new horse.

A Monday morning final at Santa Anita means music echoing over the racetrack and a crowd that waits for each final pose. Santa Anita's individual dressage history includes Klimke's 1984 win.
