FBL48.blurb:
Nashville hosts a women's quarterfinal with a trip to the semifinals on the line. Geodis Park is the largest soccer-specific stadium in the United States, so this is a real football crowd.

The tournament has grown to 16 teams, the biggest women's field since 2008. That gives this knockout round more depth and more potential surprises.

The open-air stadium has four stands close to the pitch, canopies over much of the seating, and a standing supporters' section that keeps the noise steady. Inter Miami beat Nashville SC here in the 2023 Leagues Cup final, with Lionel Messi playing.

The Fairgrounds site is just south of downtown, and traffic and parking can back up afterward, so build in extra time.

FBL49.blurb:
San Diego gets a women's quarterfinal, and with it a first look at how the 16-team bracket is shaping up. A semifinal and the bronze medal matches will also be played at this stadium later in the week.

Snapdragon Stadium is home to NWSL side San Diego Wave FC, whose first match here in 2022 set a league attendance record. The crowd is used to big women's soccer occasions.

The compact bowl of about 35,000 seats was designed with soccer in mind, and the pitch is natural Bermuda grass. Mission Valley is about 120 miles south of Los Angeles, so this is a road trip for most LA fans.

FBL50.blurb:
San Jose's PayPal Park is the smallest stadium in MLS, which makes this women's quarterfinal an up-close experience. Hardly a seat is far from the pitch.

The steep stands rise like a European ground, and a roof covers much of the seating. Bay FC of the NWSL plays here, so the crowd knows its women's football.

The stadium is known for a big outdoor bar behind one end. Planes arriving at the airport next door pass overhead during matches.

San Jose is about 340 miles north of Los Angeles, so this is the Bay Area leg of the tournament.

FBL51.blurb:
A place in the men's gold medal match is on the line in San Diego. This is one of two men's semifinals, and the winner heads to the Rose Bowl.

The field is only 12 teams this time, down from 16 at Paris 2024. The men's event relies mostly on under-23 squads, so the semifinalists may include players few fans know yet.

The 1:00 PM start means a sunny afternoon at Snapdragon Stadium. The compact bowl of about 35,000 seats keeps the crowd close to the pitch, and the natural Bermuda grass is a good surface for attacking football.

FBL52.blurb:
The second men's semifinal comes under the lights at the Rose Bowl. It's the late slot, with a spot in the gold medal match two days later on the line.

The stadium has hosted a men's Games final before: France beat Brazil 2-0 in 1984 in front of 101,799 fans. It also staged the 1994 World Cup final.

The open-air bowl sits low in the Arroyo Seco with mountain views behind the stands. Evening temperatures should be milder than at afternoon sessions, but the bench seats are tight on legroom.

FBL53.blurb:
A women's semifinal in San Diego puts four wins from the gold medal match within reach. The 5:30 PM start brings the match into the early evening in Mission Valley.

The tournament has expanded to 16 teams, and the football program has more women's teams than men's for the first time. The United States, coached by Emma Hayes, are defending champions.

Snapdragon Stadium is home to San Diego Wave FC, and the compact 35,000-seat bowl suits a loud, close crowd.

FBL54.blurb:
The second women's semifinal comes at night at the Rose Bowl, with the gold medal match here four days later. It's a prime-time stage for a sport that has packed this stadium before.

The field grew from 12 to 16 teams, so the bracket has more depth. Emma Hayes has widened the United States' player pool since Paris 2024, and Alex Morgan was not on her Paris roster.

The open-air bowl sits in the Arroyo Seco with the San Gabriel Mountains behind the stands. Expect a cooler evening than at the afternoon sessions.

FBL55.blurb:
The men's bronze medal match is a final of its own, with a medal and a place on the podium for the winner. Morocco won bronze in Paris 2024, so this is a medal that has real history.

Both teams will have lost in the semifinals two days earlier, so expect a looser, more open match. Under-23 rosters mean new names may stand out.

The 6:00 PM start at Snapdragon Stadium brings golden evening light to Mission Valley. The compact 35,000-seat bowl keeps everyone near the pitch.

The women's bronze medal match is the last chance for two semifinal losers to leave with a medal. It starts at 1:00 PM in San Diego.

The United States took bronze in Tokyo before winning gold in Paris, a reminder that this match can be a step toward better. Germany won the bronze in Paris 2024.

The tournament has 16 teams, the first time it has exceeded 12 since 2008. Snapdragon Stadium, home of NWSL side San Diego Wave FC, has a compact bowl and a sunny afternoon feel.

FBL57.blurb:
The men's gold medal match is the final of the tournament at the Rose Bowl. Spain are defending champions after beating France 5-3 after extra time at the Parc des Princes in Paris 2024.

The Rose Bowl has staged a men's Games final before: France beat Brazil 2-0 in 1984 in front of 101,799 fans. The 1994 World Cup final was also played here.

The tournament is down to 12 teams and mostly under-23 squads, so a new generation will contest the title. The finalists are not yet known.

The 6:00 PM start brings evening light over the Arroyo Seco and the San Gabriel Mountains. Bench-style seats mean little legroom, so arrive early.

FBL58.blurb:
The women's gold medal match decides the champion of the first 16-team women's tournament. The United States are defending champions after a 1-0 win over Brazil in Paris 2024 on a Mallory Swanson goal.

That was a record fifth women's gold for the United States, won under Emma Hayes about 80 days after she took the job. She is now preparing for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil and a home title defense.

The Rose Bowl hosted the 1999 Women's World Cup final, which the United States won on penalties in front of 90,185 fans. The finalists are not yet known.

The 12:30 PM start puts the match in the heat of a Pasadena afternoon, so plan for sun exposure and bring water.

FEN01.blurb:
The first Saturday of the 2028 Games begins on the fencing strips. Women's épée and men's sabre brackets run from the Table of 64 down to the last eight in one long day.

Every bout is direct elimination to 15 touches, so upsets come quickly and a top seed can be out before lunch. Épée tends to be patient and tactical, while sabre is fast and explosive.

The venue is a downtown convention hall with about 7,000 temporary seats, steps from L.A. Live. It suits fans who like to drift between strips and catch several bouts in a day. Organizers note the dates may change.

FEN02.blurb:
These are the first fencing medals of the 2028 Games. Women's épée and men's sabre semifinals and medal bouts close out Saturday night.

The pace changes in the evening. The field is down to the final four in each weapon, and each medal bout is a 15-touch race with no margin for error.

The temporary arena inside the Convention Center should feel tighter and louder than a typical trade-show hall. About 7,000 fans surround the strip, and the opening-weekend crowd will add to that.
FEN02.potentialContendersIntro: The Paris 2024 champions are Hong Kong's Vivian Kong in women's épée and Korea's Oh Sang-uk in men's sabre. Whether either will defend a title in 2028 hasn't been confirmed.

FEN03.blurb:
Sunday's early session is a full day of men's épée and women's foil. Bouts run from the Table of 64 to the quarterfinal stage.

For home fans, the women's foil bracket is the draw. The United States won both individual and team gold in Paris, so American fencers will be watched closely if they qualify.

Men's épée has its own storyline. Japan's Koki Kano won Paris 2024 gold, and all of it plays out in a direct-elimination format to 15 touches.

Sunday night brings medals in women's foil and men's épée. Both weapons play down to the semifinals and medal bouts in one evening.

The big home story is Lee Kiefer. If she competes and wins, it would be her third straight individual foil title, in front of a home crowd. Her plans for 2028 haven't been confirmed.

Expect the 7,000-seat hall to be at its loudest. An American in a final here could make it feel like a home match.

Monday is women's sabre and men's foil, from the Table of 64 through the quarterfinals. It is a long day of fast, high-scoring bouts and sharp footwork.

Men's foil comes with a recent record. Hong Kong's Edgar Cheung defended his title in Paris, and Japan took team gold, so the field is deep.

Women's sabre has the Paris 2024 storyline of a French one-two and Ukraine's Olha Kharlan on the podium. The hall has temporary seating for about 7,000 near the competition area.

In men's foil, a third straight title for Hong Kong's Edgar Cheung is a possible storyline. He hasn't confirmed his 2028 plans.

Women's sabre brings France's Manon Apithy-Brunet and Ukraine's Olha Kharlan into the discussion if they compete. The seated crowd sits close to the strip, so the quick touches are easy to follow.

Team matches are relay-style and go to 45 touches, so a deficit can disappear quickly. Classification bouts also decide the final placings for the eliminated teams.

It is a good daytime session for anyone who likes the swings of a relay. The Convention Center hall will be set up around the strip.

Italy is the defending champion, having beaten France in Paris. Poland won bronze, so a rematch of the podium is possible but not certain.

Thursday morning is the men's épée team event, from the Table of 8 to the semifinals and classification matches. The field is unusually open.

Hungary won Paris 2024 gold over Japan in overtime. Japan reversed that at the 2025 World Championships, and Kazakhstan has since climbed to No. 1 in the team rankings.

Behind these eight teams, 47 nations competed at the 2025 Worlds, so reaching this session is already a big step. It is a good morning for tight matches.

FEN16.blurb:
Japan won men's team foil gold at Paris 2024, beating Italy, with France taking bronze. This session hands out the 2028 versions of those medals, and the champions will be defending in a hall built for the occasion.

Team bouts run to 45 touches, so a deficit can vanish quickly once a anchor fencer takes the strip. Italy won the 2025 world title in Tbilisi, and the United States took silver there after a semifinal comeback over Hungary.

The LA Convention Center Hall 1 is normally a trade-show floor, but temporary seating for about 7,000 wraps the strip here. Expect a loud, close-in atmosphere, especially if the U.S. men are fencing for a medal.
FEN16.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 champion Japan, silver medalist Italy and bronze medalist France set the benchmark, while 2025 world results point to Italy and the U.S. as likely contenders. Who actually qualifies for 2028 is not yet known.

FEN17.blurb:
This is the full day-one drama of women's team sabre: the Table of 8, then the semifinals, plus classification bouts. Quarterfinal losers are out of the medal hunt, so every early match carries real pressure.

Sabre is the fastest of the three weapons, and 45-touch team matches can swing on a single hot streak. Ukraine are the defending champions, though Olha Kharlan, their Paris leader, paused her career after announcing a pregnancy.

In the hall, the format means a steady procession of matches with flags and chants from several countries. It is an easy way to see the field narrowed to the final four before the evening medal matches.

FEN18.blurb:
The final day of fencing at the 2028 Games ends with the women's team sabre bronze and gold medal matches. Ukraine won Paris 2024 gold over Korea, with Japan taking bronze.

The field has shifted since then. France, whose Manon Apithy-Brunet and Sara Balzer went one-two in Paris individual sabre, won the 2025 world title, and Korea again took silver. Hungary earned bronze.

Expect a charged evening at the Convention Center, with seating around a single raised strip and flags from several nations. Ukraine's Olha Kharlan paused her career after announcing a pregnancy, so their 2028 team is an open question.

FFB01.blurb:
Flag football's first day as a Games medal sport opens here, the afternoon after the opening ceremony. Three games across the men's and women's tournaments set the tone for a brand-new event.

Only some of the field is known. The U.S., Italy and Canada have men's spots, and the U.S., Canada and Mexico have women's spots. The other three berths per gender are decided at qualifiers in June 2028.

Exposition Park Stadium holds about 22,000 and sits beside the Coliseum. Expect a debut-day buzz as fans see this version of the sport at the Games for the first time.
FFB01.potentialContendersIntro: The U.S. men are reigning world champions after beating Italy 46-26 in the 2026 final, and Canada's women won the 2026 women's world title. Who plays on day one depends on the schedule and the June 2028 qualifiers.

FFB02.blurb:
Saturday night brings the first evening games under the lights. Each session offers three games in a little over three hours, so it works well for newcomers.

The rules are easy to pick up. It is five-on-five with no linemen or special teams. Each drive starts at the offense's own 5-yard line, and a play ends when a defender pulls one of two flags from the ball carrier's waist.

Organizers' renderings show temporary stands on the field, which shrinks the playing surface that flag football shares with lacrosse. Seats should be close to the action.

FFB03.blurb:
Sunday afternoon is a relaxed way to see the sport. Each game is two 20-minute halves, so there is not much downtime.

The men's side has a strong storyline in Italy, which reached the 2026 world final by beating Germany and then Canada 41-36. On the women's side, Mexico has won big events, including the 2025 World Games.

The stadium has steep stands set close to the field, and the crowd should be loud even at a young Games sport. It is an easy afternoon out in South LA.

Sunday night belongs to a stadium taking on a new role. It opened in 2018 as an LAFC home, and this will be its first time as a Games venue.

The women's bracket carries the biggest storyline. The U.S. women edged Germany 35-34 and beat Great Britain in the 2026 semifinals, then lost the final to Canada.

Expect LA fans in team colors alongside curious soccer regulars. Even prelim games under the lights can feel big in a close stadium like this.

Monday afternoon puts flag football at the heart of the Games' first week. NFL.com noted that the timing could reduce conflicts with NFL training camps.

That matters because NFL clubs voted in May 2025 to let players on NFL contracts try out for national teams, with one per club. No NFL player had been confirmed for a 2028 roster as of late 2026.

The session is a good fit for someone who wants to see several national teams in one afternoon. Men's and women's games share the same intimate setting.

FFB06.blurb:
Monday night offers a good look at how fast a flag football game moves. With no linemen and short fields, offenses often score quickly and defenders must stay sharp to pull flags.

The U.S. men are heavy favorites on paper, but American Samoa beat them 38-32 in 2026 group play. The women's field has stiff competition, with Canada, Mexico and the U.S. all qualified.

A seat close to the field is the draw here. Temporary stands are planned on the field itself, so the action should feel nearby.

Tuesday afternoon sits in the middle of the preliminary run, with medal games still a few days away. Teams will start to know what they need to reach the semifinals.

The field has plenty of intrigue. Canada's women have quarterback Sara Parker, the 2026 MVP, while the men's draw includes teams that played close games at the worlds.

The stadium sits next to the Coliseum, so it is easy to turn a game into a bigger day in Exposition Park.

Wednesday afternoon is one of the last chances to see prelim play before the semifinals. Top four of six teams advance in each tournament, so every game has a little extra weight.

The tournament also shows how global the sport has become. Nigeria qualified for the 2026 worlds as African champions but could not compete due to visa issues.

The afternoon slot is a relaxed way to catch a few games, with parks, museums and the Coliseum all nearby.

Wednesday night is the last prelim session, and seeding for the semifinals will be up for grabs. It is the most consequential of the group-stage evenings.

Expect a full house feel under the lights, with the Coliseum next door adding to the sense of place.

Friday afternoon at Exposition Park Stadium should have a tense feel, with the entire tournament narrowed to four teams.

The U.S. men have won seven of 12 world titles and enter as reigning champions. Italy was the 2026 runner-up, and Canada beat Mexico in overtime for bronze.

Friday night at Exposition Park Stadium should be the biggest crowd of the tournament so far. Expect a loud, tight venue for history in the making.

GAR01.blurb:
The 2028 gymnastics program opens with the first of three men's qualification sessions on Saturday afternoon at DTLA Arena. The scores set the fields for the team final, the all-around final and the eight-man apparatus finals.

This is an easy way into the sport. With 96 men competing across three subdivisions, you will see top contenders and long-shot specialists on the same floor.

The steep downtown bowl puts even upper-level seats right above the floor, high bar and rings. It is a casual, in-and-out kind of session before the medals begin.
GAR01.potentialContendersIntro: Subdivision assignments are not set, so these names are projections for a session that could include any of the top men. Daiki Hashimoto won the 2025 world all-around title, and Zhang Boheng took silver.

GAR02.blurb:
The middle men's qualification session is the afternoon slot on opening Saturday. Every routine here counts toward team standings and individual advancement to the finals.

Twelve men's teams are expected in Los Angeles, so several contenders could be working through six apparatus rotations at once. Look for the quiet specialists: pommel horse, rings and vault routines can change the apparatus-final picture.

Early in the session the arena is relaxed and easy to move around. By the end, the crowd usually starts to feel the pressure of the cut lines.

The last men's qualification subdivision runs on Saturday night and finalizes who advances. When it ends, the men's team final on July 17 and the all-around final on July 19 will be set.

The night session carries extra tension because the leaderboard is nearly complete. Gymnasts in the late rotations know exactly what scores they need.

With the evening crowd in, the arena feels more like a major event. The lights and noise build as the final routines wrap up.

The qualification scores will set the team final, the all-around final and the apparatus finals. This is also a way to see the names that could shape the next few days.

Expect a loud, morning crowd and a big focus on every U.S. routine. Whether Simone Biles will compete in 2028 remains unknown.

The arena is full and loud by mid-afternoon, and you can follow the scoreboard from anywhere. It is a good slot for fans who care more about specific gymnasts than the full day.

The men's team final is the first gymnastics medal of the 2028 Games, and it is a must-see for the sport's best team format. Five gymnasts per team compete with no reserves, so every fall matters.

Japan won Paris 2024 ahead of China and the United States, and Japan also won the 2026 world team title. Twelve teams are expected in Los Angeles, with three qualified through the 2026 Worlds and nine more via 2027.

GAR09.blurb:
The women's team final is a Tuesday-night showcase of the sport's strongest depth. Each nation brings a five-gymnast team with no reserves, so a single mistake can change a medal.

The United States won Paris 2024 ahead of Italy and Brazil, and ESPN has described the U.S. women as heavy favorites in 2028. China did edge the U.S. by 0.233 to win the 2026 world team title, so the race looks closer.

It is a high-ceiling night for the arena, with floor often the loudest apparatus. Biles's eventual decision remains unknown.

GAR10.blurb:
The men's all-around final is the title for the sport's best multi-event gymnast. Each athlete competes across six apparatus, and nations are usually limited to two entries.

Paris 2024 champion Shinnosuke Oka is back in the picture, but Daiki Hashimoto has won three straight world titles, including 2026 with 85.988. China's Zhang Boheng has been the runner-up.

The evening crowd can track each rotation from high in the seats. It is a long, tense ranking race that can change late on high bar.

GAR11.blurb:
The women's all-around final is Thursday night, and Simone Biles's status could dominate the headlines. She won in Paris 2024 but had not decided on 2028 as of late 2026.

Skye Blakely won the 2026 world title, and the U.S. has had a woman on every world and Games all-around podium since 2003. Rebeca Andrade has said she plans to compete in 2028.

Expect a big, loud, full arena and a close race across vault, bars, beam and floor. This could be one of the most closely watched sessions of the program.

GAR12.blurb:
This is the first of three apparatus final sessions on the schedule. FIG has not yet confirmed which apparatus will be in each session, so the exact lineup is still open.

Apparatus finals are the best place to see specialists on a single event, with eight finalists each. Men and women are both part of the program, so expect a mix of events across the three days.

The session runs from late morning to mid-afternoon, so it is an easy daytime ticket. Floor, vault, bars and pommel horse are all possible depending on the final schedule.

The second apparatus final session spans a late-morning slot on Sunday. FIG has not confirmed which events are in each session, so treat the events as undecided.

The 2026 Worlds hint at the stories to follow. Beam, parallel bars and vault all had tight finishes, including Nemour beating Zhang Qingying on a tiebreak.

The daytime crowd usually includes many families and gymnastics fans, and the arena keeps an intimate feel. Each routine stands alone, with the scoreboard moving after every gymnast.

GAR14.blurb:
The third apparatus final session wraps up the individual medals on Monday. FIG has not announced the apparatus for each session, so which events appear is still to be determined.

Floor and horizontal bar are possibilities. Claire Pease won floor at the 2026 Worlds in a U.S. one-two, and Tang Chia-Hung won high bar over Shinnosuke Oka.

This is the last big individual day before the mixed team event. Floor and high bar are two of the most dramatic apparatus to watch live.

GAR15.blurb:
The mixed team final closes the artistic gymnastics schedule as a new medal event for 2028. FIG has not approved the format or duration, so what this session looks like is still unknown.

The 2025 European Championships trial used one man and one woman per nation, with the top 16 qualifying pairs advancing. Gymnastics Now reported that entrants are expected to come from each nation's existing five-person teams.

Expect a festive final day at DTLA Arena with a lot of crossover from the men's and women's fan bases. Nations with strong men's and women's programs should have an edge.

GLF01.blurb:
The men's 72-hole tournament opens at Riviera, a course known to the PGA Tour crowd as Hogan's Alley. Round 1 is the first look at 60 players navigating a layout most know from the Genesis Invitational.

Scottie Scheffler arrives as the Paris 2024 champion, having closed with a 62 for gold at 19 under. Tommy Fleetwood took silver and Hideki Matsuyama bronze, and Scheffler won two majors in 2025.

There is no central grandstand here. Fans spread along the fairways of a Pacific Palisades canyon, so pick a hole and watch the field come through.

Round 2 is where the men's leaderboard begins to take shape at Riviera. It still leaves plenty of room for a charge, as Scheffler showed in Paris by starting slowly and finishing with a 62.

Many players here have already competed at Riviera in the Genesis Invitational, so course knowledge should matter. Scheffler's 2025 included wins at the PGA Championship and the Open Championship.

This is a good day for wandering the hillsides. Fans can watch the clubhouse amphitheater around the 18th green or follow a group across the canyon fairways.

Moving day sets the 54-hole standings before the final round. The leaders here are not guaranteed medals, as Paris 2024 showed.

Jon Rahm and Xander Schauffele shared the 54-hole lead in Paris and both missed the podium. Scheffler came from behind to win.

Expect louder crowds around the closing holes, where the slopes below the clubhouse form a natural amphitheater. It is a good session to watch the pressure build.

GLF04.blurb:
This is the final round and the day the men's medals are decided. After it ends, Riviera turns to the first mixed-team event.

Scheffler is the defending champion after a closing 62 in Paris. If he wins again, he would be the first man to win back-to-back individual golf golds since golf returned in 2016.

Fleetwood and Matsuyama are also back as Paris medalists, if they qualify. The finish should unfold around the 18th green, where a Ben Hogan statue stands nearby and the hillside gives fans a view.

GLF05.blurb:
Golf gets its first team medal event at the Games since 1904. Each team pairs one man and one woman from the same country.

The IGF lists four-ball as Round 1, so partners play their own balls and count the better score on each hole. Sixteen teams are planned, drawn from those already in the individual fields.

The event is played on the Sunday and Monday between the men's and women's tournaments. Teams have not been named, though media previews have floated a possible USA pairing of Scheffler and Nelly Korda.

GLF06.blurb:
The first golf mixed-team medals at the Games are decided in 18 holes of foursomes, or alternate shot. Partners share one ball and take turns hitting.

That format tends to punish mistakes and reward composure. Scores after the opening four-ball round carry over, so the medal race is still moving.

With the whole event done by early afternoon, this is a compact, high-stakes day. The elevated clubhouse and the finishing holes should give fans a view of the closing moments.

Lydia Ko is the defending champion and the most decorated golfer in Games history, with silver in 2016, bronze in Tokyo and gold in Paris. Esther Henseleit won silver and Janet Lin bronze in Paris.

Expect a field of about 60 players making a first pass at the course. Fans can walk the fairways and get a sense of how the layout plays.

The final round decides the women's individual medals and closes the golf program at Riviera. It is the last chance to see the course at a Games.

Ko, the defending champion, completed her set of medals in Paris and is the most decorated golfer in Games history. Henseleit took silver and Lin bronze.

GRY01.blurb:
The first of two qualification sessions opens rhythmic gymnastics at the 2028 Games. Each gymnast performs four apparatus routines, and only the top 10 combined scores move on to the all-around final.

Up to 24 individuals compete, with a maximum of two per nation. Early sessions like this are a chance to see the full field, including gymnasts from smaller federations who earned places through World Championships, World Cup Series results, Continental Championships or universality spots.

The Galen Center is an indoor bowl of about 10,000 seats, close to the floor, on the USC campus beside the Jefferson/USC Metro station. Expect a lively, flag-waving crowd and the quiet that falls before each routine.

GRY02.blurb:
The evening qualification session finishes the individual field. Combined scores from both sessions decide the 10 gymnasts who reach the all-around final, so every drop or out-of-bounds exit can cost a place.

The usual contenders have a hard job here. Ribbons, hoops, balls and clubs are judged for difficulty, execution and artistry, and one error can change a whole rotation.

Evening sessions at the Galen Center usually have a stronger atmosphere than daytime ones. The upper deck is still close enough for a clear view of the floor, and the crowd responds to every big throw and catch.

GRY03.blurb:
Group qualification puts the five-gymnast ensembles on the floor together. The groups with the highest scores advance to the group all-around final, which is held the following day.

The event is about synchronization, exchanges and risky tosses. At the 2025 World Championships, groups performed two routines, five ribbons and three balls plus two hoops, so one mistimed throw can ruin a routine.

The field looks wide open. Japan won the 2025 world title, Paris 2024 champion China missed the podium that year, and the Paris silver and bronze medalists, Israel and Italy, finished fifth and 15th at those worlds.

This is the individual all-around final, where medals are decided. The top 10 qualifiers each perform four apparatus routines, and their combined scores set the podium.

Paris 2024 brought Germany its first gold in the sport when Darja Varfolomeev won with 142.850. Bulgaria's Boryana Kaleyn took silver and Italy's Sofia Raffaeli took bronze. Varfolomeev retained her world title in 2025 with 121.900, though scoring differences make comparisons with Paris difficult.

The podium looks competitive. Stiliana Nikolova took world silver, Raffaeli keeps reaching the podium, and Onofriichuk finished fourth at the 2025 worlds. Who actually gets there in 2028 is open.

The Galen Center should be loudest in the final rotation, when the leaderboard is tight and the crowd is on its feet.

The group all-around final is the last rhythmic gymnastics medal event of the 2028 Games. The gymnasts perform together on the floor, and the tension is in the details of every exchange.

China won Paris 2024 gold with 69.800, 0.95 ahead of Israel, with Italy third. Japan then won the 2025 world title by 0.300 with 55.550, ahead of Brazil and Spain, while China finished fourth.

The field looks open. Japan won silver at the 2026 Worlds in Frankfurt, though it placed ninth at the Baku World Cup and sixth at the Beijing World Challenge Cup that year.

This short afternoon session should have a closing-day feel, with flags in the stands and a crowd that has watched the discipline all week.

GTR01.blurb:
Trampoline is one of the shortest, most vertical spectacles at the Games: athletes launch several stories above the bed and spin through ten skills in about 20 seconds. This session packs the men's qualification and the medal-deciding final into one afternoon.

Paris 2024 went to Ivan Litvinovich (AIN), ahead of China's Wang Zisai and Yan Langyu. Wang then won the 2025 world title, with the USA's Ruben Padilla taking silver and Japan's Hayato Miyano bronze.

Judges score difficulty, execution and time in the air, and no format change has been announced. Expect a qualification round that trims the field, then a final where a single bounce can reshuffle the podium.

DTLA Arena's steep bowl means even upper-level seats look straight down onto the trampoline. It is an indoor, midday session in the L.A. Live district, with the Metro A and E lines stopping nearby.

Saturday morning returns to the women's group stage. For a weekend outing, a 9:00 AM double-header is hard to beat.

Saturday afternoon puts two more women's group matches on the court. With the weekend crowd, it's a good value for fans new to handball.

The arena's roughly 12,000 seats circle the court closely. Walk the waterfront and see the Wyland whale mural before heading in.

Saturday night caps a full week of women's group play with an evening double-header. The final preliminary matches help set up the knockout bracket, so the stakes build.

Norway comes in as the benchmark after fifth world title in 2025. Henny Reistad has signed with French club Brest for 2027-28, so she's expected to be in top form by 2028, if selected.

Come for a prime-time atmosphere in a drum-shaped arena on the Long Beach waterfront. Handball in Long Beach is listed as running July 12-28.

The 12-team field splits into two groups of six, and the top finishers advance. Pairings depend on group results and qualification, and as of mid-2026 only the host United States men have a confirmed place.

Inside the drum-shaped arena, about 12,000 seats ring a compact court. Outside, Wyland's giant whale mural wraps the building near the harbor.

The men's field is wide open at the edges even if Denmark looks like the benchmark. The Danes won the 2025 world final 32-26 over Croatia, with goalkeeper Emil Nielsen making a key stop on Josip Sipic.

Bring a jacket for the cool arena. You will see big bodies, fast restarts and long-range shots.

Denmark coach Nikolaj Jacobsen guided the Danes to the 2026 European title, and he rested star Mathias Gidsel when he could. Whether the same team and approach carry to 2028 is unknown.

With the harbor close by, a night session in Long Beach can feel like a festival, and the Wyland mural frames the walk in.

HOC31.blurb:
The men's bronze medal match is the last game for teams that came to Carson hoping for gold. It is also the last chance to leave with a medal. Nobody plays it for show.

India took this medal at Paris 2024, beating Spain, but the 2028 field is wide open. Recent Pro League form points to Belgium, England, Australia, Germany and Spain as strong candidates to be in the mix.

This is a new-format Games, with a play-in round before the quarterfinals, so the teams in this match will have navigated a longer path. The 10:30 AM start suits a relaxed morning on the temporary stands of a field set beside the LA Galaxy stadium and the velodrome.
HOC31.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 men's qualifiers beyond the host place were confirmed at the time of writing, so these are projections based on recent form. India won bronze at Paris 2024, while Belgium, England, Australia and Germany have been consistent Pro League performers.

HOC32.blurb:
The men's gold medal match is the final of the field hockey tournament. It closes the first Friday of the hockey program at Carson Field under the lights.

The Netherlands are defending champions. At Paris 2024 they drew 1-1 with Germany and won the shoot-out 3-1 for their first men's title since 2000. A shoot-out is always possible if the match is level, and it is dramatic.

The field is hard to call. Belgium won the 2025-26 Pro League and the Dutch took the 2024-25 edition, while Australia, England and Germany are all in the picture. No 2028 qualifiers beyond the host place were confirmed at the time of writing.

The night final at the roughly 15,000-seat primary pitch should be the loudest ticket of the hockey schedule. The stands are temporary, so expect a compact, loud setting.

HOC33.blurb:
The women's bronze medal match is the last game of the day for teams that missed out on the final. Medal hopes are still alive for whoever wins.

Argentina won this medal at Paris 2024 by drawing 2-2 with Belgium and winning the shoot-out 3-1. Belgium, who lost that match, were third in the 2024-25 Pro League, so a rematch is plausible but not guaranteed.

A play-in round is new for 2028, so teams here will have had a long road. The 10:30 AM start is a good fit for a relaxed morning session.

Carson Field's temporary stands put fans close to a fast, passing game, and it sits near the soccer stadium, tennis stadium and velodrome.

HOC34.blurb:
The women's gold medal match is the final session of the hockey tournament. It is a big Saturday-night ticket at Carson Field.

The Netherlands are the defending champions and own a record five women's golds. At Paris 2024 they beat China in a shoot-out after a draw, with China leading for much of the match.

The Dutch also won the 2024-25 Pro League by eight points over Argentina. Argentina, Belgium and China are recent contenders, but 2028 qualifiers are unconfirmed.

The primary pitch has roughly 15,000 temporary seats. Expect a loud, close-up crowd in the South Bay evening air next to the soccer stadium and tennis stadium.

The mats sit in temporary stands inside Hall 2 of the Convention Center downtown. It is an easy way to see many nations in action, with the host USA guaranteed a place in every weight class.

Hifumi Abe won men's -66kg in Tokyo and defended in Paris, but his Japan teammates Takeshi Takeoka (2025 world champion) and Ryoma Tanaka (2024) have also won world titles. Japanese team selection is a storyline in itself.

Women's -52kg centers on Uta Abe, who won her fifth world title in 2025. Paris 2024 champion Diyora Keldiyorova of Uzbekistan is among the challengers.

Finals at the Convention Center are loud, close-up affairs, with tatami just a few rows from the stands.

The final session of the 2028 judo program is the mixed team event, where bronze and gold are decided back to back. Six-person squads from different weight classes fight in a relay-style tie, so one lucky bout can swing the whole afternoon.

France has won both Games mixed team finals, beating Japan in Tokyo and again at Paris 2024, where Teddy Riner won the deciding bout. Whether Riner competes in 2028 is not confirmed.

The field may look different this time. Georgia beat Korea 4-1 at the 2025 world final in Budapest, ending a run in which Japan had won every world mixed team final against France.

The venue is LA Convention Center Hall 2, an indoor hall in the downtown cluster near L.A. Live. Fans sit in temporary stands around the mats, so expect a loud, close-in finish to the week.

potentialContenders.note: Winner of both Games mixed team finals, including a comeback over Japan at Paris 2024. Likely contender if its core squad stays strong; Teddy Riner's participation is unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Lost both Games finals to France but won every world mixed team final before 2025, and took bronze at the 2025 worlds. Projected medal contender.

potentialContenders.name: Georgia
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world title with a 4-1 victory over Korea, led by a roster including Lasha Bekauri and Guram Tushishvili. Could be a gold-medal threat if its stars are in form.

potentialContenders.name: Korea
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2025 world runner-up, with Kim Min-jong and Kim Ha-yun on that roster. Likely to be in the medal mix.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist; could return to the medal matches if it qualifies and keeps its depth.

LAC01.blurb:
Lacrosse returns to the Summer Games program as a medal sport for the first time since 1908, and this is where it starts. Monday's men's session opens the tournament with three round-robin games.

The Sixes format is a quick-hitting version of the sport: six players per side, a smaller field and short games. Six men's teams play a round robin, and the standings decide who reaches the medal games on July 29.

The midday slot at Exposition Park Stadium puts you close to the field in a compact, soccer-style bowl. Expect a curious, first-of-its-kind crowd.
LAC01.potentialContendersIntro: Only the United States is confirmed as host; the other five men's teams are decided through 2027 and early 2028 qualifying. Canada currently tops World Lacrosse's men's sixes rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 1 in World Lacrosse's men's sixes rankings and winner of the men's title at the Super Sixes event in Oshawa; a projected contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Qualifies automatically as host and is ranked No. 2 in men's sixes; won the 2026 Pan-American Sixes gold.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 3 in men's sixes; a possible Asia-Pacific qualifier if it secures a place.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Took the first Asia-Pacific spot for the 2027 World Sixes Championships; a plausible 2028 qualifier.

LAC02.blurb:
Women's lacrosse plays for Summer Games medals for the first time, and the opening night gets the spotlight under the lights. Three round-robin games make up the session.

The United States and Canada have traded recent big wins. Canada beat the U.S. 14-12 in the 2022 World Games sixes final, and the U.S. answered 16-8 in 2025.

Evening games at Exposition Park Stadium should feel energetic, with the steep stands close to the field. The north-end supporters' terrace is built for noise.
LAC02.potentialContendersIntro: Only the host United States is guaranteed a place; five more women's teams will come mainly from the 2027 World Lacrosse Sixes Championships and a qualifier in early 2028. These are projected contenders based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and 2025 World Games sixes gold medalist; Marie McCool was that tournament's MVP.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: 2022 World Games sixes champion and 2025 silver medalist; a likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Won bronze in women's sixes at the 2025 World Games; a possible qualifier.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2025 World Games sixes semifinals; could return if it qualifies.

LAC03.blurb:
Day two of the men's round robin raises the stakes. With only six teams and a short schedule, every early result shapes the path to the July 29 medal games.

Sixes is built for momentum swings. Small rosters and a tighter field mean a hot goalie or one scoring run can flip a game quickly.

This is a good midday option if you want to see the new format with some context. The stadium sits next to the LA Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park.
LAC03.potentialContendersIntro: The men's field is not set; five teams come from the 2027 World Sixes Championships in Colorado Springs and one from a qualifier in early 2028. These teams are likely contenders based on current rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: No. 1 in men's sixes rankings, with a double gold at the Super Sixes event in Oshawa; projected contender.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Qualified as host and ranked No. 2; has built a sixes-specific program under coach Andy Shay.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 3 in men's sixes; will need to qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Great Britain
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 4 in men's sixes; a possible qualifier via the European route.

LAC04.blurb:
The women's round robin rolls into night two with three more games. The pool is small, so early results carry weight.

The United States arrives with world titles in women's field, box and sixes lacrosse. Canada has been its closest rival in recent sixes events.

Evening games bring a late-night atmosphere to Exposition Park Stadium. Sixes is short and fast, so it suits first-time lacrosse fans.
LAC04.potentialContendersIntro: Apart from the host United States, the women's field will not be settled until after the 2027 and early-2028 qualifying events. The list below is based on 2025 World Games results.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Went unbeaten at the 2025 World Games; Marie McCool has five world titles with the U.S. national team, a record for a U.S. player.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Beat Australia 21-4 in the 2025 World Games semifinal and took silver; a likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games bronze medalist; a possible qualifier.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2025 World Games semifinals before losing 24-10 to the U.S.; could appear if it qualifies.

LAC05.blurb:
Midweek men's action carries a unique storyline: the Haudenosaunee, whose Confederacy is credited with inventing lacrosse. Their participation in 2028 is not yet confirmed.

The Haudenosaunee Nationals are ranked No. 5 in men's sixes and No. 3 in men's field. In January 2025 the U.S. and Canadian governments asked the IOC to allow them to compete.

If they take the field in Los Angeles, this session could feel historic. Either way, it is the middle day of the five-day round robin at Exposition Park Stadium.
LAC05.potentialContendersIntro: The Haudenosaunee are the headline, but their eligibility for the Games was still pending IOC approval in available reports. Other teams are likely contenders based on rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Haudenosaunee
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 5 in men's sixes and a 2026 Pan-American qualifier for the 2027 Worlds; 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and No. 2 in men's sixes; won the 2026 Pan-American gold.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: World No. 1 in men's sixes; a projected contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 6 in men's sixes and No. 4 in men's field; a possible qualifier.

LAC06.blurb:
The middle night of the women's round robin is a good look at how fast sixes can turn. Games are 32 minutes, with little room to recover from a slow start.

The 2025 World Games final showed the stakes. An early red card on Canada's Jordan Dean helped the U.S. race to a 7-3 first-quarter lead on the way to a 16-8 win.

Expect a loud evening at Exposition Park Stadium, with close sight lines and a first-ever women's Games tournament as backdrop.
LAC06.potentialContendersIntro: All six women's teams will not be known until after the final qualifier in early 2028. The names below are projections based on 2025 World Games results.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games champion; goalkeeper Shea Dolce made 38 saves in five games there.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Two World Games silver medals (2017, 2025) plus the 2022 sixes gold; a likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2025 World Games semifinals; could return if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games bronze medalist; a possible qualifier.

LAC07.blurb:
With the round robin on day four, men's teams are jockeying for medal-game spots. Three games fill the midday window.

This session could showcase the sport's international spread. Japan, Great Britain and Australia all sit in the top six of the men's sixes rankings, though none are confirmed for 2028 yet.

The sun-drenched afternoon at Exposition Park Stadium suits a casual first visit to lacrosse. The stadium seats about 22,000, with seating tight to the field.
LAC07.potentialContendersIntro: Only the United States is guaranteed a place. Qualifying runs through 2026 continental events, the 2027 World Sixes Championships and a final qualifier in March or April 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 3 in men's sixes; a projected contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Great Britain
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 4 in men's sixes; qualification through the European route is plausible.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 6 in men's sixes, and took the first Asia-Pacific spot for the 2027 Worlds.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 1 in men's sixes; a likely contender if it qualifies.

LAC08.blurb:
Women's lacrosse makes its Summer Games debut, and by Thursday night the round robin is deep enough for real pressure. Three games shape the standings ahead of the medal games.

Sixes was launched by World Lacrosse in 2021 with the Games in mind. Seeing it at full volume in a stadium is a fitting way to witness the format's first big stage.

Evening sessions at Exposition Park Stadium should have a lively, packed feel. The tight sight lines mean you are never far from the action.
LAC08.potentialContendersIntro: The women's field will not be known until after 2027 and early-2028 qualifiers, with the U.S. already in as host. These are projected contenders based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games bronze medalist, winning 13-12 over Japan on a golden goal; a possible qualifier.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and 2025 World Games champion; also won the 2022 World Lacrosse Women's Championship in field.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Has three silver and two bronze medals at the Women's Championship; a likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games semifinalist; could appear if it qualifies.

LAC09.blurb:
The final day of the men's round robin sets the bracket for Saturday. Anyone chasing a medal-game spot has to deliver by the end of this three-game session.

The top rivalry in the sport is Canada versus the United States. Canada is No. 1 in men's sixes and box, while the U.S. is No. 1 in men's field.

This is a high-leverage afternoon at Exposition Park Stadium, which will be hosting its first Summer Games competition. Expect scoreboard watching all session.
LAC09.potentialContendersIntro: The six men's teams are not confirmed. The list below is speculative, based on rankings and qualification results through 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: No. 1 in men's sixes rankings; a likely medal-round contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, No. 2 in sixes, and 2023 world champion in field after beating Canada.

potentialContenders.name: Haudenosaunee
potentialContenders.note: Took bronze at the 2023 men's field worlds; 2028 participation is still pending IOC approval.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 3 in men's sixes; will need to qualify.

LAC10.blurb:
The last night of the women's round robin decides who plays for gold and bronze the next evening. With six teams, there is little margin for error.

The U.S. and Canada split the last two World Games sixes titles, each beating the other in the final. A third meeting in Los Angeles would be a natural storyline, though no field is set yet.

Evening energy at Exposition Park Stadium makes this one of the tournament's most compelling nights. You will see seeding settled in real time.
LAC10.potentialContendersIntro: Beyond the host United States, the women's field was not decided as of late 2026. These projected contenders reflect 2025 and 2026 results.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host and 2026 Pan-American gold medalist; Marie McCool was named All-World at the 2026 Women's Championship.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Pan-American runner-up and Super Sixes champion in Oshawa; a likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Bronze at the 2025 World Games; beat the Philippines 24-3 at the 2026 Asia-Pacific event.

LAC11.blurb:
Gold and bronze are on the line on the final day of men's lacrosse. It is the closing act of a sport that last awarded Games medals in 1908.

The tournament is a six-team Sixes format, and the round-robin standings feed these two games. Canada beat the U.S. for the 2022 World Games title, and the U.S. won 2026 Pan-American gold over Canada.

The afternoon at Exposition Park Stadium should have a big-game feel. The Haudenosaunee story adds another thread, with their eligibility unconfirmed.
LAC11.potentialContendersIntro: Rosters for 2028 are not set, so these are projected names from the U.S. and Canadian sixes pools. Their selection and the qualification of each country are unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Pat Kavanagh
potentialContenders.note: PLL MVP finalist in the 2025 U.S. Sixes pool; could appear if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Brennan O'Neill
potentialContenders.note: Another PLL MVP finalist in the 2025 U.S. pool; a potential attacking star.

potentialContenders.name: Coulter Mackesy
potentialContenders.note: Led the U.S. with 11 goals and 16 points at the 2025 Atlas Cup; a name to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Jeff Teat
potentialContenders.note: PLL Championship Game MVP on Canada's 2025 Atlas Cup roster; projected if Canada qualifies.

LAC12.blurb:
The first women's lacrosse medals at the Summer Games are awarded on closing night of the tournament. Bronze and gold games make it a historic evening.

The U.S. beat Canada 16-8 for 2025 World Games gold, avenging a 14-12 loss in 2022. A rematch is possible in 2028, though the field is not set.

The late slot at Exposition Park Stadium should bring a charged, nighttime crowd. Medal ceremonies will mark a lasting moment for the sport.
LAC12.potentialContendersIntro: Only the host United States is guaranteed a spot, so these are projected stars based on the 2025 World Games and recent national rosters. Participation is unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Marie McCool
potentialContenders.note: MVP of the 2025 World Games, leading with 32 points; could appear if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Charlotte North
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games World Team honoree and part of the 2025 Atlas Cup roster; a likely contender if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Shea Dolce
potentialContenders.note: Goalkeeper on the 2025 World Games World Team; projected if she makes the roster.

potentialContenders.name: Erica Evans
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Games World Team selection; could feature if Canada qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Brooklyn Walker-Welch
potentialContenders.note: Also made the 2025 World Games World Team; a possible Canadian standout.

MPN01.blurb:
The 2028 Games open with women's modern pentathlon, and the first medal chase starts early on a Saturday morning. This semifinal sets the field for the final two days later.

Eighteen athletes run a four-part sequence: direct-elimination fencing, a head-to-head obstacle race, swimming, then the laser run. The 70m obstacle course with eight obstacles replaces the horse riding last used at Paris 2024.

The storylines are fresh. Egypt's Farida Khalil won the 2025 world title at age 14, while Paris 2024 champion Michelle Gulyás missed those championships through injury. Whether either is in form in 2028 is not yet known.

Valley Complex 2 is a temporary open-air venue in the Sepulveda Basin park. Expect a casual, park-like feel, with other Valley Zone sports close by for a combined trip.
MPN01.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gave Hungary's Michelle Gulyás the gold, and 2025 produced a new world champion in Egypt's Farida Khalil. Qualification for 2028 is not settled, so these names are projections based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Farida Khalil
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 senior world title and the World Cup Final at age 14. A likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Michelle Gulyás
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with a world-record 1,461 points. Missed the 2025 Worlds with injury, so her 2028 form is uncertain.

potentialContenders.name: Blanka Guzi
potentialContenders.note: Fourth at Paris 2024 and world silver medalist in 2025, her second in a row. Projected to be a strong contender.

potentialContenders.name: Aurora Tognetti
potentialContenders.note: Took bronze at the 2025 World Championships, her first major medal. Could be a factor if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Seong Seung-Min
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and reigning world champion going into 2025. Could return in the field if she qualifies.

MPN02.blurb:
Day two of the Games schedule belongs to the men, and the format they face is brand new. This semifinal is where 18 pentathletes try to reach Tuesday's final.

The order is direct-elimination fencing, a head-to-head obstacle race over 70m and eight obstacles, swimming, and finally the laser run. Obstacle racing takes the place of the horse riding last seen at Paris 2024.

Egypt arrives with momentum. Paris 2024 champion Ahmed El-Gendy said he was training for obstacle racing in 2025, and compatriot Moutaz Mohamed won that year's world title. Neither is confirmed for 2028.

The venue is a temporary arena set in a large Valley park. It should feel more like a festival morning than a stadium, with other Valley Zone sports a short trip away.
MPN02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 saw Egypt's Ahmed El-Gendy win gold, ahead of Japan's Taishu Sato and Italy's Giorgio Malan. 2028 rosters are not set, so the following are projections based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Ahmed El-Gendy
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with a world-record 1,555 points. If he qualifies, he is a likely title contender.

potentialContenders.name: Moutaz Mohamed
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 World Cup Final and senior world title, Africa's first individual world champion in the sport. Projected top contender.

potentialContenders.name: Mihaly Koleszar
potentialContenders.note: Ranked world No.2 before the 2025 Worlds and named a leading contender. Could be a factor in 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Giorgio Malan
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Expected to remain a threat if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Taishu Sato
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist. Could return if he qualifies.

MPN03.blurb:
This is the women's medal day, and it is decided in a single morning. The laser run is the finale: the first athlete across the line wins the whole competition.

Eighteen finalists go through direct-elimination fencing, an obstacle race, and swimming before the run. Points convert into head starts, so the finish order is the final order and spectators can see exactly who is leading.

The 2025 season set up a possible generational rivalry between Paris 2024 champion Michelle Gulyás and Egypt's teenage world champion Farida Khalil. Khalil lost to Gulyás in the laser run in Budapest but won the World Cup Final.

At Valley Complex 2 in the Sepulveda Basin, expect a short, intense morning in an open-air setting. The final lasts only two hours, so arrive early.
MPN03.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Hungary's Michelle Gulyás, with France's Élodie Clouvel taking silver and Korea's Seong Seung-Min bronze. For 2028, the names below are projections based on 2025 form and are not confirmed entrants.

potentialContenders.name: Farida Khalil
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion at age 14, with three World Cup golds that year. A projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Michelle Gulyás
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion, and winner of the 2025 Budapest World Cup. An injury kept her out of the 2025 Worlds, so 2028 form is uncertain.

potentialContenders.name: Blanka Guzi
potentialContenders.note: Two-time world silver medalist through 2025 and fourth at Paris 2024. Could challenge for a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Aurora Tognetti
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world bronze medalist. A rising name who could be in contention if she qualifies.

MPN04.blurb:
The final day of modern pentathlon decides the men's champion. It also closes the sport's four-day opening stretch of the 2028 Games, its first start-of-schedule slot since 1992.

Eighteen men start with direct-elimination fencing, then run the obstacle course, swim, and finish with the laser run. The first athlete across the line takes gold.

Egypt holds both the Paris 2024 title through Ahmed El-Gendy and the 2025 world title through Moutaz Mohamed, who won by 17 seconds. France's Rochat and Czechia's Matej Lukes also medaled at the 2025 Worlds.

The setting is a temporary open-air venue in the Sepulveda Basin park. Expect an early-morning crowd, a quick two-hour program, and a clear finish-line moment.
MPN04.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 produced a first African medal in the sport, a gold for Egypt's El-Gendy. The 2028 field is not decided, so these contenders are projected from 2025 results.

potentialContenders.name: Moutaz Mohamed
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion by 17 seconds and World Cup Final winner. A projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Ahmed El-Gendy
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with a world-record 1,555 points. His 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Rochat
potentialContenders.note: Former world junior champion who took world silver in 2025. Could contend if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Matej Lukes
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world bronze medalist and World Cup Final silver medalist. A possible medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Giorgio Malan
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Could return among the contenders if he qualifies.

MTB01.blurb:
One start line, no heats, no second chances. The men's cross-country final on July 17 decides the medals in roughly an hour and a half of racing on a new course in the San Gabriel Valley hills.

Tom Pidcock (GBR) won in Tokyo and Paris, and has said he plans to return to mountain biking before 2028 for a third straight gold. Paris also showed how quickly a puncture can reshape a race.

American interest should be high. Christopher Blevins (USA) won both the 2025 XCO and short track World Cup overall titles, and a home-soil medal bid could become a major storyline.

Industry Hills is built around technical drops, jumps and rough ground. Riders pass several times, so spectators can move between viewing areas along the loop and catch the race at different points.
MTB01.potentialContendersIntro: Pidcock won Paris 2024 gold, with Victor Koretzky (FRA) taking silver and Alan Hatherly (RSA) bronze. The 2028 field is not set, so the names below are projected contenders based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Pidcock
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 and Tokyo 2020 gold medalist and 2026 XCO world champion. He has said he will return to mountain biking before 2028; his participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Alan Hatherly
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and back-to-back XCO world champion in 2024 and 2025. A likely contender if he keeps his focus on mountain biking.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Koretzky
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who won the 2025 short track world title and took XCO world bronze. Projected to be a podium threat again.

potentialContenders.name: Christopher Blevins
potentialContenders.note: Won both the 2025 XCO and XCC World Cup overall titles. If he qualifies, he would be a leading home-soil medal hope.

potentialContenders.name: Charlie Aldridge
potentialContenders.note: Runner-up to Pidcock at the 2026 world championships and winner of the 2025 World Cup finale at Mont-Sainte-Anne. A possible challenger if selected.

MTB02.blurb:
Paris 2024 was decided by margins of almost three minutes, and the women's cross-country final on July 18 could bring a very different kind of race. It is a single mass-start final with no heats on a brand-new course.

Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (FRA) won Paris gold, but no source confirms whether she will defend the title. Haley Batten (USA), the Paris silver medalist, would be racing on home soil if she competes, though her 2028 plans are unconfirmed.

Recent form points to a wide-open field. Jenny Rissveds (SWE) won the 2025 world title and Samara Maxwell (NZL) took the World Cup overall. Savilia Blunk (USA) finished fifth at the 2025 worlds.

The Industry Hills course offers technical drops and jumps, with spectator zones close to the trail. Riders lap the same loop, so fans can reposition and watch the race change shape.
MTB02.potentialContendersIntro: Ferrand-Prévot won Paris 2024 gold, Batten took silver and Rissveds bronze. Who lines up in 2028 is not settled, so these are projected contenders based on recent results.

potentialContenders.name: Jenny Rissveds
potentialContenders.note: Rio 2016 champion and Paris 2024 bronze medalist. She won her first XCO world title in 2025, making her a likely contender if she continues at this level.

potentialContenders.name: Samara Maxwell
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 XCO World Cup overall title and was runner-up at the 2025 world championships. A projected podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Pauline Ferrand-Prévot
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist. No source confirms whether she will defend her title in 2028, so her presence is uncertain.

potentialContenders.name: Haley Batten
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist. A home-soil medal contender if she competes, though her 2028 plans have not been confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Savilia Blunk
potentialContenders.note: Finished fifth at the 2025 XCO world championships, one of the strongest recent U.S. results. A possible home-team presence if she qualifies.

OWS01.blurb:
The first of two ocean-swimming medal races sends the women's field into the Pacific for 10 kilometers of mass-start racing. It is a single final, with no heats and no second chances.

The Paris 2024 champion, Sharon van Rouwendaal of the Netherlands, retired in September 2025, so the title is open. Paris silver medalist Moesha Johnson of Australia and bronze medalist Ginevra Taddeucci of Italy are projected to renew their rivalry, though neither has qualified yet.

Races run just offshore from Belmont Shore in Long Beach, with fans watching from the beach and the area around Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier. Expect a shoreline crowd, swimmers jostling in packs, and ocean conditions that could shape the race.
OWS01.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 went to Sharon van Rouwendaal (NED), Moesha Johnson (AUS) and Ginevra Taddeucci (ITA), but van Rouwendaal has retired. The names below are projections from 2025 form, and none has qualified for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Moesha Johnson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 world 10km champion, the first Australian to win that title. Projected contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Ginevra Taddeucci
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist, 2025 world 10km silver medalist and 2025 World Cup overall winner. Likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Pou
potentialContenders.note: Bronze in the 2025 world 10km, Monaco's first medal at a World Aquatics Championships. A possible podium threat if she qualifies.

OWS02.blurb:
The men's 10km closes out the two-day open water program with another one-shot final in the Pacific. Medals are decided in the water, with 22 swimmers and a maximum of two per nation.

The Paris 2024 podium was Kristof Rasovszky and David Betlehem of Hungary, with Oliver Klemet of Germany in between. Germany's Florian Wellbrock and Italy's Gregorio Paltrinieri went one-two at the 2025 World Championships and are projected contenders, though neither has confirmed participation.

The course runs just off Belmont Shore in Long Beach, close enough for beachgoers to follow the packs. Poor water quality postponed the 2025 world races in Singapore, so conditions could be a storyline.
OWS02.potentialContendersIntro: Rasovszky (HUN) won Paris 2024, ahead of Klemet (GER) and Betlehem (HUN). The 2028 names below are projections based on recent form, and none is confirmed or qualified.

potentialContenders.name: Florian Wellbrock
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 10km champion and winner of the 2025 world 10km, his third world title in the event. Projected contender, not yet confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Gregorio Paltrinieri
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at the 2025 world 10km, his 17th World Championships medal. Could appear in 2028 if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Kristof Rasovszky
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who missed the 2025 world podium. Could return as a contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Kyle Lee
potentialContenders.note: Bronze in the 2025 world 10km, his first individual international medal. A rising name to watch if he qualifies.

RCB01.blurb:
Coastal rowing makes its Games debut on the Long Beach shoreline, and this opening morning is where the solo fields get sorted. Two time trials set the seeding, then the last 16 begins head-to-head knockout racing.

Each race is a sprint across the sand, a 250m slalom row through the surf around two buoys, a 180-degree turn, and a run back up the beach. It is the first time a Games rowing event is raced on open ocean.

Seeding helps but doesn't decide much. At the 2026 world finals, Samuel Forbes was seventh in the time trials and still won men's solo silver. Rough surf and capsizes marked those trials.

Fans watch from the Belmont Shore waterfront near the pier, with the action just offshore. Expect an early-morning, beach-day atmosphere as quota-earning nations, one man and one woman each, take their first strokes.

RCB02.blurb:
Medals are awarded in both solo events in a single afternoon session as the men's and women's solo finals, the last eight in each bracket, decide the first coastal rowing champions in Games history.

The form book is wide open. Chris Bak won men's solo world titles in 2024 and 2025, but 21-year-old Liu Jiayu of China took the 2026 crown after fixing a loose sliding seat mid-final. Samuel Forbes knocked Bak out in the quarterfinals along the way.

The women's side has similar chaos. Isabella Scammell won the 2026 world title, while Magdalena Lobnig, a podium finisher three years in a row, went the wrong way around a buoy in her semifinal.

At Belmont Shore, fans line the sand and the area around the pier as the races unfold just offshore. Sprints, surf and a single missed buzzer can swing a medal.

RCB03.blurb:
The first mixed-gender rowing event in Games history opens with time trials and a last 16 knockout round. It is one woman and one man sharing a double scull through the surf.

Crews race two time trials for seeding before head-to-head racing begins. A run, a 250m slalom row, a turn around the final buoy and a run to the finish must all be coordinated across two athletes.

The field is well worth a look. Lithuania won the 2024 and 2025 world titles, then Germany beat them in 2026. A nation can also enter different athletes than those who earned the quota place, so line-ups could change.

This is a morning session on the Long Beach waterfront, a relaxed way to see the new discipline up close before the final that afternoon.

RCB04.blurb:
These are the first medals ever awarded in a mixed-gender rowing event at the Games. The final eight crews decide who goes into the record books for coastal rowing's newest event.

Teamwork matters here. A woman and a man must pair their sprints and sculling through open-ocean surf, so the crews that look strongest on paper do not always win.

Recent results show how open it is. Lithuania were world champions in 2024 and 2025, and Germany beat them in 2026, with Poland taking its first beach sprint medal in bronze. The USA took silver in 2025.

Belmont Shore gives spectators a close view from the beach and near the pier, as the races end with a sprint up the sand. With the afternoon sun and a home crowd likely, expect a lively finale to the coastal program.

ROW01.blurb:
The regatta opens on Marine Stadium's narrow saltwater channel, with the women's single sculls heats and the men's double sculls and pair heats. Everyone starts here, and no medals are decided yet.

All three events race a historically short 1,500 metres, the shortest course ever used at the Games. Lane draws and quick starts matter more over less distance, and heats put plenty of pressure on early positioning.

The 2025 world champion, Fiona Murtagh of Ireland, is a likely name to watch in the women's single, if she qualifies. Paris 2024 gold went to Karolien Florijn (NED), ahead of Emma Twigg (NZL) and Viktorija Senkutė (LTU).

Spectators watch from the shoreline beside the racing lanes, with Belmont Shore and the Long Beach skyline behind. It is a relaxed late-afternoon introduction to a venue that first hosted Games rowing in 1932.

ROW02.blurb:
Sunday morning brings the men's single sculls heats, the first look at one of rowing's deepest events. The men's double sculls and pair also race semifinals, and the women's double sculls and pair run heats.

The single field is the main draw. Oliver Zeidler (GER) won Paris 2024, Stefanos Ntouskos (GRE) took the 2025 world title, and Zeidler won another world title in 2026, so a Zeidler-Ntouskos rematch looks possible if both qualify.

The men's double and pair semifinals are where finalists are sorted from the rest. Missing the A final over 1,500 metres leaves little room to recover.

Expect a morning crowd on the shoreline with the sun climbing over the Alamitos Bay channel. With five events racing in under two hours, the session moves fast.

potentialContenders.name: Simon van Dorp

ROW03.blurb:
The first medals of the regatta are decided Monday morning, with the men's double sculls and men's pair A, B and C finals. The women's single sculls quarterfinals and the women's double and pair semifinals share the program.

Paris 2024 gold went to Romania in the men's double, with the Netherlands taking silver, and to Croatia in the men's pair. Simon van Dorp (NED) won the 2026 world double sculls title, so the Dutch could be a medal threat again.

In the women's single quarterfinals, the 2025 world champion Fiona Murtagh (IRL) could appear, along with Karolien Florijn (NED), who won Paris 2024.

The finals are short, loud and close to the bank. At Marine Stadium, where 1932 crews once raced four abreast, spectators can watch a medal race from a few steps away.
ROW03.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders are for the men's double sculls final and the women's single sculls quarterfinals. All 2028 participation is projected until qualification ends.

potentialContenders.name: Fiona Murtagh

potentialContenders.name: Lauren Henry

ROW04.blurb:
Tuesday's medal action is in the women's double sculls and women's pair, with A, B and C finals. The session also includes the men's quadruple sculls and four heats and the men's single sculls quarterfinals.

Paris 2024 gave New Zealand gold in the women's double, with Romania second, and the Netherlands gold in the women's pair, again with Romania second. At the 2026 worlds, the United States took pair bronze and a world best time was set in the pair.

The men's four heats are worth watching for the United States, which won Paris 2024 and the 2026 world title. The single sculls quarterfinals could bring Oliver Zeidler (GER) or Stefanos Ntouskos (GRE) back on the water.

Morning racing at Marine Stadium is easy to follow, with finals in close sequence and the course alongside the bank. It is a good day to catch both medal races and heats.

ROW05.blurb:
Wednesday's marquee races are the men's quadruple sculls and men's four A and B finals. The women's quadruple sculls and four heats and the women's single sculls semifinals also run.

The Netherlands won the Paris 2024 men's quad, and the United States won the men's four at Paris and again at the 2026 worlds. Germany won a 2026 worlds quad heat in 6:16.11, ahead of Australia and Poland.

The women's four heats include the United States, whose crew won the 2026 world title in a world best 6:09.87. The single sculls semifinals also show who might be a title favorite, with Fiona Murtagh (IRL) the 2025 world champion.

A four or quad racing over 1,500 metres should be loud and close along the Marine Stadium bank. This is a good day to see crew boats with real medal stakes.

ROW06.blurb:
Thursday's medal races are the women's quadruple sculls and women's four A and B finals. The men's eight heats open the big-boat program, and the men's single sculls semifinals and E and F finals fill out the morning.

Great Britain won the Paris 2024 women's quad, with the Netherlands second, and the Dutch won the women's four. The United States won the 2026 world title in the four in a world best 6:09.87 and took quad bronze.

The men's eight heats matter because the Netherlands won the 2025 world title ahead of Great Britain and the United States. Each crew is trying to avoid the repechage and keep a direct path to the final.

The finals are a clean, quick watch from the bank. A 9:30 start leaves time for the full session before the day warms up.

ROW07.blurb:
Friday brings the men's eight A and B finals, the biggest boat on the Marine Stadium course. The session also has the women's eight heats and the women's single sculls A to D finals.

The Netherlands won the 2025 and 2026 world titles, with Finn Florijn, Wibout Rustenburg and Jonna de Vries among the crew. Great Britain won Paris 2024 with the Dutch second, and the 2025 worlds had Great Britain second and the United States third.

The women's single A final could bring in Fiona Murtagh (IRL), the 2025 world champion, and Karolien Florijn (NED), the Paris 2024 gold medalist, if they qualify. The shorter 1,500 metres may help crews with fast starts.

Eights are the loudest races on the bank, with eight rowers and a coxswain flashing by in seconds. A 10:00 AM start fits a full session before lunch.

ROW08.blurb:
The regatta ends Saturday with the men's single sculls A to D finals and the women's eight A and B finals. It is a short final session, with the last medals on Marine Stadium.

Oliver Zeidler (GER) won Paris 2024, Stefanos Ntouskos (GRE) won the 2025 worlds with Zeidler second, and Zeidler won again in 2026. Yauheni Zalaty (AIN) was Paris silver, and Simon van Dorp (NED) was bronze.

In the women's eight, Romania won Paris 2024 and the 2026 world title, and the United States took 2026 worlds bronze. If those crews hold, it could be a Romania-United States final.

The finale gives a single in the morning light and a big eight on the bank. With Belmont Shore and the Long Beach skyline behind, it is a fitting close to a regatta that began here in 1932.

RU701.blurb:
The women's tournament opens the Games at Carson, and the 12-team field starts pool play here. Six matches in three hours means a steady stream of tries, with every result feeding quarterfinal seeding.

New Zealand arrives as two-time defending champion after Tokyo and a 19-12 comeback win over Canada in the Paris 2024 final. The United States is in as host and Paris 2024 bronze medalist. The other teams and pool draws are not yet confirmed.

Carson Stadium is a soccer-specific bowl of about 27,000 seats, so even the cheap seats sit close to the touchline. Morning pool play is a relaxed way to see several teams in one sitting.
