RU702.blurb:
Evening pool play brings the first big home-crowd moment, as the host nation is likely to be on the pitch in a session like this. The exact schedule of who plays when has not been confirmed.

The United States is the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, and Ilona Maher's profile made that team a major story. Maher has also played fifteens, including the 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup, and had not publicly decided on a 2028 sevens spot.

The stadium sits in the South Bay, and the evening session should have a louder, more festive feel than the morning games. Expect families, club-rugby crowds, and plenty of casual fans seeing the sport for the first time.

RU703.blurb:
This is the last day of pool play, and the stakes are higher. When these six matches finish, the standings are set and the quarterfinal lineup for the afternoon is locked.

Teams that miss the cut drop into the 9-12 classification bracket, so even a mid-table team has plenty to play for. Seven-minute halves mean one slip can end a medal hope.

The morning sun at Carson suits a rugby crowd with picnic energy. Seats close to the pitch let you hear the collisions and the calls between players.

RU704.blurb:
Knockout rugby begins. Four quarterfinals decide who stays in the medal chase, while the 9-12 matches settle the bottom of the table.

With two seven-minute halves, a single try can swing a match. In Paris 2024, New Zealand, Canada, the United States and Australia all reached the semifinals, and any of them could again be in the mix.

This session has an elimination feel, with the crowd leaning into every turnover. A U.S. quarterfinal at home would likely be one of the loudest of the afternoon.

RU705.blurb:
Two semifinals decide who plays for gold and who drops to the bronze match. The 5-8 and 9-12 placing matches fill the early part of the afternoon.

At Paris 2024, New Zealand and Canada won their semifinals to reach the final, while the United States lost its semifinal and then won bronze. If the host reaches this stage in 2028, it would be playing a semifinal at home.

The afternoon crowd at Carson should be at its fullest yet. With the medal matches only hours away, the atmosphere tightens as the day goes on.

RU706.blurb:
Gold arrives early at these Games. The women's final and bronze match close out the first rugby sevens medals of 2028, before the men begin.

New Zealand won in Tokyo and again in Paris 2024, coming from behind to beat Canada 19-12. A win here would be a third straight title. The U.S. won its first sevens medal in Paris 2024, a last-second 14-12 bronze win over Australia.

The 5-8 games lead into the evening medal matches under the Carson lights. Medal finishes in sevens often come down to the final seconds, and the closeness of the seats should bring the noise.

RU707.blurb:
The men take over the field on Sunday morning. Twelve teams open pool play with six matches, setting up a three-day sprint to the gold medal match.

France is the defending champion after a 28-7 win over Fiji in Paris 2024, and Fiji's silver ended its unbeaten Games record. South Africa took bronze, and the United States qualifies automatically as host.

The sport has a reputation for fast, open play and loud crowds, and the stadium's close seating keeps the action near the touchline. It is an easy way to catch several teams in a short window.

RU708.blurb:
Evening pool play on the opening men's day is where the host crowd is most likely to show up in force. The evening schedule is ideal for fans who want rugby after work.

France enters as champion, and Antoine Dupont's two tries and an assist off the bench in the Paris 2024 final are part of that story. Dupont returned to fifteens and suffered a serious knee injury in March 2025, and had not publicly committed to a 2028 sevens comeback.

The United States is in as host, and a men's team with no Games medal has a strong incentive to make noise at home. Seats at Carson are close to the action, so the hits are heard as well as seen.

RU709.blurb:
Pool play ends here, and the men's quarterfinal lineup gets locked in. After this session, every team knows whether it is in the title chase or heading for the 9-12 bracket.

The pressure builds quickly, since a slow start can cost a team its seeding. The final pool lineups depend on qualification that finishes after the 2027 SVNS World Championship, regional events, and the repechage.

Recent history gives the session extra interest. Fiji won the first two men's golds, in Rio 2016 and Tokyo, before France won in Paris 2024.
RU709.potentialContendersIntro: With the field not yet finalized, these are projections based on Paris 2024 medalists and recent form. The United States is confirmed as host.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and defending champion.

potentialContenders.name: Fiji
potentialContenders.note: Winner of the first two men's golds and Paris 2024 silver medalist.

potentialContenders.name: South Africa
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist; projected to contend.

potentialContenders.name: United States
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, qualified automatically.

RU710.blurb:
Monday afternoon is the men's elimination session, with four quarterfinals plus the 9-12 classification matches. Win and you are one game from a medal match; lose and you drop into the 5-8 bracket.

France won in Paris 2024 by beating Fiji 28-7, and South Africa took bronze. Fiji's loss in that final was its first defeat at the Games after golds in Rio 2016 and Tokyo.

If the United States reaches this stage, it would play a quarterfinal in front of a home crowd. The crowd here should be big, and a close finish could bring the stadium to its feet.
RU710.potentialContendersIntro: The men's quarterfinal field is not yet set, so this is a projection from Paris 2024 and recent form. Only the United States is confirmed, as host.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Defending champion; a projected quarterfinalist if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Fiji
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and a perennial favorite.

potentialContenders.name: South Africa
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist; projected to contend.

potentialContenders.name: United States
potentialContenders.note: Host nation; would play any quarterfinal at home.

RU711.blurb:
The men's semifinals decide who plays for gold on the final night. The 5-8 and 9-12 placing matches fill out the early afternoon.

South Africa won the 2025/26 SVNS series, beating Fiji 10-7 in the New York final in March 2026. Together with France, the defending champion, they are projected to contend, though qualification for the 2028 field is not yet settled.

The afternoon crowd should be loud, with some fans staying for the night medal matches. Sevens semifinals can swing on a single try, which makes this one of the most tense sessions of the tournament.
RU711.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 men's rosters are confirmed, so these players are projections based on Paris 2024 and recent SVNS form. Each would have to be selected and healthy.

potentialContenders.name: Antoine Dupont
potentialContenders.note: Scored two tries off the bench in the Paris 2024 final; had not publicly committed to a 2028 sevens return after a March 2025 knee injury.

potentialContenders.name: Selvyn Davids

potentialContenders.name: Jerry Tuwai
potentialContenders.note: Fiji's long-time leader; his 2028 availability is uncertain given his age.

RU712.blurb:
The final night of rugby sevens at the 2028 Games ends with the men's bronze and gold medal matches, after the 5-8 placing games.

France is defending champion after beating Fiji 28-7 in Paris 2024. Fiji won gold in Rio 2016 and Tokyo, and South Africa took bronze in Paris 2024 before winning the 2025/26 SVNS series with a 10-7 defensive win over Fiji. The United States has never won a men's sevens medal at the Games.

The tournament closes under the Carson lights. Paris 2024 set attendance records at the Stade de France, so expect a big crowd for the finale.
RU712.potentialContendersIntro: Medal matchups for 2028 are not known, so these players are projections tied to Paris 2024 form and the 2025/26 SVNS season. Each would need to be selected and healthy.

potentialContenders.name: Antoine Dupont
potentialContenders.note: Two tries and an assist off the bench in the Paris 2024 final; his 2028 sevens return has not been confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Selvyn Davids

potentialContenders.name: Siviwe Soyizwapi
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist; could appear if South Africa reaches a medal match.

potentialContenders.name: Jerry Tuwai
potentialContenders.note: Fiji's veteran leader; whether he competes in 2028 is uncertain.

SAL01.blurb:
The sailing program starts here, on the Long Beach waterfront, with the opening day of the kite qualification series. Men and women race in a foiling format that only debuted at Paris 2024.

Qualifying days sort the field before the medal rounds. It is an accessible, low-pressure way to see riders launch off the line at speed and learn the format before the stakes rise.

The races run just offshore from Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier, so spectators on the sand can follow the action close to the beach. Long Beach also hosted sailing at the 1984 Los Angeles Games.
SAL01.potentialContendersIntro: The 2025 Formula Kite World Championships offer the best current form guide. Who actually qualifies for 2028 is still undetermined, so these names are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Riccardo Pianosi
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 Formula Kite men's world title in Sardinia. A likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Max Maeder
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2025 Worlds silver medalist. Expected to be a front-runner if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Jessie Kampman
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 women's world title, her first, and has represented the Netherlands since July 2025.

potentialContenders.name: Daniela Moroz
potentialContenders.note: Six-time Formula Kite world champion and 2025 Worlds bronze medalist. A projected home-nation favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Lauriane Nolot
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 Worlds silver medalist. A likely women's contender.

SAL02.blurb:
Two disciplines share the water today. Windsurfing racing begins at Belmont Shore while the kite fleet moves into its second qualification day.

The windsurfers sail the iQFOiL class, which has resized its sails for this cycle. Men now use 8 square meter sails and women a new 7.3 square meter design, intended to level the field across body types.

These are the first windsurfing races on the revised gear, so the early results will show who has adapted fastest. The kite fleet continues its own sorting for finals day.

An afternoon session here suits fans who want to see both foiling disciplines in one visit. Racing happens close to shore, and the pier area is a natural place to watch.
SAL02.potentialContendersIntro: For windsurfing, the 2025 iQFOiL World Championship in Aarhus gives the latest form. Who qualifies for 2028 is not yet known, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Emma Wilson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist who won the 2025 iQFOiL world title, her first. A likely women's contender.

potentialContenders.name: Andy Brown
potentialContenders.note: Won the men's 2025 iQFOiL world title in Aarhus. Projected to be a podium threat if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Arnoux
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at the 2025 iQFOiL Worlds after leading the men's fleet on day three.

potentialContenders.name: Kiran Badloe
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champion who sat second after day three at the 2025 Worlds. Could return to the mix if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tamar Steinberg
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at the 2025 iQFOiL Worlds. A possible women's medal contender.

SAL03.blurb:
The third kite qualification day arrives with finals just a day away. Riders are jockeying for position, and each race can reshape the standings.

Windsurfing holds its second day of racing alongside. Both fleets are still in the sorting phase, so this is a good session to see the field before medal races narrow it.

Plenty of storylines are in play. Reigning men's windsurfing champion Tom Reuveny has a four-year sponsorship backing his run toward 2028. Kite's top riders are trying to peak for the following day.

The racecourse sits just off the beach near Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier. That makes it easy to follow the action from the shoreline as the late-afternoon wind builds.
SAL03.potentialContendersIntro: With kite finals the next day, this session is about the kite qualifiers. The names below are projections based on the 2025 Formula Kite Worlds, not confirmed 2028 entries.

potentialContenders.name: Daniela Moroz
potentialContenders.note: Six-time Formula Kite world champion and 2025 Worlds bronze medalist. A home-nation contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Toni Vodišek
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's silver medalist who was tied for second after day four of the 2025 Worlds.

potentialContenders.name: Max Maeder
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2025 Worlds silver medalist. Likely to be among the men's front-runners if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Jessie Kampman
potentialContenders.note: 2025 women's world champion, projected to be among the top women's riders.

SAL04.blurb:
The first sailing medals of the 2028 Games are decided here. Men's and women's kite finals close out the session at Belmont Shore.

Paris 2024 champions Valentin Bontus of Austria and Ellie Aldridge of Britain would be the defending names, if they qualify. The 2025 world titles went to Italy's Riccardo Pianosi and Jessie Kampman, who now represents the Netherlands.

The World Championships used a medal series format and saw heavy pressure in the finale. Expect similar tension in a final with shifting leads.

Kite races run close to the beach, so fans on the sand can follow the action up close. Windsurfing also wraps up its qualification series in the same session, with medals the next day.
SAL04.potentialContendersIntro: The 2025 Formula Kite Worlds set the current pecking order. Which riders actually reach the 2028 final is unknown, so these are projected contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Riccardo Pianosi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 men's world champion in Sardinia. A likely men's contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Max Maeder
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2025 Worlds silver medalist. Expected to challenge for a medal if he competes.

potentialContenders.name: Jessie Kampman
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 women's world title, her first. A projected women's favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Daniela Moroz
potentialContenders.note: Six-time world champion and 2025 bronze medalist. Could be the home crowd's favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Ellie Aldridge
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's gold medalist. A defending champion who would be in the mix if she qualifies.

SAL05.blurb:
Windsurfing medals are decided today, the day after the kite finals. Men's and women's iQFOiL finals close out the board sailing program at Belmont Shore.

These will be the first Games medal races on the class's new sails: 8 square meters for men and a newly designed 7.3 square meters for women.

The 2025 World Championships in Aarhus used a quarterfinal, semifinal and final medal series. Expect a similar knockout feel, with sailors tested in gusty breeze.

It is a short afternoon session, which makes it easy to catch. Racing runs just offshore, so shoreline viewers near the pier see the foiling boards at close range.
SAL05.potentialContendersIntro: Tom Reuveny of Israel and Marta Maggetti of Italy are the Paris 2024 champions. Who qualifies and reaches the final in 2028 is not yet known, so the others here are projections based on 2025 form.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Reuveny
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's gold medalist. Backed by a four-year sponsorship toward 2028, though qualification is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Andy Brown
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 men's iQFOiL world title. A likely men's contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Arnoux

potentialContenders.name: Marta Maggetti

potentialContenders.name: Emma Wilson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2025 world champion. A projected women's medal contender.

SAL06.blurb:
The sailing programme at the Port of Los Angeles begins here, with the men's and women's one-person dinghy fleets starting their qualification series. Nobody wins a medal today, but the standings start to take shape.

The ILCA 7 and ILCA 6 are single-handed boats, so every result comes down to one sailor's tactics, fitness and nerve. Fleet racing means a single bad start can cost real points.

The harbor sits in San Pedro Bay, the same waters that hosted the 1932 regatta. Spectators watch from shore with working container-port cranes and ships behind the racecourse, a backdrop few regattas offer.
SAL06.potentialContendersIntro: Recent world champions are the early names to follow in the dinghy fleets, though 2028 rosters and qualification are still being settled.

potentialContenders.name: Willem Wiersema
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 ILCA 7 World Championship in Qingdao, one point clear of Pavlos Kontides. Projected contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 ILCA 7 Worlds in Dún Laoghaire, Hungary's first title in the event. A likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Charlotte Rose
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 ILCA 6 Worlds on Dublin Bay, the first non-European winner in 20 years. A potential home favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Louise Cervera

SAL07.blurb:
Day two widens the field. The one-person dinghies continue their qualification series, while the mixed two-person dinghy (470) and mixed multihull (Nacra 17) fleets start racing for the first time.

The Nacra 17 is the one to watch for spectacle. At the 2025 worlds, medal races were sailed on foiling catamarans at more than 20 knots in rough seas.

The 470 is a very different test, with a helm and crew working in tight sync. Both mixed events are open and unsettled: Britain's Gimson and Burnet won the 2025 Nacra 17 title, but a first-time champion took the 2026 crown.

From the shoreline, the harbor course keeps boats close enough to follow the starts and mark roundings without binoculars.
SAL07.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders below are for the mixed Nacra 17 and 470 events. These are projections from recent world championship form, and none are confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 Nacra 17 Worlds, their third title in the class, then took bronze at the 2026 Worlds. Likely contenders if they continue.

potentialContenders.name: Jordi Xammar / Marta Cardona
potentialContenders.note: 2025 470 world champions in Gdynia. Projected medal contenders if they compete.

potentialContenders.name: Martin Wrigley / Bettine Harris
potentialContenders.note: Led most of the final race at the 2025 470 Worlds but finished third. Could be a contender.

SAL08.blurb:
The skiffs arrive. The men's 49er and women's 49erFX open their series today, joining the ongoing dinghy, mixed dinghy and multihull racing for the busiest day of the prelim stretch so far.

Skiffs are fast, twitchy and physically demanding, with two-person crews trapezing off the wing in the breeze. Capsizes and big comebacks are part of the show.

The men's skiff has a clear storyline. Spain won Paris 2024 gold, New Zealand took silver and the United States took bronze, and the Spanish crew won the 2025 world title while the Kiwis took 2026.

Four classes racing in one afternoon give the harbor a lively feel, with plenty of boats to watch.

SAL09.blurb:
This is the first medal day of the dinghy classes. The men's and women's one-person dinghy finals decide gold, silver and bronze, with skiffs on day two and the mixed boats on day three.

Both ILCA fields have been unpredictable lately. The men's world title changed hands in 2025 and 2026, and the 2026 worlds were decided under sailing's new finals format.

Home interest could run high in the women's fleet. American Charlotte Rose won the 2026 ILCA 6 Worlds, which would make her a contender if she qualifies.

Be in the harbor early. Medal racing is where tactical duels play out in the open, and the shoreline gives a close view of the finish.
SAL09.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the men's ILCA 7 and women's ILCA 6 finals. Matt Wearn and Marit Bouwmeester won at Paris 2024, but 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Matt Wearn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's one-person dinghy gold medalist. Could defend if he qualifies and stays in the class.

potentialContenders.name: Willem Wiersema
potentialContenders.note: 2025 ILCA 7 world champion, one point ahead of Pavlos Kontides. A projected medal contender.

potentialContenders.name: Jonatán Vadnai

potentialContenders.name: Marit Bouwmeester

SAL10.blurb:
Two more golds go on the line today. The mixed two-person dinghy (470) and mixed multihull (Nacra 17) hold their finals, while the skiffs race their third day.

The Nacra 17 final is the highlight, with foiling catamarans lifting out of the water at high speed. Italy won at Paris 2024, but Britain's Gimson and Burnet won the 2025 world title and the class has since crowned a new champion.

The 470 offers a contrast. Austria won Paris 2024 gold, and Spain's Xammar and Cardona overtook a leading British pair on the final leg to win the 2025 worlds.

With medals on the water and the skiffs still racing, it is a full late afternoon of action in San Pedro Bay.
SAL10.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the mixed Nacra 17 and mixed 470 finals. These are projections from recent form, since 2028 crews are not confirmed.

SAL11.blurb:
The sailing finale. The men's skiff (49er) and women's skiff (49erFX) medals are the last decided in sailing, closing the regatta on July 28 at the Port of Los Angeles.

The skiffs are the fastest, most athletic boats in the regatta, and a final can swing on one gust or one capsize. The shorter 2:00-5:00 PM window is built around the climax.

The men's field looks open. Spain won Paris 2024 gold, New Zealand silver and the United States bronze, and Spain's Botín and Trittel won the 2025 world title. The Kiwi pair of Menzies and Lee Rush won in 2026.

It is a good ticket for fans who want a medal outcome in a harbor setting, with the last finishes close to shore.
SAL11.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the men's 49er and women's 49erFX finals. They are projections from recent world championship results, not confirmed 2028 crews.

SHO01.blurb:
Two events share one long day in Long Beach: women's and men's 10m air rifle, each run as a qualification round followed by a medal final. It is the first shooting medal session of the 2028 Games.

Air rifle is a game of tiny margins, with final shots scored in tenths of a point. Paris 2024 went to China's Sheng Lihao in the men's event and South Korea's Ban Hyo-Jin in the women's.

The temporary indoor range sits inside the Long Beach Convention Center, with marked lanes and a hushed, tense atmosphere. Expect polite applause after each shot and a roar when a final tightens.
SHO01.potentialContendersIntro: Ban Hyojin and Sheng Lihao are Paris 2024 champions, and 2025 world champions Ban and Maximilian Dallinger show how open the field is. Who actually competes in 2028 depends on qualification, which starts in Doha in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Elavenil Valarivan

SHO02.blurb:
Men's and women's 10m air pistol fill this Sunday session, each with a qualification round and a final. Pistol fans get a full day of one-handed precision at the Long Beach waterfront.

China's Xie Yu won the men's title at Paris 2024. South Korea's Oh Ye-Jin and Kim Ye-Ji went one-two in the women's event, with India's Manu Bhaker taking bronze.

The venue is a temporary indoor range in a convention hall, so the mood is quiet and focused rather than boisterous. It is a close-up view of a sport decided by steady hands.
SHO02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 medalists lead the projected field, though none of their 2028 spots are confirmed. Qualification begins at the 2026 World Championship in Doha.

SHO03.blurb:
The skeet competition opens here, with men and women shooting qualification on the first of two days. It is a long, steady morning-to-afternoon grind where nobody wins a medal yet, but a bad round can end a run.

The 2028 format sends the top eight from qualification into the final, up from six at Paris 2024. The rest of qualification is shot on day 2.

Whittier Narrows is an open-air range in parkland, with temporary stands behind the stations holding about 2,000. Expect hushed concentration, the crack of the shots and clay targets crossing the fields.
SHO03.potentialContendersIntro: Americans have momentum after going one-two in men's skeet at Paris 2024 and sweeping the men's medals at the 2025 World Cup Final. Who actually qualifies for 2028 is still open, so these names are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Vincent Hancock
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's skeet gold medalist and 2025 world champion. He has said he intends to go for a fifth gold in 2028, but a spot is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Christian Elliott
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 World Cup Final in Doha ahead of Hancock. A likely contender for a U.S. spot if he keeps his form.

potentialContenders.name: Samantha Simonton

potentialContenders.name: Francisca Crovetto

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Yiting

SHO04.blurb:
Mixed team air rifle and air pistol arrive with a new twist. The top four qualifying teams in each event go into one combined medal final using elimination, replacing the separate gold and bronze matches from Paris 2024.

The format should mean fewer lulls and a sharper climb in tension, since every finalist is on the line together. Qualification still decides who gets there.

At Paris 2024, China beat South Korea for air rifle gold and Serbia took air pistol gold ahead of Türkiye, with India's Manu Bhaker part of the bronze. In Long Beach, expect a compact evening session in a convention hall where elimination drama is easy to follow.
SHO04.potentialContendersIntro: These teams are projected from Paris 2024 and 2025 form; actual 2028 pairings are not set. The list covers both mixed team events.

SHO05.blurb:
Skeet medals are decided in a single day. The final stretch of qualification comes first, then eight finalists shoot for gold, silver and bronze in both the men's and women's events.

The headline storyline is Vincent Hancock. After Paris 2024 he said he had expected to retire but could not pass up a home Games, and a fifth men's skeet gold would be a Games first. His place is not guaranteed.

The women's field looks wide open, with the Paris 2024 champion and the current world champion both likely names to watch. The temporary stands at Whittier Narrows put you right behind the stations for the elimination-style finish.
SHO05.potentialContendersIntro: These contenders are projections based on recent form. The 2028 rosters are not set, and the men's and women's finals are both in this session.

potentialContenders.note: Won Paris 2024 gold, hitting 58 of 60 in the final, and the 2025 world title. He also won the 2026 U.S. national title and is a projected contender if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Conner Prince
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist behind Hancock in Paris 2024 and a member of the 2026 U.S. national team. A potential home medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Samantha Simonton
potentialContenders.note: 2025 women's skeet world champion and World Cup Final silver medalist. Projected to be among the home favorites.

potentialContenders.name: Francisca Crovetto
potentialContenders.note: Reigning Paris 2024 women's skeet champion. Could appear if she qualifies for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Amber Rutter
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's skeet silver medalist. A possible finalist if she qualifies.

SHO06.blurb:
The men's 50m rifle 3 positions is the long-form test of rifle shooting. Athletes shoot kneeling, prone and standing, then the best advance to a final.

The final has a new look for 2028. Kneeling and prone are merged into one time-limited phase where athletes choose when to switch, and standing plus elimination rounds still decide the medals.

China's Liu Yukun won at Paris 2024 and again at the 2025 Worlds with 467.1, just 0.2 ahead of India's Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar. Expect a morning session in a quiet hall, with rhythm and nerves on show.
SHO06.potentialContendersIntro: Liu Yukun is the Paris 2024 champion and 2025 world champion, but 2028 spots are still to be earned. Qualification opens at the 2026 World Championship in Doha.

potentialContenders.name: Liu Yukun
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion and 2025 world champion with 467.1; a projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar
potentialContenders.note: Took silver at the 2025 Worlds on 466.9 after a late challenge; a likely contender if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Romain Aufrere
potentialContenders.note: Bronze medalist at Cairo 2025 and part of France's world-title team; a possible finalist.

potentialContenders.name: Jon-Hermann Hegg
potentialContenders.note: Shot 592 in qualification at Cairo 2025; could appear in 2028 if Norway qualifies him.

SHO07.blurb:
The women's 50m rifle 3 positions asks for patience across three positions and a long final. This morning session runs both qualification and the medal final.

The 2028 final merges kneeling and prone into one timed phase, and athletes decide when to change position. Standing and elimination still settle the podium.

Switzerland's Chiara Leone won at Paris 2024 ahead of the USA's Sagen Maddalena. Maddalena's silver adds a home-nation angle, if she qualifies, to a calm, technical morning in Long Beach.
SHO07.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 medalists set the benchmark, but 2028 fields are not set. Qualification starts at the 2026 World Championship in Doha.

potentialContenders.name: Chiara Leone
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion; a projected contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sagen Maddalena
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist; a home-crowd storyline if she makes the US team.

potentialContenders.name: Ashi Chouksey
potentialContenders.note: Placed 15th in qualification at Cairo 2025 and missed the final; a speculative name to watch.

SHO08.blurb:
Trap shooting begins here, with women and men shooting the first day of qualification. This is an accessible way to see the sport at work before the medal day.

The 2028 trap final takes eight athletes, not six. Day 1 is where shooters need a clean, steady score to stay in the hunt for a top-eight spot.

Whittier Narrows is a public clay range in the San Gabriel Valley, and the 2028 setup adds expanded temporary seating. Trap targets fly away from the shooter, so you can follow each flight from the stands.
SHO08.potentialContendersIntro: Trap has been open lately. Croatia's Josip Glasnovic and Spain's Mar Molne Magrina are the reigning 2025 world champions, and the 2028 fields are still projections.

potentialContenders.name: Josip Glasnovic
potentialContenders.note: 2025 men's trap world champion in a field of 133. Croatia also won the 2025 team title, so he is a likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Will Hinton
potentialContenders.note: Won men's trap at the 2025 World Cup Final. A projected home-nation contender if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Mar Molne Magrina
potentialContenders.note: 2025 women's trap world champion. Could appear if she secures a Spanish spot.

potentialContenders.name: Silvana Stanco
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 World Cup Final winner. A likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Nathan Hales
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's trap champion. He placed 78th in qualification at the 2025 Worlds, so his 2028 form is a question mark.

SHO09.blurb:
This is a qualifying day for two pistol events: stage 1 of the men's 25m rapid fire and the precision stage of the women's 25m pistol. Both finish the next day.

Rapid fire is a different tempo from air pistol, with quick bursts at fast-turning targets. For 2028 the men's final grows from six to eight shooters, so more athletes get a shot at the medal round.

It is a good entry point for fans who want a lower-stakes look at the discipline. The convention hall setting makes it easy to follow along from the stands.
SHO09.potentialContendersIntro: This session decides positions rather than medals. Projected names come from Paris 2024 and the 2025 World Championship, but 2028 participation depends on qualification.

potentialContenders.name: Clement Beseguet
potentialContenders.note: 2025 men's rapid fire world champion; a likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Anish Bhanwala
potentialContenders.note: Silver at Cairo 2025 after surviving four shoot-offs; a possible finalist.

potentialContenders.name: Li Yuehong
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's rapid fire champion; his 2028 place is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Yang Jiin
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 and 2025 world champion in the women's 25m pistol; a projected contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Yao Qianxun
potentialContenders.note: Silver in the 2025 world 25m pistol final; could be a threat if she qualifies.

SHO10.blurb:
Trap medal day. Qualification wraps up in the morning, then eight women and eight men go to the line in their separate finals for gold, silver and bronze.

The finals are stacked with recent history. Great Britain's Nathan Hales won Paris 2024 with a Games-record final, missing only two of 50, and Guatemala's Adriana Ruano won her country's first gold. Neither is guaranteed a 2028 place.

The Whittier Narrows stands sit behind the shooters, so you hear the call, the shot and the crowd's reaction in quick succession. A single miss can change the final order.
SHO10.potentialContendersIntro: These names mix Paris 2024 medalists and 2025 results with projections. Trap quota places open at the November 2026 World Championship in Doha, so the 2028 field is not yet set.

potentialContenders.name: Josip Glasnovic
potentialContenders.note: 2025 men's trap world champion. A projected medal contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Will Hinton
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 World Cup Final and led the U.S. to 2025 team silver. A likely home-crowd favorite if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Nathan Hales
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's trap gold medalist and Great Britain's first trap champion since 1968. His 2028 status depends on qualifying.

potentialContenders.name: Adriana Ruano
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's trap gold medalist. Could return if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Silvana Stanco
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, 2025 world silver medalist and World Cup Final winner. Mar Molne Magrina of Spain, the 2025 world champion, is another name to watch.

SHO11.blurb:
This long Sunday session has the finish for two events. The men's 25m rapid fire pistol completes stage 2 and its final, while the women's 25m pistol finishes qualification and then shoots its final.

The men's final now has eight shooters instead of six, giving the showdown a bigger field. Hits are counted quickly, and shoot-offs can decide medals.

Paris 2024 gave China's Li Yuehong the men's rapid fire title and South Korea's Yang Jiin the women's. For a ticket buyer, this is a full day of pistol action ending in two medal rounds.
SHO11.potentialContendersIntro: Names below are projected from Paris 2024 and the 2025 World Championship in Cairo, not confirmed entrants. They cover both the men's rapid fire and women's 25m pistol finals.

potentialContenders.name: Clement Beseguet
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 men's rapid fire world title with 31 hits; a likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Li Yuehong
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion in men's rapid fire pistol; 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Yang Jiin
potentialContenders.note: Won Paris 2024 and the 2025 world title in women's 25m pistol; a projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Yao Qianxun
potentialContenders.note: Runner-up to Yang at Cairo 2025 after a three-gold championship; a possible challenger.

potentialContenders.name: Camille Jedrzejewski
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's 25m pistol silver medalist; could return if she qualifies.

SHO12.blurb:
Mixed team trap is new to the 2028 Games, replacing the one-time mixed skeet event from Paris 2024. Teams of one woman and one man shoot qualification, and the top four advance to the final.

The final is also new. Instead of separate gold and bronze matches, all four teams shoot together, which ISSF says keeps every medal contender in the contest to the end.

That should make for a clear storyline from the stands at Whittier Narrows. Skeet shooters have called the switch disappointing, so this event is a fresh test for many trap specialists.
SHO12.potentialContendersIntro: Italy won the 2025 world mixed trap title, and the USA took bronze. No quota places for mixed trap are awarded at the 2026 Worlds, so the 2028 pairings are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Massimo Fabbrizi
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world mixed team trap title with Alessia Iezzi. A projected leader of the Italian pairing if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Alessia Iezzi
potentialContenders.note: Fabbrizi's partner in the 2025 world title win, when they topped qualification with 145. Could appear for Italy in 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Walton Eller
potentialContenders.note: Won 2025 world mixed trap bronze, his first world medal in trap. A possible home-team shooter.

potentialContenders.name: Ava Downs
potentialContenders.note: Won her first world medal at age 20 in the 2025 mixed trap bronze. A potential U.S. contender.

potentialContenders.name: Alessandra Perilli
potentialContenders.note: Won 2025 world silver with Gian Marco Berti after a four-way shoot-off. San Marino could be a dangerous finalist if the pair qualifies.

SKB01.blurb:
Street skateboarding's women's field gets cut down here, with 22 skaters chasing a place in the final. It is an accessible way into the sport, with heats and tricks coming one after another.

The field is likely to be deep and young. Ibuki Matsumoto (JPN), who won the world title in Sao Paulo in March 2026, is the projected headliner if she qualifies. Paris 2024 champion Coco Yoshizawa is also expected to be in the mix.

The temporary, open-air venue sits in the Sepulveda Basin in Encino, near where the 405 and 101 meet. This is the first time the San Fernando Valley has hosted Games events, and the early evening session runs into dusk.
SKB01.potentialContendersIntro: Places are decided by the World Skateboarding Ranking, so the 2028 field is not set. Based on 2025-26 results, these skaters are projected contenders if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Ibuki Matsumoto
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion from Sao Paulo (March 2026) and world No. 1 going into qualifying; won her first World Skateboarding Tour title at age 13 in Kitakyushu.

potentialContenders.name: Chloe Covell
potentialContenders.note: Won the Rome street World Cup in both 2025 and 2026, scoring 177.01 in the 2026 final; a likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Coco Yoshizawa
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and world championships bronze medalist in 2026; her form has been uneven since, so her 2028 spot is not guaranteed.

potentialContenders.name: Rayssa Leal
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and four-time SLS Super Crown winner through December 2025; a likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Yumeka Oda
potentialContenders.note: Runner-up at Kitakyushu 2025 and Rome 2026; a projected finalist if she makes Japan's team.

SKB02.blurb:
Men's street is where the tricks get technical, with 22 skaters putting down runs and tricks on a course built for stair sets, rails and ledges. Only the strongest advance to the final.

Japan arrives as the projected powerhouse. Toa Sasaki defended his world title in Sao Paulo, and Sora Shirai won Rome in 2025 and 2026. Two-time Games champion Yuto Horigome has had a rougher recent stretch.

American interest centers on whether Nyjah Huston and Jagger Eaton qualify. Huston fractured his skull and eye socket in a January 2026 crash, but has said he is aiming for 2028.

This is a morning session at an open-air temporary venue in the Sepulveda Basin. It is a relaxed way to see the full field before the final.
SKB02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 medalists Yuto Horigome, Jagger Eaton and Nyjah Huston are confirmed past results, not 2028 selections. The names below are projected contenders based on recent form and rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Toa Sasaki
potentialContenders.note: Defended his world title in Sao Paulo (March 2026) with 174.10; a projected favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sora Shirai
potentialContenders.note: Won the Rome World Cup in 2025 and 2026, and was third at the 2026 world championships; a likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Ginwoo Onodera
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 SLS Super Crown at age 15; a rising talent to watch if Japan selects him.

potentialContenders.name: Yuto Horigome
potentialContenders.note: Won gold at Paris 2024 for his second straight Games title, though he went out early at the 2025 and 2026 events listed; his 2028 place is unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Nyjah Huston
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist who has said he is aiming for 2028 after a serious January 2026 crash; participation is uncertain.

SKB03.blurb:
This is the women's street medal session, held in the evening with a start around 8:30 pm. The prelims narrow the field to the top skaters, and everything is decided over a short, high-pressure final.

Recent finals have often come down to the last trick. Ibuki Matsumoto won Kitakyushu 2025 with her third and final trick, beating Yumeka Oda by 0.22 points, so a close finish is plausible here.

The podium could come from several countries. Japan and Brazil took all three Paris 2024 medals, while Chloe Covell (AUS) has been the strongest recent winner, taking Rome 2026 by more than 20 points.

The open-air venue in the Sepulveda Basin puts the crowd close to the course. Expect a loud, hopeful evening atmosphere.
SKB03.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Coco Yoshizawa, silver to Liz Akama and bronze to Rayssa Leal. The 2028 finalists are not yet known; these are projected contenders based on 2025-26 results.

potentialContenders.name: Ibuki Matsumoto
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion and world No. 1 entering the qualifying period; a projected medal favorite if she competes.

potentialContenders.name: Chloe Covell
potentialContenders.note: Won the Rome World Cup in 2025 and 2026, with a 177.01 final score in 2026, so a likely podium contender.

potentialContenders.name: Yumeka Oda
potentialContenders.note: Second at both Kitakyushu 2025 and Rome 2026; a consistent finalist who could challenge for a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Rayssa Leal
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and four-time SLS Super Crown winner; fourth at the 2026 world championships, but a strong closer in finals if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Coco Yoshizawa
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion and 2026 world championships bronze medalist; could return to the podium if she qualifies.

SKB04.blurb:
Eight skaters, one evening, and a medal on the line. The men's Street final at Valley Complex 1 is where the 2028 Games' skateboarding story reaches its sharpest point, in the sport's Southern California home region.

The format follows Paris 2024: a skater's best run is combined with their two highest single-trick scores. That leaves room for late comebacks. Yuto Horigome won in Paris from fourth place on his last trick, a nollie 270 bluntslide.

The 8:30 PM start puts the action under evening skies in the Sepulveda Basin, a temporary open-air venue in the San Fernando Valley. Expect a loud crowd, a park-like setting, and the usual skate-contest tension as the final tricks go down.
SKB04.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Yuto Horigome (JPN), with Jagger Eaton and Nyjah Huston (both USA) taking silver and bronze. The 2028 field is not set, so these are projected contenders based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Yuto Horigome
potentialContenders.note: Won gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Whether he qualifies for 2028 is not confirmed, but he would be a threat in any final.

potentialContenders.name: Sasaki Toa

potentialContenders.name: Sora Shirai
potentialContenders.note: Won World Cup Street finals in Rome (June 2025) and Kitakyushu (November 2025). A strong form-based pick if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Jagger Eaton
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist. If he qualifies, he would have a home crowd in Los Angeles.

potentialContenders.name: Nyjah Huston
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. A 2028 spot is not confirmed, but he could be a crowd favorite if he qualifies.

SKB05.blurb:
The men's park preliminary opens the skateboarding program at a temporary bowl in the San Fernando Valley. It is a morning session where the full 22-skater field first drops in, and only the top skaters advance to the final.

The field is not set, since places come from the World Skateboarding Ranking of 11 June 2028. Paris 2024 champion Keegan Palmer, born in San Diego but skating for Australia, is a projected name to watch.

Valley Complex 2 sits inside the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, a big open-air city park. This is an accessible way to see the sport up close, and nearby complexes host other sports.
SKB05.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Keegan Palmer, with Tom Schaar and Augusto Akio on the podium. Qualification is still open, so the names below are projections based on recent form, not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Keegan Palmer

potentialContenders.name: Egoitz Bijueska

potentialContenders.name: Tom Schaar

potentialContenders.name: Gavin Bottger
potentialContenders.note: 2023 world champion and X Games park winner in 2025 and 2026. Finished 10th at Paris 2024. Projected to push for a US spot.

SKB06.blurb:
Under the Valley lights, the women's park preliminary brings together a field that has become very young and very hard to separate. Paris 2024 showed how little room there is at the top, and the final here is only a few good runs away.

A nation can enter no more than three skaters, which matters for Japan's deep pool of talent. Rosters depend on the World Skateboarding Ranking of 11 June 2028 and the 2028 Qualification Series.

Expect an evening session in an open-air temporary venue in the Sepulveda Basin. It is a relaxed, loud setting where crowds tend to cheer every landed trick, not only the winning ones.
SKB06.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Arisa Trew (AUS), with Kokona Hiraki (JPN) in silver and Sky Brown (GBR) in bronze. Who actually qualifies for 2028 is not yet known, so these are projected names based on form.

potentialContenders.name: Mizuho Hasegawa
potentialContenders.note: Aged 15, she won the 2026 Rome World Cup with a 96.33 run, called the highest women's park score on the tour. A projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sky Brown
potentialContenders.note: Won the world title in São Paulo in March 2026 and also in 2023. Bronze medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

potentialContenders.name: Cocona Hiraki
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, third at the 2026 Rome World Cup. Could appear if she makes Japan's cap of three.

potentialContenders.name: Arisa Trew

SKB07.blurb:
The men's park final is the medal session, set for a Wednesday evening at Valley Complex 2. A third straight gold for Keegan Palmer is the obvious storyline, though nothing here is certain.

In the Paris 2024 final only two of eight skaters landed their opening runs, and Palmer's 93.11 first run held up. That kind of pressure could shape the night again.

The field is not set yet, because places depend on the 11 June 2028 ranking. World Skate called the 2026 Rome final the highest standard of men's park skating it had seen, so the bar for 2028 looks high.

Evening in the Sepulveda Basin should bring a big crowd, and plenty of Southern California skaters could have the local fans behind them.
SKB07.potentialContendersIntro: Palmer won park gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, with Tom Schaar (silver) and Augusto Akio (bronze) on the Paris podium. The 2028 field is not confirmed, so the names below are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Keegan Palmer
potentialContenders.note: Two-time defending gold medalist (confirmed). A win would make three in a row. Recent X Games results are silver in 2025 and bronze in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Egoitz Bijueska
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion with a 95.83 run and 2025 Rome World Cup winner. A likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Schaar

potentialContenders.name: Gavin Bottger
potentialContenders.note: 2023 world champion from Oceanside, California, and X Games park gold winner in 2025 and 2026. Could appear if he qualifies.

SKB08.blurb:
The women's park final could be one of the closest medal contests of the Games. At Paris 2024 only 0.87 points separated gold from bronze, and a single clean run can change the podium.

The story is generational as well as tight. Arisa Trew won gold at 14, while Japan's Mizuho Hasegawa, 15, scored 96.33 at the 2026 Rome World Cup, the highest women's park score on the tour.

Sky Brown, a two-time world champion, and Cocona Hiraki, a two-time silver medalist still chasing gold, add experience. The final field is not set, since it depends on the 11 June 2028 ranking and the Qualification Series.

Thursday evening in the Sepulveda Basin should be a big night for a sport at home in Southern California.
SKB08.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Arisa Trew, with Kokona Hiraki in silver and Sky Brown in bronze. The 2028 final field is unconfirmed, so these are projected contenders based on current form.

potentialContenders.name: Mizuho Hasegawa
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Rome World Cup with a record-level 96.33 and was runner-up at the 2026 worlds. Projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sky Brown
potentialContenders.note: Won the world title in March 2026 and in 2023, with bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Second in Rome in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Arisa Trew
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist (confirmed) and winner of park and vert at X Games Osaka 2025. A likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Cocona Hiraki
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, still seeking gold. Third in Rome in 2026, and she could appear if she makes Japan's cap of three.

SQU01.blurb:
Squash's first night on a Summer Games program kicks off on a Universal Studios backlot. Four Round of 16 matches, men's and women's, open the sport's debut.

It's single elimination, so every loser goes home after one match. Each country can enter no more than two players per event, and the 16-player draws are set through five qualification routes.

The courts sit at Courthouse Square, the Back to the Future set, with temporary stands built around it. Expect a night session under studio-lot lighting, running roughly 7:30 to 11:15 pm.
SQU01.potentialContendersIntro: Rosters aren't set, but current form points to these names for the men's and women's draws. All are projected, not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal
potentialContenders.note: Men's world No. 1 in the October 2026 PSA rankings and reigning two-time world champion; projected top seed if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Paul Coll

potentialContenders.name: Nour El Sherbini
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world title in Chicago, her eighth; could appear if she is one of Egypt's two women.

potentialContenders.name: Olivia Weaver
potentialContenders.note: World championship semifinalist in 2024 and 2025; a potential home-crowd draw if she qualifies.

SQU02.blurb:
Night two of the Round of 16 brings more four-match, single-elimination drama. A single bad evening ends a player's tournament.

The field includes universality places, which Squash Mad said could produce some early mismatches. It also reflects the two-per-country cap, meaning Egypt's depth of talent won't all fit into the draws.

Settle into temporary stands on the open-air Universal lot, with film-set facades as scenery. The sessions run late, so expect an evening crowd and a lively, close-up atmosphere.
SQU02.potentialContendersIntro: The final draws will be confirmed by 22 May 2028. These projected names come from October 2026 PSA form and could appear in the men's or women's matches.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Crouin
potentialContenders.note: Ranked sixth in the October 2026 PSA men's rankings; a likely contender for the French spot.

potentialContenders.name: Joel Makin

potentialContenders.name: Leonel Cardenas

potentialContenders.name: Olivia Weaver
potentialContenders.note: Reached the world championship semifinals in 2024 and 2025; likely a leading American hope if she qualifies.

SQU03.blurb:
The third Round of 16 night is a good entry point for fans who want a mix of favorites and underdogs. Four matches, men's and women's, with no second chances.

Qualification blends world rankings with continental and other routes. This helps players from places like Malaysia and Colombia reach a draw that Egypt would otherwise dominate.

The backlot setting gives squash an unusual look. Expect a fast, intimate evening in a temporary arena, with the glass-and-court action very close to the seats.
SQU03.potentialContendersIntro: Qualified players will be published around 22 May 2028. These are projected names based on October 2026 PSA rankings and are not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Marwan ElShorbagy
potentialContenders.note: Ranked ninth in the October 2026 men's list; could appear if he qualifies for England.

potentialContenders.name: Mohamed ElShorbagy

potentialContenders.name: Eain Yow Ng

potentialContenders.name: Nele Gilis

SQU04.blurb:
The last night of the Round of 16 finishes the quarterfinal lineups. By the end, eight men and eight women will remain.

For several players, this may be the biggest match of their careers. The qualification system was designed to include top players while spreading places across many national committees.

The Universal backlot makes for a memorable close to the opening round. Expect a late-night crowd and plenty of tension around the temporary courts.
SQU04.potentialContendersIntro: Nothing about 2028 participation is confirmed. These names are projections from recent world championship results and rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Diego Elias

potentialContenders.name: Ali Farag

SQU05.blurb:
The first quarterfinal session turns the draw into a medal race. Win and you're one match from guaranteeing at least a bronze-medal match. Lose, and you leave without a medal.

Four matches across the men's and women's draws mean the best of recent world championships may cross paths. Egypt's two-per-country limit means some top-ranked Egyptians won't be here at all.

The night has a bigger feel than the Round of 16. The Courthouse Square setting gives high-stakes squash a distinctive film-backlot backdrop.
SQU05.potentialContendersIntro: These are likely quarterfinal names from recent form, not confirmed qualifiers. Asal's results are recent facts, and his 2028 presence is a projection.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal

SQU06.blurb:
The second quarterfinal night sets the semifinal lineups. The results will also decide which names get to chase a medal in squash's debut.

Every medal in the tournament will be a first for the sport at a Summer Games. Nerves and pressure will likely matter as much as pure squash skill.

The temporary stands and movie-set surroundings give the evening a strange but fitting glamour. It's a late-night session with plenty at stake.

SQU07.blurb:
Two women's semifinals decide who plays for the first women's squash gold at a Summer Games. The winners head to the gold medal match and the losers to bronze.

Egyptians have shared the last three world titles: Nouran Gohar in 2024, Nour El Sherbini in 2025 and Amina Orfi in 2026. Yet at most two Egyptians can be in the draw.

This is a shorter, sharper session in the Universal backlot venue. Expect a charged crowd, and a loud one if an American reaches this stage.

SQU08.blurb:
The men's semifinals put four players one match from the gold medal match. Lose, and you still have bronze to play for on the final night.

Mostafa Asal has won the last two world titles, but Diego Elias beat him in the 2024 final. Paul Coll is also a major threat if all three qualify.

The session is a late-night showcase on an open-air studio lot. Expect a sizable crowd and long rallies right under the backlot facades.

SQU09.blurb:
Squash awards its first women's medals at a Summer Games tonight. The bronze medal match opens the session, followed by the gold medal match.

Egypt has taken the last three women's world titles, but the two-per-country cap means it can't sweep unless both qualifiers reach the medal matches. A host-nation contender such as Olivia Weaver would add home energy.

The medals will be decided on the court at Courthouse Square on the Universal backlot. This is the sport's debut medal moment, so expect a celebratory atmosphere.

SQU10.blurb:
The men's bronze and gold medal matches close out the squash tournament, and the first men's squash medals in Games history are awarded. It's also the last squash session of the Games.

Asal is the reigning two-time world champion, while Elias and Coll have the pedigree to challenge him. With at most two Egyptians in the draw, the podium will include at least one player from another country.

The finale plays out at the Universal Studios backlot courts. Expect a loud, celebratory night with a film-set backdrop.

SRF01.blurb:
Surfing opens at Lower Trestles with Round 1 for both men and women. It is the first look at a 48-surfer field, 24 per gender, working one of California's best-known high-performance waves.

The full field likely won't be settled until shortly before the Games, since most places are decided in 2028. Universality places mean smaller surfing nations could appear alongside the heavyweights.

There are no permanent grandstands at this state beach. Temporary facilities will go up, and fans will watch from the sand and cobblestone shore near the lineup, with attendance capped well below a regular pro event.

SRF02.blurb:
Round 2 raises the pressure at Trestles. Surfers who got through the opener now need to keep scoring on a wave that rewards sharp turns and clean lines.

Qualification is a big storyline. The ISA trimmed World Surfing Games places to seven per gender and partly restored places for the Championship Tour, and each pathway is capped at one surfer per nation. Three-surfer teams will have had to collect results from several routes.

Expect the same open-air, surf-break feel as day one: sand underfoot, the ocean in front of you, and heat results traded between spectators. Early starts reward fans who arrive with the morning light.

SRF03.blurb:
Round 3 is where the bracket tightens. The field narrows toward the quarterfinals, and a single poor heat can end a surfer's run.

This is also where deep surfing nations could show their strength. With up to three surfers per gender allowed, Brazil, Australia and the USA could each still have several names left in the draw, if they fill all their places.

Many of the likely contenders have surfed high-stakes heats at Lower Trestles, which hosted the one-day WSL Finals from 2021 to 2024. Watching from the shore, you feel how close the action is.

SRF04.blurb:
This is the medal day. Men's and women's quarterfinals, semifinals and the bronze and gold medal matches are all scheduled for a single day at Lower Trestles, so the stakes build through the session.

The defending champions are Kauli Vaast (FRA) and Caroline Marks (USA), if they qualify and compete. Paris 2024 produced a 0.17-point women's final and a men's final at Teahupo'o, so a close match is a real possibility.

There are no permanent stands here. Expect a limited, temporary spectator area on the beach, and off-site viewing parties in San Clemente for those who can't get in. The day's timing may shift with wave conditions.

SWA01.blurb:
The artistic swimming program opens with the women's duet technical routine, the first half of the duet medal puzzle. Pairs must hit prescribed elements, so precision matters as much as flair.

The 2025 world technical final was tight, with the top three separated by under seven points. Austria's Alexandri twins won that title, and 78 swimmers from 39 nations entered, so expect a deep, competitive field.

The pool sits in a temporary open-air stadium on the Long Beach Convention Center lot, near the downtown waterfront. Sunny coastal air and a morning start make this a relaxed way to see the sport.
SWA01.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to China's Wang twins, but they have not been confirmed for 2028. These are projected contenders based on recent form, and none are confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Anna-Maria and Eirini-Marina Alexandri

potentialContenders.note: Took silver in the 2025 world duet technical final with 301.4057. China's 2025 entry, so a plausible 2028 pair.

potentialContenders.name: Kate Shortman and Isabelle Thorpe
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, reported in March 2026 to be reuniting as a duet. Shortman is reportedly targeting 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Jaime Czarkowski and Ghizal Akbar

SWA02.blurb:
Medals are awarded in the women's duet free routine, when the free score is added to the previous day's technical score. Free routines reward creativity, choreography and storytelling, and the standings can shift quickly.

The field looks open. Spain's Iris Tio Casas and Lilou Lluis Valette won the 2025 world free title, while Austria's Alexandri twins won technical, so the two 2025 world duet titles went to different pairs.

The Paris 2024 podium could also reshape the picture. Great Britain's Shortman and Thorpe are reuniting, while China has not confirmed whether the Wang twins will defend their title.

This is the duet medal session at the open-air Long Beach pool. Expect a loud, flag-waving crowd for a long late-morning block.

SWA03.blurb:
The team event opens with the technical routine, the first of three scored routines that decide the medals. Teams of eight, which can include up to two men, perform required elements in near-perfect unison.

China won the 2025 world technical title with 307.8001 points, ahead of a Russian team competing as neutral athletes and Spain. Russia's eligibility for 2028 has not been confirmed.

The session is an accessible, compact 90-minute window into the sport's synchronized, high-energy team format. It takes place in Long Beach's temporary outdoor pool, near the downtown waterfront.

SWA04.blurb:
The team free routine is the second of three team routines, and the stage for creativity and big choreography. Themes, music and costumes are all part of the show.

China has won the world team free title at every worlds from 2022 through 2025, including 348.4779 points in Singapore, ahead of Japan and Spain. At Paris 2024, China led after the technical and free routines.

The sport first appeared at the 1984 Games in Los Angeles, so this session marks its return to Southern California. The open-air Long Beach setting adds a sunny, festive atmosphere.

SWA05.blurb:
The team acrobatic routine is the last artistic swimming session of the Games, and team medals are decided here. Technical, free and acrobatic scores combine to determine the final standings.

Acrobatic routines feature lifts, throws and risky high-difficulty moves, and can reshuffle the table. China sealed its first team gold in Paris this way, with the United States second and Spain third.

Whether China can defend the title is the central storyline. It swept all three team routines at the 2025 worlds, while the U.S. raised its difficulty in an all-or-nothing push and missed the podium.

A Saturday late-morning finale at Long Beach's temporary outdoor pool should bring a loud, flag-filled crowd.

SWM01.blurb:
The pool opens at 2028 Stadium with a morning heat session, and the first heats of the new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke. Those two events were approved in April 2025 and use heats, semifinals and a final.

Also on deck are heats of the women's 100m fly, men's 400m free, men's 100m breast and women's 400m free. The men's and women's 4x100m free relay heats go straight to that evening's finals, so they set the lanes.

A 50-meter pool on an NFL stadium floor under a translucent canopy is a striking setting. Morning heats are an easy, lower-key way to see the deck and the giant ring-shaped video board.

SWM02.blurb:
The first finals night of swimming arrives with four medal races: the men's and women's 400m freestyle and both 4x100m freestyle relays. Semifinals fill out the rest, including the new men's 50m fly and women's 50m back.

The women's 400m free will crown a new champion, since Ariarne Titmus retired in October 2025. Summer McIntosh, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, beat Katie Ledecky at the 2025 Worlds, so this could be a close fight.

The relays carry real rivalry. The US men won in Paris and the Australian women won the women's race, and Australia beat the US by 0.66 seconds in the 2025 women's 4x200m relay.

Expect a loud crowd under the canopy on opening night, with the whole pool visible from the stands.

Day two's morning session has four events. The women's 100m breaststroke, men's 100m backstroke and women's 100m freestyle send swimmers to semifinals, but the men's 400m IM goes straight to the final.

Only the top eight from the 400m IM heats advance, so the one-off morning swim carries pressure. Léon Marchand won Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 world title in 4:04.73, with Tomoyuki Matsushita second both times.

The women's 100m free brings a deep sprint field, and Sarah Sjöström, Torri Huske and Siobhán Haughey took the Paris 2024 podium.

Morning sessions are quieter and easier to move around, and you can often get close to the deck.

Day two's finals include five medal races, and two are brand new: the men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke, the first Games medals in those events. Also up are the women's 100m fly, men's 400m IM and men's 100m breaststroke.

The women's 100m fly could be a USA showdown. Torri Huske and Gretchen Walsh went one-two in Paris 2024, and Walsh won the 2025 world title in 54.73.

Men's 100m breaststroke has history too. Nicolò Martinenghi won Paris gold, and Adam Peaty tied for silver, so no bronze was awarded. Léon Marchand is the one to beat in the 400m IM.

Semifinals in the women's 100m breast, men's 100m back and women's 100m free keep the evening full.

Summer McIntosh won the 400m IM at Paris 2024 and again at the 2025 Worlds, where she took four golds. David Popovici, the Paris 2024 and 2025 world 200m free champion, is the man to chase.

The men's 1500m heats test endurance, with Ahmed Jaouadi's 800m world title in 2025 hinting at a distance shake-up.

Session seating is easy in the morning, and it makes a good chance to see future finalists up close.

Summer McIntosh could add another IM gold after her Paris 2024 win and 2025 world title. In the 100m free, Sarah Sjöström won Paris 2024 ahead of Torri Huske and Siobhán Haughey.

The men's 100m back and women's 100m breast open the field after Thomas Ceccon and Tatjana Schoenmaker-Smith won in Paris.

Four finals in two hours makes for a fast evening. Watch the video board and big screens for instant replays of every finish.

Day four's heats are headlined by the women's 1500m free, which goes straight to the final. Also swimming are the women's 200m free, men's 50m free and women's 200m breaststroke, with semifinals ahead.

Katie Ledecky is the reference point in the 1500m. She won Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds in 15:26.44, though her 2028 entry is not confirmed.

The women's 200m free will miss Ariarne Titmus, who retired in October 2025. Cameron McEvoy won the men's 50m free in Paris and in 21.14 in 2025.

Sprint heats are over in seconds, so keep your eyes on the lane order as the field is set.

SWM08.blurb:
Day four's finals start fast: men's 200m free, new men's 50m breaststroke, men's 1500m free, men's 200m fly and women's 100m back. The 50m breast final is the first time this event awards a Games medal.

David Popovici won the 200m free at Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds, with Luke Hobson second in 2025. Léon Marchand won Paris 2024 gold in the 200m fly, and Kaylee McKeown won the women's 100m back.

The men's 1500m is worth watching for how the distance field has changed, with Ahmed Jaouadi winning the 2025 800m free.

A long, varied night, with the women's 200m breast, women's 200m free and men's 50m free semis as a bonus.

Day five's morning has men's 200m IM, men's 200m back and the new women's 50m butterfly heats. The men's 4x200m free relay goes straight to that evening's final.

Léon Marchand won the 200m IM at Paris 2024, and Hubert Kós won 200m back gold. Great Britain won Paris 2024 relay gold ahead of the US and Australia.

The relay heats will show who gets the eight lanes. Popovici, Hobson and Japan's Tatsuya Murasa suggest several nations could be contenders.

Arrive early for the new women's 50m fly heats and a first look at the sport's newest events.

Day five's finals include women's 200m free, men's 50m free, women's 200m breaststroke, women's 1500m free and the men's 4x200m free relay. The semifinals feature men's 200m IM and 200m back plus the new women's 50m fly.

Katie Ledecky won the 1500m at Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds in 15:26.44. Her 2028 plans are not confirmed, but if she swims, this is her kind of race.

Mollie O'Callaghan won Paris 2024 in the 200m free after Ariarne Titmus took silver and then retired. Cameron McEvoy won the 50m free at both Paris and the 2025 Worlds.

The men's relay could come down to a final-leg sprint, a perfect fit for a packed stadium.

Day six's heats include the women's 200m IM, men's 200m breaststroke, men's 100m free and women's 200m back. The women's 4x200m free relay goes straight to that evening's final.

Pan Zhanle won Paris 2024 gold in the 100m free in a world record, and Kaylee McKeown won the 200m back and won it again at the 2025 Worlds.

Australia won the women's 4x200m relay at Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds, with the US second both times by a narrow margin. The world record belongs to Australia at 7:37.50.

Heats can be a good way to spot who might surprise on the later nights.

Day six's finals include the men's 200m back, women's 50m fly, men's 200m IM and women's 4x200m free relay. The women's 50m fly is a new event, so it awards its first Games medal.

Gretchen Walsh won the 2025 world 50m fly title in 24.83, and she won the 100m too. Léon Marchand set a 200m IM world record of 1:52.69 in 2025.

Hubert Kós won 200m back at Paris 2024 and 2025 Worlds. Australia won the relay in both and beat the US by under a second in 2025.

The event sequence is quick, with four medal races and several semifinals.

Day seven's heats feature men's 100m fly, new men's 50m backstroke, new women's 50m breaststroke, men's 800m free and the mixed 4x100m medley relay. The 800m and the mixed relay go straight to finals.

Kristóf Milák won the men's 100m fly at Paris 2024, and Maxime Grousset won the 2025 Worlds in 49.62. Caeleb Dressel, the world record holder, did not swim that event in 2025.

The mixed medley relay was won by the US in Paris 2024, ahead of China and Australia.

Morning heats give a relaxed look at new events while the men's 800m field sorts itself out.

Day seven's finals include women's 200m back, men's 200m breaststroke, women's 200m IM and men's 100m free. Semifinals include men's 100m fly, new women's 50m breast and new men's 50m back.

Kaylee McKeown has won the 200m back at Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds, with Regan Smith second both times. Summer McIntosh won the 200m IM in Paris, while Kate Douglass was second.

Pan Zhanle's world-record win in the 100m free at Paris 2024 sets a high bar. Léon Marchand won the 200m breast there too.

This is a strong night for a first-time visitor to the pool, with four finals and new events.

Day eight's heats bring the women's 50m free, 200m fly, 800m free and both 4x100m medley relays. The 800m and the relays go straight to finals, so these heats set the lanes.

Sarah Sjöström won Paris 2024 in the 50m free, and Summer McIntosh won the 200m fly. Katie Ledecky won Paris 2024 in the 800m, though her 2028 plans are not confirmed.

The US women won the Paris 2024 medley relay, with Australia second. Gretchen Walsh and Kaylee McKeown are projected as key legs.

A good session to see how the relay teams shape up before the final.

SWM16.blurb:
A stacked Saturday evening at the pool: five finals, two semifinals, and the first Games medals ever awarded in the men's 50m backstroke and women's 50m breaststroke. Both events were approved in April 2025, so history is on the program.

The men's 100m butterfly and 800m freestyle finals headline the distance and power ends of the card. The mixed 4x100m medley relay closes things out, with the United States the Paris 2024 champion ahead of China and Australia.

The women's 50m freestyle and 200m butterfly semifinals set up the next day's finals. Sarah Sjöström and Summer McIntosh are Paris 2024 champions in those events, though their 2028 participation is not confirmed.

You'll sit in 2028 Stadium, looking down on a temporary 50-meter pool built on the field, with the ring-shaped video board overhead. Expect the open-sided canopy to let in a coastal breeze, and a big crowd roaring through the sprints.

Sunday afternoon packs five finals into 90 minutes, and nearly every one is a women's marquee event. With swimming moved to the second week of the Games, this lands on the program's final weekend.

The women's 50m freestyle is a flat-out sprint, with Sarah Sjöström the Paris 2024 champion. The 200m butterfly follows, with Summer McIntosh the Paris 2024 gold medalist, Regan Smith silver and Zhang Yufei bronze.

The women's 800m freestyle brings a long, tactical race, with Katie Ledecky the Paris 2024 champion ahead of Ariarne Titmus. The men's and women's medley relays close the session, with China and the United States the Paris 2024 winners.

At 2028 Stadium, you'll look down on a temporary 50-meter pool on the field, with the big ring-shaped video board tracking splits above. Expect a loud, flag-heavy crowd for the relays.

TEN01.blurb:
Tennis at the 2028 Games opens here, with mixed doubles first-round matches under the Carson sun. The event now launches the program instead of closing it.

Three matches share Center Court from 11:00 AM, part of eight first-round matches spread across three courts. The 16-pair field is cut to eight, and the winners are back for quarterfinals that evening.

Center Court seats about 8,000 in an open-air bowl on the Cal State Dominguez Hills campus. It opens just three days after the Wimbledon final on July 16, and organizers say the schedule could still change.

Opening day of tennis is a sprint, and Court 1 is one of three courts running mixed doubles at once. Teams here will probably be back on court for a quarterfinal that same night.

Three first-round matches run from 11:00 AM. The 2028 format squeezes mixed doubles into two days, so every point carries extra weight and fatigue builds quickly.

Court 1 is a smaller show court than Center Court, so fans sit close to the players in the open air. It is a good spot to catch quick, high-energy doubles without the stadium crowd.

Court 2 hosts just two of the eight first-round mixed doubles matches. It is a lower-profile start to a tournament that will have its first medals less than 36 hours later.

The 16-pair draw is cut to eight teams here and on the neighboring courts. Winners go straight into evening quarterfinals, so a quick win could matter later.

Court 2 is an open-air court with far fewer seats than Center Court, which puts fans very close to the baseline. It is a relaxed way to see Games-level tennis on a hard surface, a change from the clay of Paris 2024.

Evening quarterfinals on Center Court give opening day a late-night feel. Any team on court has already played once today, and the winners will play again tomorrow morning.

Two of the four quarterfinals are scheduled here from 6:30 PM, with the other two on Court 1. Anyone who went deep at Wimbledon would be playing just three days after that final.

The stadium seats about 8,000 under open sky, with the stands cooling as the sun drops. It is a good chance to see the first serious medal-race tennis of the tournament.

Winners advance to the semifinals on Center Court on July 20, with medals decided that night. Matches are best of three sets on outdoor hard courts.

Court 1 is smaller and closer to the action than the main stadium, so you can hear every shout and see every volley. The format follows the U.S. Open in putting mixed doubles at the start of the tournament.

Two semifinals on Center Court narrow mixed doubles to four teams. The winners play for gold that evening, while the losers are sent straight to the bronze-medal match.

That makes this a medal-race session, with every team still having something to play for. The pairs will have played two matches yesterday and may still be on court for a third today.

It is also the first day of singles, so any team with a player in both events may face a heavy day. The open-air stadium seats about 8,000, and a daytime crowd should be full of early-tournament energy.

All matches are best of three sets on hard courts, four days after Wimbledon ends. Some top names may skip the Games to rest, and others may be limited by injury.

Court 1 is a compact outdoor court with fans sitting close to the baseline. If a seed or fan favorite lands here, you will see the first round from a few rows back.
