Play here overlaps with the mixed doubles medal action on Center Court. Tennis moves from the clay of Paris 2024 to hard courts, which tends to favor big servers and flat hitters.

Seats are limited, and fans are close enough to the court to hear the players talk. Wander between courts and you may catch a rising player who could become a headline name.

Courts 3-10 are the outer courts, where fans can roam between matches and take in the whole first round. This is where the 64-player draws turn into a wide sweep of nations.

There are 64 first-round singles matches in total across the complex, and many unfold here. Players who just came from grass at Wimbledon must adjust quickly to hard courts.

Seating is close to the court, and the open-air setting makes it feel like a tennis festival. It is a casual, affordable way to spot a future star, or a veteran chasing one last big week.

The first tennis medals of the 2028 Games are decided here, in mixed doubles. The bronze match opens the evening, followed by the gold-medal match in the late hours.

Medalists will have played four matches in about 36 hours, starting just three days after Wimbledon ends. Stamina and quick-fire doubles tactics may matter as much as raw power.

Center Court seats about 8,000, and a Friday-night style crowd should make this a lively start to the tennis program. The session runs until midnight, so be ready for a late finish.

Center Court hosts a daytime singles session on the second day of first-round play. By now the mixed doubles medals are settled, and the focus shifts fully to the 64-player singles draws.

The field is set by the June 12, 2028 rankings, with 56 direct places, one host-country place, six ITF continental places and one universality place per gender. Alcaraz and Sinner remain the headline stars if healthy.

Fans sit under open sky in the 8,000-seat bowl. A top seed's first match here would be the first big-stadium singles test after Wimbledon's grass.

TRI01.blurb:
The first medals of the 2028 Games get decided on a beach at sunrise. The women's individual triathlon opens the medal schedule, the first time triathlon has done so since Sydney 2000.

The race starts from the sand into Pacific surf, with a 1,000m lap, a 25m beach run and a 500m second lap. Then come eight 5km bike laps with two technical turnarounds, and a four-lap 10km run through the Venice canals area.

Expect an early-morning crowd along the bike path and boardwalk, with limited grandstands at the finish where Venice Boulevard meets the sand. The single transition beside the finish keeps the action close.

One day after the women, the men take on the same Venice Beach course. It is a single final with no heats, so every start-line athlete is racing for a medal.

The 1.5km swim starts in the surf over two laps. Then comes the eight-lap, 40km bike with two technical turnarounds, and a four-lap 10km run through the Venice canals area. Paris 2024 showed how a race can flip in the last minute, when Alex Yee passed Hayden Wilde to win.

The finish sits right on the sand, and fans can spread along the course near the boardwalk and Muscle Beach. The 7:30 AM start keeps the whole race in cool coastal morning light.

The order for 2028 is woman, man, woman, man. That reverses Paris 2024, where Germany edged the United States and Great Britain in a three-way sprint for its first gold in the event.

Each athlete swims 350m from the shoreline, bikes 6.6km over two laps and runs 1.6km over two laps. All four legs finish at the same Venice Beach line, so the crowd gets repeated handoffs and a close finish.

Hall 3 is an exhibit hall converted for competition, so seats sit close to the tables and the rallies feel intimate. It is an easy way to see the sport's top names early.

Chen Meng won gold in Paris over Sun Yingsha, but she said it would be her last Games. That points to a new champion in 2028, and a chance to end China's run of golds since 1988.

Hall 3 should be at its loudest for the final, with fans close to the table.

China has won each Mixed Team World Cup so far, including 8-1 over Japan in 2025. Hall 3 should offer fast, team-driven matches on Monday morning.

Each tie is a race to 8 games across five three-game sets: mixed doubles, women's singles, men's singles, men's doubles, women's doubles. Group results shape seeding and bracket paths into Thursday's quarterfinals, so late matches can still swing.

The hall is an exhibit space turned arena in downtown LA, with seats close to the tables. Expect a tight, loud room and a long evening of table-hopping between ties.

The stadium is open-air, with the Pacific behind the court. A 9 AM start means cool coastal air and a relaxed crowd, a short walk from downtown Long Beach.

The participants aren't known yet. The United States took bronze at Paris 2024 and play as hosts, while Poland, silver medalists in Paris, are another team that could land here.

This is an evening session at Honda Center, starting at 8:30 PM. Expect a night-game atmosphere, with the Anaheim arena lit up for a medal presentation to follow.

VVO50.blurb:
The men's gold medal match is the final act of the men's tournament, and the stakes are huge. France are chasing a third straight title after back-to-back golds.

That would extend a run that only the United States in 1984 and 1988 matched in the men's game before France. The finalists will be set by the semifinals on Jul 26.

France beat Poland 3-0 in the Paris 2024 final. The United States, bronze medalists, would love to turn that into gold at home.

A 10:00 AM start at Honda Center means morning volleyball in a packed arena of roughly 18,000. It's a good ticket for anyone who wants the tournament's biggest moment.

Bronze means a medal, and the Saturday afternoon match is a chance for two teams to finish with something after a semifinal loss.

The teams aren't set. Brazil, Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2025 World Championship bronze winners, and Japan, who finished fourth in 2025, are among teams that could appear.

The host United States, Paris 2024 silver medalists, qualify automatically but finished fifth at the 2025 World Championship. If they reach this match, the crowd at Honda Center will be vocal.

The match runs 2:45 PM to 5:15 PM, a relaxed afternoon slot before the next day's gold medal match.

The last match of the women's tournament decides gold. Italy won their first-ever gold at Paris 2024 with a 3-0 sweep of the United States, and they head into 2028 as reigning champions.

Italy also won the 2025 World Championship, beating Turkey 3-2, and the 2025 Nations League, beating Brazil 3-1. Whether that run carries into 2028 is an open question, since the finalists won't be set until Jul 27.

The United States could be a major storyline if the host nation, Paris 2024 silver medalists, make a run. Turkey and Brazil are other contenders.

A 10:00 AM start on Sunday at Honda Center promises a morning of drama in a bowl of roughly 18,000 fans.

The opening night of weightlifting belongs to a brand-new weight class. Men's 65kg did not exist at Paris 2024, so this final starts with no defending champion and a field that is still being sorted out.

Every lifter gets three snatches and three clean and jerks, and the best combined total takes gold. Qualification runs through May 2028, and no entry list has been published yet.

The Peacock Theater puts everyone in front of one raised platform, facing a huge stage, with air conditioning and L.A. Live outside. Expect a loud, close-up start to the weightlifting program.

Women's 53kg is a new category, and the first women's final of the 2028 weightlifting program. There is no reigning champion at this exact weight, so the title is open from the start.

Each final is a full session of snatches and clean and jerks, with the best total taking gold. The 69kg class sits near the Paris 2024 middleweight division won by American Olivia Reeves, though her 2028 weight has not been confirmed.

Every lifter takes three snatches and three clean and jerks, and the highest total wins. The closest Paris 2024 division was the 73kg class won by Indonesia's Rizki Juniansyah, though his 2028 weight is unconfirmed.

There are 12 teams this time, in three groups of four. The top two in each group plus the two best third-placed teams reach the quarterfinals, so every opening goal matters.

The pool is a temporary open-air stadium on the Long Beach Convention Center lot, near the downtown waterfront. Expect coastal sun and a crowd settling into the first splash of the men's event.

WPO13.blurb:
Monday morning continues the men's group stage, with the tournament running from July 12 to July 22. The format of three groups of four is a shift from the two groups of six used before.

Paris 2024 gives context. Serbia was beaten by Australia, Spain and Hungary in that group stage and still won its third straight title, 13-11 over Croatia.

The United States, bronze medalists in Paris for their first medal since 2008, qualify automatically and could be part of this session. A temporary outdoor pool in Long Beach sets the scene.

WPO14.blurb:
The Monday afternoon men's session has two group-stage matches with plenty of room for upsets. In a four-team group, one bad day can be costly.

There is a safety valve: the two best third-placed teams join the six group winners and runners-up in the quarterfinals. A team finishing third can still advance.

The Long Beach Aquatics Center is a temporary open-air venue, built for the Games on a convention-center lot near the waterfront.

Monday night closes out a day of men's group play with two evening matches. The tournament's three groups of four are now deep into the rotation.

The United States men qualify automatically as host, after taking Paris 2024 bronze in their first medal since 2008. Hungary, who lost that bronze match, will be a motivated rival if it qualifies.

Water polo has been at the Summer Games since 1900, the oldest team sport on the program. Long Beach's temporary pool gives that history a fresh outdoor home.

WPO16.blurb:
The women's group stage opens its doubleheader at Long Beach's temporary open-air pool. A 12-team field, the largest women's tournament in Games history, means more teams and more tight group races.

Three groups of four feed the quarterfinals. The top two in each advance, along with the two best third-placed teams, so even a mid-group match can swing the bracket.

Expect morning sun, a waterfront breeze and a relaxed, accessible crowd. It's a good way to see world-class water polo up close without a final's ticket price.

WPO17.blurb:
Afternoon brings two more women's group matches, with teams already feeling the pressure of the third-place wild-card math. Each result tightens the picture of who reaches the quarterfinals.

This is the first Games where the women's field matches the men's at 12 teams. For comparison, the World Aquatics Championships first had 12 women's teams back in 1994.

Seating is outdoors in Long Beach's coastal summer weather, a short walk from the downtown waterfront. The women's tournament also ends after the men's final, a first.

WPO18.blurb:
Tuesday's evening session closes the women's group-stage day under the lights in Long Beach. The 12-team format makes every match matter for seeding and for the race to the knockout rounds.

The host United States is the big storyline. The U.S. won medals at every women's Games tournament before missing the Paris 2024 podium, and it will want to rebound in front of a home crowd.

European Aquatics expects Hungary, Italy and Greece to be in the field. An evening crowd near the water is the closest thing water polo has to a night out.

WPO19.blurb:
Knockout water polo begins here: two men's quarterfinals, one loss and you're out. The eight teams come from three groups, the top two in each plus the two best third-placed sides.

Serbia comes in as three-time defending champion, though it lost three group games in Paris 2024 and still won gold. Anyone can wobble in the group stage and then win in the knockouts.

Expect a loud, flag-heavy crowd and fast, physical play from the first whistle. It's a strong value pick for a day of high-stakes games in the outdoor Long Beach pool.

The evening quarterfinals decide the last men's semifinalists. Some teams arrive as group winners, while others sneak in as one of the best third-placed sides.

Croatia lost the Paris 2024 final 13-11 to regional rival Serbia, and Hungary missed bronze to the United States. Both are projected to carry revenge motives if they reach this round.

Water polo has been on the Games program since 1900, the oldest team sport at the Summer Games. Seeing it in a temporary Long Beach arena at dusk feels like a nod to that long tradition.

The women's quarterfinals start with two single-elimination matches. Spain's unbeaten path to gold in Paris 2024 shows how quickly a bracket can turn into a statement run.

The field is wide open. Greece won the 2025 World Championships, the Netherlands won the 2026 Europeans and Hungary has lost three consecutive major finals, so no one is a lock.

The U.S. had medaled at every women's Games tournament before Paris 2024, so a home run in Long Beach is a storyline to watch if the Americans advance.

Spain is the reigning champion, and Bea Ortiz was named World Aquatics Athlete of the Year after Paris 2024. Whether those names are on the roster in 2028 is still to be seen.

Two men's semifinals mean the first real shot at a medal. Win and you play for gold, lose and you're in the bronze match.

Serve recent form as a guide: Spain won the 2025 Worlds, Serbia won the 2026 Europeans at home and Greece took 2025 world bronze. Dusan Mandic, if he plays in 2028, would be the headline name.

Sightlines in the temporary Long Beach stadium are close to the water, so you'll hear the splashing, the whistles and the bench shouting.

It's played on the same day as the gold medal match, so the Long Beach crowd is already warm. Expect intense, sometimes ragged play, with both teams knowing it's their last game.

Wrestling opens the 2028 Games with a morning of bracket-clearing bouts in Hall 2. The round of 16 and quarterfinals are on the mats for men's Greco-Roman 60kg and 130kg and women's freestyle 50kg.

Only a loss to a finalist keeps a wrestler alive for bronze through repechage, so early upsets can end a medal run fast. Expect three brackets running through the session.

The hall is a converted downtown exhibition space with temporary stands around the mats, a short walk from L.A. Live. It is a close-up, climate-controlled way to catch the first bouts of the tournament.

Evening sessions in Hall 2 should feel louder than the morning rounds, with temporary stands close to the mats. If Sarah Hildebrandt makes the U.S. team, a home crowd could be a big factor.

WRE09.blurb:
Round of 16 and quarterfinals in men's freestyle 74kg and 125kg and women's 68kg make this a morning with some of the sport's biggest weight classes. Repechage bouts follow for the previous day's brackets.

The home storyline is women's freestyle. Amit Elor won 68kg gold at Paris 2024, though she moved to 72kg in 2025, so her path to 2028 is not settled.

Hall 2 keeps the action tight. Heavyweights at 125kg bring a different pace than lighter classes, and fans can see both in the same session.
WRE09.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 champions and 2025 world medalists give a projected field for 74kg, 125kg and 68kg. Nothing here is confirmed for 2028.

WRE10.blurb:
Gold arrives in men's freestyle 57kg and 86kg and women's freestyle 62kg, with semifinals in 74kg, 125kg and women's 68kg on the same evening. It is a strong night for freestyle fans.

Japan won both 57kg and 62kg in Paris 2024 through Rei Higuchi and Sakura Motoki, so both classes could be worth following. Spencer Lee gives the 57kg final a home angle if he qualifies.

The session runs about 3.5 hours, with temporary stands close to the mats. Expect a big crowd for any U.S. wrestler in a final.
WRE10.potentialContendersIntro: The marquee medal matches are men's 57kg, 86kg and women's 62kg. These are projected contenders drawn from Paris 2024 results, not confirmed 2028 entries.

WRE11.blurb:
Men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's 76kg get their round of 16 and quarterfinals. Repechages run for classes with medal matches later the same day.

The 97kg class has some of the biggest names in the sport. Kyle Snyder won the 2025 world title, and Akhmed Tazhudinov won Paris 2024 gold.

A Saturday morning in Hall 2 is a good way to see depth in freestyle. Early rounds can include well-known names facing unknown qualifiers, with a close-up view from the stands.
WRE11.potentialContendersIntro: These projected names come from Paris 2024 and the 2025 World Championships. Who qualifies for 2028 is still open.

WRE12.blurb:
Three gold-medal finals share this Saturday night: men's freestyle 74kg and 125kg and women's 68kg. Semifinals in 65kg, 97kg and women's 76kg open the session.

The 125kg bracket has a long rivalry. Iran's Amir Hossein Zare beat Geno Petriashvili in the 2021 and 2023 world finals, and Zare won another world title in 2025.

Gable Steveson has said he wants 2028 gold, but in 2026 he said UFC is his priority. Amit Elor is also in the mix after returning from pregnancy.

This could be one of the biggest nights in Hall 2, with temporary stands right beside the mats.
WRE12.potentialContendersIntro: The headline finals are men's freestyle 125kg, women's 68kg and men's 74kg. These are projected names, and several have unsettled 2028 plans.

potentialContenders.name: Gable Steveson
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 125kg champion; his 2028 plans are unclear given his UFC focus, so he is a long shot to appear.

WRE13.blurb:
Wrestling closes in Hall 2 with repechages, bronze matches and gold-medal finals for men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's 76kg. It is the last day of the tournament.

The 97kg final is the marquee event if Kyle Snyder qualifies, with Akhmed Tazhudinov and Iran's Amir Ali Azarpira also in the picture. Snyder beat Azarpira 4-2 for the 2025 world title.

Sunday midday gives families a good window. The last medals are decided close to the mats, with crowds likely to support U.S. wrestlers if any reach the finals.
